signals.title: [Feature]: per-component response cost headers (input, output, cache read, cache write, reasoning, tool usage)
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature `x-litellm-response-cost` tells the caller what a request cost in total, and the sibling headers `x-litellm-response-cost-original`, `-discount-amount`, `-margin-amount`, and `-margin-percent` already expose pricing adjustments. What is missing is the split of that total across input tokens, output tokens, cache reads, cache writes, reasoning tokens, and built-in tool usage. LiteLLM already computes exactly this split for every request and records it in spend logs, so this is surfacing work rather than new accounting Proposal: for non-streaming responses, emit one header per component next to the existing total, following the naming of the current family: `x-litellm-response-cost-input`, `x-litellm-response-cost-output`, `x-litellm-response-cost-cache-read`, `x-litellm-response-cost-cache-creation`, `x-litellm-response-cost-reasoning`, and `x-litellm-response-cost-tool-usage`. Reasoning cost is a subset of output cost and should be documented as such so consumers do not double count Headers over a `cost_breakdown` field on the response body, for three reasons. The values are already available at the moment response headers are assembled, which is where the discount and margin headers come from today. Headers are purely additive, so strict OpenAI-shape response parsers keep working without any opt-in flag. And the ask is scoped to non-streaming, where headers can carry final cost. An in-band breakdown for streaming can be a follow-up on top of the existing `include_cost_in_streaming_usage` mechanism The earlier ask for an input/output split in headers (#11260) was closed stale without a fix. This supersedes it with the full component set. Requested by a customer running LiteLLM as their central gateway ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a platform team fronting all LLM traffic through the LiteLLM proxy wants to show each internal app where its spend goes, but callers only ever see one total, so they rebuild the split by hand from their own pricing tables (the same dead end as #11260) 1. An app sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a prompt-cached context on a reasoning model such as gpt-5.4-nano 2. The 200 response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 7.4e-06` and the body's `usage` block carries token counts (`prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) 3. To split the total they multiply those token counts by per-model rates copied into their own pricing table, which drifts: cache-write premiums, reasoning rates, and built-in tool charges (web search, code execution) differ per provider, and tool charges never appear in `usage` at all 4. When their hand-computed components fail to sum to the header total, they cannot tell which component is wrong After this feature (ideal user flow): the same response states the split directly and it sums to the total 1. The app sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same prompt-cached context 2. The 200 response now also carries `x-litellm-response-cost-input`, `-output`, `-cache-read`, `-cache-creation`, `-reasoning`, and `-tool-usage` 3. The components sum to `x-litellm-response-cost` (reasoning being a subset of output), so the team attributes spend per component with no local pricing table ### How far you got Config the proxy ran with, plus `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, and `DATABASE_URL` in the environment (values redacted): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.4-nano litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.4-nano api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY ``` Version or commit: 9d069f21dc Commands and their full output, hitting the real OpenAI API: ``` $ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config c19_config.yaml --port 47311 $ curl -sD headers.txt -o body.json http://localhost:47311/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-5.4-nano", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with one word: hello"}]}' $ grep -i "^x-litellm-response-cost" headers.txt x-litellm-response-cost: 7.4e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 7.4e-06 x-litellm-response-cost-discount-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-amount: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-margin-percent: 0.0 $ cat body.json {"id": "chatcmpl-ECcleXkHEngsdpkRwkqLYrRXh9EvZ", "created": 1786677666, "model": "gpt-5.4-nano", "object": "chat.completion", "choices": [{"finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": {"content": "hello", "role": "assistant", "provider_specific_fields": {"refusal": null}, "annotations": []}, "provider_specific_fields": {}}], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 4, "prompt_tokens": 12, "total_tokens": 16, "completion_tokens_details": {"accepted_prediction_tokens": 0, "audio_tokens": 0, "reasoning_tokens": 0, "rejected_prediction_tokens": 0}, "prompt_tokens_details": {"audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": 0}}, "service_tier": "default"} ``` What stopped me there: step 2 of the After flow dead-ends. The response exposes the total and its pricing adjustments only. No header and no body field carries the input, output, cache, reasoning, or tool components, so the split cannot be read from the response at all ### What a fix PR should look like `_get_cost_breakdown_from_logging_obj` in `litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py` already reads the fully populated `CostBreakdown` (defined in `litellm/types/utils.py` with fields `input_cost`, `output_cost`, `cache_read_cost`, `cache_creation_cost`, `reasoning_cost`, and `tool_usage_cost`) and returns only the discount and margin fields. Widen it to hand back the component fields too, emit the six new headers next to `x-litellm-response-cost` in `get_custom_headers`, and omit them when no breakdown was computed. A regression test should assert the six headers appear on a costed non-streaming response and that input plus cache read plus cache creation plus output plus tool usage equals the total, with reasoning excluded as a subset of output. The response headers docs page (`docs/proxy/response_headers.md` in the docs repo) gains the six rows ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: /v1/responses guardrail-blocked replies report zero token usage despite real upstream consumption
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a post-call guardrail blocks a response on `/v1/responses`, the proxy returns a 200 with the violation message and a usage object that is hardcoded to all zeros, even though the upstream LLM call completed and consumed real tokens. The same guardrail block on `/v1/chat/completions` (and `/v1/messages`) reports the real token usage the blocked upstream call consumed This matters because a guardrail-blocked call still costs real money upstream, and the response body is the only place the caller can learn that: the blocked request is logged on the failure path with 0 tokens and $0 spend, so any client-side token accounting built on response bodies silently undercounts every blocked `/v1/responses` call. Callers who reconcile their own per-request token counts against provider bills see an unexplained gap that grows with guardrail activity Expected: the `/v1/responses` blocked reply carries the real `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, and `total_tokens` the upstream call consumed, exactly like the `/v1/chat/completions` blocked reply already does (zeros remain correct for pre-call blocks, where no upstream call ever happened) ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app tracks per-request token spend from response bodies gets zeros for every guardrail-blocked Responses API call, so their accounting drifts under what the provider bills 1. Their platform team runs a LiteLLM proxy with a post-call guardrail (content policy) enabled by default 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "..."}` and the reply trips the guardrail 3. They get a 200 whose output text is the violation message and whose usage reads `"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0`, so their app records zero consumption for a call the provider billed 4. A teammate sends the same prompt as POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions, gets the same violation message with `finish_reason: "content_filter"`, but their usage shows the real counts, so the two apps' dashboards disagree about identical traffic 5. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs the blocked request shows 0 tokens and $0 spend, so nothing in the gateway lets the developer recover the real number After a (hypothetical) fix: the same blocked call reports the tokens it really consumed, so body-based accounting matches across endpoints 1. Their platform team runs a LiteLLM proxy with a post-call guardrail (content policy) enabled by default 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "..."}` and the reply trips the guardrail 3. They get a 200 whose output text is the violation message and whose usage carries the real counts, e.g. `"input_tokens": 14, "output_tokens": 20, "total_tokens": 34` 4. The teammate's POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions shows the same real counts for the same prompt, so both dashboards agree 5. Pre-call blocks (prompt never reached the provider) still report zero usage on both endpoints ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (`c17_repro_config.yaml`), using a minimal post-call guardrail that blocks every response the way any content policy guardrail would: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY guardrails: - guardrail_name: zero-usage-repro litellm_params: guardrail: c17_zero_usage_guardrail.ZeroUsageReproGuardrail mode: post_call default_on: true general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 litellm_settings: drop_params: true ``` `c17_zero_usage_guardrail.py`, mirroring how in-tree post-call guardrails (e.g. Straiker) raise their block with the original response attached: ```python from litellm.exceptions import ModifyResponseException from litellm.integrations.custom_guardrail import CustomGuardrail from litellm.proxy._types import UserAPIKeyAuth class ZeroUsageReproGuardrail(CustomGuardrail): async def async_post_call_success_hook( self, data: dict, user_api_key_dict: UserAPIKeyAuth, response, ): raise ModifyResponseException( message="Content flagged by policy, response withheld", model=data.get("model", "unknown") or "unknown", request_data=data, guardrail_name=self.guardrail_name or "zero-usage-repro", original_response=response, ) ``` Version: commit 9d069f21dc on litellm_internal_staging, proxy booted with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config c17_repro_config.yaml --port 41893 --detailed_debug`, real OpenAI API key, real provider calls Same prompt through both endpoints: ``` $ curl -sS http://localhost:41893/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a haiku about token accounting"}]}' ``` returns the block with the real usage the upstream call consumed: ```json { "id": "chatcmpl-66663aed-a8c6-4c2d-97cd-9eff02f7e001", "choices": [{"message": {"content": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld"}, "finish_reason": "content_filter"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 14, "completion_tokens": 18, "total_tokens": 32} } ``` ``` $ curl -sS http://localhost:41893/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"Write a haiku about token accounting"}' ``` returns the block with usage zeroed: ```json { "id": "resp_a87a5e6a-60ae-47c3-8602-59347a4b9ca2", "output": [{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld"}]}], "status": "completed", "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_details": null, "output_tokens": 0, "output_tokens_details": null, "total_tokens": 0} } ``` The proxy's own `--detailed_debug` log proves the blocked `/v1/responses` upstream call really consumed tokens. The RAW RESPONSE for it (upstream id `resp_00b30e92cd26f454006a7e8dc088d08198b9f384df52662262`) ends with: ```json "usage": { "input_tokens": 14, "input_tokens_details": {"cache_write_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 20, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 34 } ``` And the spend log rows for both blocked requests (GET /spend/logs/ui) show `prompt_tokens: 0, completion_tokens: 0, spend: 0.0` with an empty usage object, confirming the response body was the caller's only chance to see the real consumption ### What a fix PR should look like `litellm/proxy/response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py` catches `ModifyResponseException` and builds the synthetic blocked reply with `usage=ResponseAPIUsage(input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0, total_tokens=0)`, never reading `e.original_response`. That field exists exactly for this: the chat completions handler in `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` passes it through `_blocked_response_usage`, whose docstring spells out the contract (report the real usage the upstream call consumed, zero only for pre-call blocks), and `litellm/proxy/anthropic_endpoints/endpoints.py` does the same for `/v1/messages` The fix is to derive the `ResponseAPIUsage` from `e.original_response` in that handler: when the original response is a `ResponsesAPIResponse` its usage can be lifted directly, and when it is a chat `ModelResponse` (bridged calls) the `Usage` fields map as prompt_tokens -> input_tokens and completion_tokens -> output_tokens, falling back to zeros when `original_response` is `None` (pre-call block). Worth extracting a shared helper next to `_blocked_response_usage` rather than a third hand-rolled mapping Two adjacent gaps worth closing in the same PR so the fix actually reaches all guardrails: `raise_passthrough_exception` in `litellm/integrations/custom_guardrail.py` and the guardrail pipeline raiser in `litellm/proxy/utils.py` both raise `ModifyResponseException` without attaching `original_response`, so blocks raised through them zero out usage on every endpoint even where the handler is correct Regression test: extend the mapped test file for `response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py` with a post-call guardrail block carrying a known usage on `original_response` and assert the returned body's usage matches it, plus a pre-call block asserting zeros ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? commit 9d069f21dc (litellm_internal_staging) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: Vertex/Gemini: content-less candidate (thinking model at MAX_TOKENS) yields empty choices -> IndexError on choices[0]
signals.text: ### What happened When a Gemini candidate comes back with no `content` — for example a thinking model that spends its whole token budget on reasoning, so the candidate has `finishReason=MAX_TOKENS` and no content part — the Vertex transformation skips that candidate. If every candidate in the response is content-less, `model_response.choices` is left empty, and any caller that reads `response.choices[0]` hits `IndexError: list index out of range`. ### Expected The completion should still return a choice (with empty content) carrying a truncation `finish_reason` of `length`, so callers can see the response was cut off by the token limit and handle it (raise the limit, retry) instead of getting an opaque crash. ### Where `VertexGeminiConfig._process_candidates` in `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py`, the `if "content" not in candidate: continue` branch (non-streaming path). The streaming path already has its own empty-choice recovery. ### Repro Call a Gemini thinking model through litellm with a small `max_tokens` so the reasoning consumes the whole budget. The response has no content and `response.choices[0]` raises `IndexError`. Fix: #36870

signals.title: [Bug]: LiteLLM Proxy v1.93.0 intermittently drops prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens from final streaming usage
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? ### Actual behavior When LiteLLM Proxy `v1.93.0` serves OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions in streaming mode with: ```json { "stream": true, "stream_options": { "include_usage": true } } ``` the final SSE usage chunk intermittently contains `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, and `total_tokens`, but omits: ```json "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 0 } ``` The field is present on some streaming calls and absent on later calls through the same production route/model. ### Expected behavior If the upstream provider returns native cache usage, LiteLLM Proxy should preserve: ```json "prompt_tokens_details": { "cached_tokens": 0 } ``` in the final streaming usage chunk. `cached_tokens: 0` is valid telemetry and must not be removed by a truthy-value check. If the upstream provider does not return cache details, LiteLLM should keep the field absent rather than synthesizing `0`. ### Impact We calculate cache-aware token usage as: ```text effective_input_tokens = prompt_tokens - cached_tokens ``` When `cached_tokens` is missing, we must fail closed rather than assume `0`. Therefore otherwise successful calls cannot be included in cache-aware token or cost accounting. ### Investigation boundary Our client records whether the cache field exists before its own stream-usage merge logic. We can rule out client-side aggregation as the cause of the observed missing field. However, we do not yet have the raw upstream provider usage for every failed request, so we cannot fully distinguish between: 1. LiteLLM Proxy serialization dropping a field that was present upstream; and 2. the upstream provider not returning the field for that request. The LiteLLM streaming usage dict reconstruction path is the suspected Proxy-side code path. ### User Flow 1. Run LiteLLM Proxy `v1.93.0`. 2. Use a provider/model that can return `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. 3. Set: ```bash export LITELLM_CHAT_COMPLETIONS_URL="https://your-litellm-proxy/v1/chat/completions" export LITELLM_API_KEY="REDACTED" export MODEL="your-model-name" ``` 4. Run: ```python import json import os import httpx url = os.environ["LITELLM_CHAT_COMPLETIONS_URL"] api_key = os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"] model = os.environ["MODEL"] payload = { "model": model, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: ok"}, ], "temperature": 0, "stream": True, "stream_options": {"include_usage": True}, } def capture_terminal_usage(): usage = None with httpx.Client(timeout=120) as client: with client.stream( "POST", url, headers={ "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}", "Content-Type": "application/json", }, json=payload, ) as response: response.raise_for_status() for line in response.iter_lines(): if not line.startswith("data: "): continue body = line[len("data: "):] if body == "[DONE]": break event = json.loads(body) if event.get("usage") is not None: usage = event["usage"] if usage is None: raise RuntimeError("No terminal usage chunk received") return usage for attempt in range(1, 6): usage = capture_terminal_usage() details = usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {} print( json.dumps( { "attempt": attempt, "prompt_tokens": usage.get("prompt_tokens"), "completion_tokens": usage.get("completion_tokens"), "cached_tokens_present": "cached_tokens" in details, "cached_tokens": details.get("cached_tokens"), "full_usage": usage, } ) ) ``` 5. Observe that some final streaming usage chunks contain `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, while other chunks only contain top-level prompt/completion/total token counts. ### Proof the bug occurs # Application-level observation captured before client-side stream usage merging group=a answer_stream=1 prompt_tokens=5730 completion_tokens=1164 cache_detail_present=true cached_tokens=0 group=a answer_stream=2 prompt_tokens=7587 completion_tokens=1635 cache_detail_present=false cached_tokens=null group=a answer_stream=3 prompt_tokens=7587 completion_tokens=1635 cache_detail_present=false cached_tokens=null group=b answer_stream=1 prompt_tokens=13344 completion_tokens=1475 cache_detail_present=true cached_tokens=0 group=b answer_stream=2 prompt_tokens=16963 completion_tokens=2063 cache_detail_present=false cached_tokens=null group=b answer_stream=3 prompt_tokens=16963 completion_tokens=2063 cache_detail_present=false cached_tokens=null ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.93.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug] RetryPolicy has no NotFoundErrorRetries; router retries 404s and cools the whole deployment pool
signals.text: ### What happened? `RetryPolicy` (in `litellm/types/router.py`) lets you set per-exception retry counts, but there is **no `NotFoundErrorRetries` field**, and `get_num_retries_from_retry_policy()` (in `litellm/router_utils/get_retry_from_policy.py`) never checks for `litellm.NotFoundError`. As a result, a `404` cannot be pinned to `0` retries via `retry_policy`. It falls back to `num_retries`, so the router **retries 404s**. This is especially damaging with the Responses API. A `GET /responses/{id}` retrieve routed to a deployment that did not create the response returns `404`. Because 404 also triggers an **immediate cooldown** per deployment ("Non-Retryable Error" per the [cooldown docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/routing#cooldowns)), each retry: 1. picks a fresh deployment, 2. gets another 404, 3. cools that deployment down. After `num_retries` attempts the whole pool is cooled → `RouterRateLimitError("No deployments available")` → the client receives a **500** (which most clients treat as retriable) → the client retries → the burst amplifies into a fleet-wide 5xx storm. There is a **paradox** in the current behavior: 404 is documented as a "Non-Retryable Error" for cooldown purposes, yet the retry loop still retries it. So 404 is non-retryable for cooldown but retryable for retries — and each retry cools another deployment. ### Current `RetryPolicy` fields ``` BadRequestErrorRetries AuthenticationErrorRetries TimeoutErrorRetries RateLimitErrorRetries ContentPolicyViolationErrorRetries InternalServerErrorRetries # note: defined but never checked in get_num_retries_from_retry_policy() ``` `NotFoundErrorRetries` is missing. ### Proposed fix 1. Add `NotFoundErrorRetries: Optional[int] = None` to `RetryPolicy` in `litellm/types/router.py`. 2. Wire it into `get_num_retries_from_retry_policy()`: ```python from litellm.exceptions import NotFoundError ... if isinstance(exception, NotFoundError) and retry_policy.NotFoundErrorRetries is not None: return retry_policy.NotFoundErrorRetries ``` This lets operators set `NotFoundErrorRetries: 0` so 404s are surfaced to the client immediately instead of being retried across the deployment pool. Separately (secondary), it would be good to resolve the paradox so that an exception which triggers an immediate cooldown is not also retried by default. ### Relevant log output ``` RouterRateLimitError: No deployments available rejection_tracker WARNING - Request rejected reason=provider_error status_code=500 endpoint=/responses/resp_... ``` ### Are you a ML Ops Team? Yes ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: GET /health returns extra_headers and aws_session_token in plaintext
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related, not a duplicate: #18818 fixed masking of `extra_headers` on `/model/info`. `GET /health` is a different sanitizer. It still returns those values in full. `api_key` is stripped (CVE-2025-11203 class). `extra_headers` and `aws_session_token` were never added to that strip list. ### What happened? LiteLLM 1.96.2. No master key. A deployment in `config.yaml` has `extra_headers` (Azure `api-key`, Google `x-goog-api-key`, a Bearer token) and `aws_session_token`. `GET /health` returns those values in plaintext on the healthy (or unhealthy) row. `api_key` is absent. `api_base` is absent for a non-admin caller. The extra headers stay. This was reproduced with fake `CANARY_*` strings, not real provider keys. A live proxy with a normal `api_key: os.environ/...` and no `extra_headers` does not echo the resolved key on `/model/info` (`api_key` is popped). The hole is specifically fields that are not `api_key`. Expected: `/health` should omit or mask `extra_headers`, `headers`, and `aws_session_token` the same way it already omits `api_key`. ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a tenant who can call `/health` can read the admin's upstream credentials out of the JSON. 1. The proxy admin puts provider auth in `litellm_params.extra_headers` (and optionally `aws_session_token`) in `config.yaml`, then starts the proxy on `http://127.0.0.1:4000`. 2. Any caller sends `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/health` with no `Authorization` header (default install, no master key). 3. HTTP 200. The `healthy_endpoints` (or `unhealthy_endpoints`) row contains `extra_headers.Authorization`, `extra_headers.x-goog-api-key`, `extra_headers.api-key`, and `aws_session_token` in full. 4. That caller can take those values and call the provider directly, bypassing the proxy. After a (hypothetical) fix: the same `/health` call still reports healthy/unhealthy, but those secret fields are gone or masked. 1. The proxy admin uses the same `config.yaml` and starts the same proxy. 2. The same caller sends `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/health`. 3. HTTP 200. The row still has `model` and health status. It does not contain the `extra_headers` values or `aws_session_token`. 4. That caller cannot recover the admin's upstream credentials from `/health`. ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: mock litellm_params: model: openai/mockmodel api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9996/v1 api_key: sk-x-CANARY_DEPLOYMENT_API_KEY extra_headers: Authorization: Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE ``` The backend at `127.0.0.1:9996` is a local OpenAI-compatible stub that returns HTTP 200 so the row lands in `healthy_endpoints`. The leak is the proxy copying `litellm_params` into the `/health` body. It does not depend on a real provider key. You can drop the stub: point `api_base` at `http://127.0.0.1:1`. The health check fails, and the same fields still appear under `unhealthy_endpoints`. No API key required. Version or commit: LiteLLM **1.96.2** Commands and their full output: ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/health ``` ```json { "healthy_endpoints": [ { "model": "openai/mockmodel", "extra_headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION", "x-goog-api-key": "CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE", "api-key": "CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY" }, "aws_session_token": "CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE" } ], "unhealthy_endpoints": [], "healthy_count": 1, "unhealthy_count": 0 } ``` `api_key` is not in that object. `GET /v1/models` and `GET /health/liveliness` do not contain the canaries. Copy-paste repro, no keys, no stub: ```yaml # leak.yaml model_list: - model_name: demo litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_base: http://127.0.0.1:1 api_key: sk-not-a-real-key extra_headers: x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE ``` ``` litellm --config leak.yaml --port 4000 --host 127.0.0.1 curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/health ``` The canaries show up on the unhealthy row. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2

signals.title: [Bug] Exa search: `contents.highlights` and `contents.summary` are sent, billed, and then dropped by `transform_search_response`
signals.text: ### What happened When calling `POST /v1/search/{exa_tool}` with Exa's `contents.highlights` or `contents.summary`, the request is forwarded to Exa correctly and Exa bills for the content retrieval — but every result comes back with `snippet: ""`. The response transformer reads only Exa's `text` field. Because `highlights` and `summary` are returned by Exa in their *own* response fields (and Exa returns **no** `text` field when you ask for highlights/summary alone), the retrieved content is discarded and the caller gets empty snippets. The result is a silent, billed no-op: no error, HTTP 200, five well-formed results, zero content. ### Environment - LiteLLM proxy `v1.83.3` (verified identical on `v1.83.3-stable` and `main`) - Provider: `exa_ai`, configured via `search_tools` ```yaml search_tools: - search_tool_name: exa-search litellm_params: search_provider: exa_ai api_key: os.environ/EXA_API_KEY ``` ### Reproduction **A — `contents.text.maxCharacters` (works, for contrast):** ```bash curl -sS -X POST "$PROXY/v1/search/exa-search" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query":"net interest margin outlook","max_results":5, "contents":{"text":{"maxCharacters":800}}}' ``` Every result returns exactly 800 characters. Correct — `contents` passes through, and Exa's `text` is mapped to `snippet`. **B — `contents.highlights` (broken):** ```bash curl -sS -X POST "$PROXY/v1/search/exa-search" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query":"net interest margin outlook","max_results":3, "contents":{"highlights":{"query":"net interest margin outlook","numSentences":3}}}' ``` **C — `contents.summary` (broken, same way):** ```bash curl -sS -X POST "$PROXY/v1/search/exa-search" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query":"net interest margin outlook","max_results":3, "contents":{"summary":{"query":"What is the outlook for net interest margin?"}}}' ``` ### Actual result (B and C) ```json { "object": "search", "results": [ { "title": "Lion Finance Group (LON:BGEO) Q1 2026 Earnings Call Transcript & Audio", "url": "https://stockanalysis.com/quote/lon/BGEO/transcripts/557900-q1-2026/", "snippet": "", "date": null, "last_updated": null } ] } ``` All results have `snippet: ""`. Measured against the same query, the same call with `contents.text` returns 2,804–65,974 characters per result, so the search itself is working — only the content is lost. ### Expected result The highlights/summary content Exa returned (and billed for) should reach the caller — either surfaced in `snippet`, or preserved as additional fields. ### Root cause `litellm/llms/exa_ai/search/transformation.py` → `transform_search_response`: ```python for result in response_json.get("results", []): search_result = SearchResult( title=result.get("title", ""), url=result.get("url", ""), snippet=result.get("text", ""), # only "text" is ever read date=result.get("publishedDate"), last_updated=None, ) ``` Exa's search response carries `highlights` (list of strings), `highlightScores`, and `summary` when those content modes are requested. None are read here, so they are dropped during transformation. The request side is correct — `transform_search_request` explicitly passes unrecognised parameters through as-is, which is why `contents` reaches Exa at all and why `contents.text.maxCharacters` works. Note that `SearchResult` already sets `model_config = {"extra": "allow"}` (`litellm/llms/base_llm/search/transformation.py`), so carrying extra fields requires no change to the unified schema. ### Proposed fix Fall back through the content modes so a caller who asked for highlights/summary gets something in `snippet`, and additionally preserve the raw fields: ```python snippet=( result.get("text") or "\n\n".join(result.get("highlights") or []) or result.get("summary") or "" ), highlights=result.get("highlights"), summary=result.get("summary"), ``` Happy to open a PR if this looks like the right shape — in particular whether you'd prefer the fallback in `snippet`, the extra fields only, or both. ### Two related observations 1. **Same pattern in the Tavily adapter.** `litellm/llms/tavily/search/transformation.py` maps `results[].content → snippet` and does not read `raw_content`, nor the top-level `answer`. Sending `include_raw_content: true` / `include_answer: true` through the proxy returns no `raw_content` field and no `answer` field, matching this Exa behaviour. If the fix above is acceptable, the same treatment probably applies there. 2. **Default `contents` injection is worth documenting.** `transform_search_request` does: ```python if "contents" not in result_data: result_data["contents"] = {"text": True} ``` Exa returns no page content unless asked, so this is a sensible default — but it means an unqualified search retrieves **full page text** for every result. In our measurements that was up to 65,974 characters per result and ~182k tokens across a single 10-result search. Callers who don't know to send `contents.text.maxCharacters` get very large payloads by default. A note in the Exa search docs would help; a default cap might be worth considering.
signals.author: petervines

signals.title: [Bug]: Anthropic /v1/messages: role:"system" messages inside messages[] are silently dropped
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a client sends an Anthropic `/v1/messages` request whose `messages[]` array contains an entry with `role: "system"`, that entry never reaches the backend model. The top-level `system` field is delivered correctly; the in-array one is discarded with no warning and no error. **What I expected:** the in-array system content reaches the model (translated into an OpenAI system message), or failing that, an explicit error. Silent omission is the harmful case, because the request succeeds with HTTP 200 and the response looks completely normal. **Why this shape matters.** Anthropic supports mid-conversation system messages, and Claude Code uses that channel to deliver its skill listing — the catalogue of available Agent Skills that a model needs in order to decide whether to invoke one. Pointing Claude Code at a LiteLLM proxy backed by an OpenAI-compatible model therefore strips the catalogue, and the model behaves as though no skills exist. We lost a 192-cell benchmark run to this. Every cell recorded zero skill invocation, which read as a model-capability finding until we captured request payloads on both sides of the proxy and saw the message count drop from 2 to 1. Anyone benchmarking agent-skill discovery across models through this bridge will silently measure the bridge instead of the model. **Related, but not duplicates:** - #23841 (open) reports five bugs in this same area — `input_text` content blocks being dropped, plus several env-var routing failures. It does not cover `role: "system"` entries inside `messages[]`. - #17904 ("Cannot use claude-code + LiteLLM with openai models") describes symptoms that may share this root cause, but does not identify it. **Workaround** for anyone hitting this now: a small shim in front of the proxy that hoists `role: "system"` messages into the top-level `system` field before the request reaches LiteLLM. Ours is ~150 lines and restored skill invocation from 0/192 cells to the expected rates. ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix** — the model never learns which skills exist, so it never invokes one, and nothing tells me why. 1. I install an Agent Skill into my project so Claude Code can use it, then point Claude Code at my gateway with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4002` and pick an OpenAI-compatible model. 2. I ask it to do the task the skill exists for: "Write the release notes for version 0.2.0." 3. Claude Code sends `POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages`. Its request carries two messages: one with role `"system"` listing the skills available to me, and one with role `"user"` holding my request. 4. I get back HTTP 200 and a perfectly normal answer — the model writes release notes in its own default style. 5. The skill is never invoked. There is no warning, no error, and no hint in the response that anything was missing. From my seat it is indistinguishable from the model deciding the skill was not relevant. 6. I can isolate the invisible part with two requests. I send `POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages` with a codeword inside a role `"system"` message in `messages[]`, asking the model to repeat it — it replies `NONE`. I send the identical request with that codeword in the top-level `"system"` field instead — it replies `PINEAPPLE-7731`. Same gateway, same model, same question, HTTP 200 both times. **After a (hypothetical) fix** — the model receives the listing and invokes the skill. 1. Identical. 2. Identical. 3. Identical. 4. I get back HTTP 200, and the release notes follow the format the skill defines rather than the model's default style. 5. The skill is invoked, because the model actually received the listing describing it. 6. Both requests in step 6 now reply `PINEAPPLE-7731` — whether the codeword arrives inside a role `"system"` message in `messages[]` or in the top-level `"system"` field. ### Proof the bug occurs Live proxy I ran myself, real provider calls, no mocks. **Version** ``` LiteLLM: Current Version = 1.91.4 ``` **config.yaml** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: qwen3.6-35b litellm_params: model: openai/qwen3.6-35b api_base: https://freeinference.org/v1 api_key: os.environ/FREEINFERENCE_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-repro-local ``` **Env vars the proxy ran with** ``` FREEINFERENCE_API_KEY=<redacted> ``` **Started with** ```bash litellm --config config.yaml --port 4002 --host 127.0.0.1 ``` --- ### TEST A — codeword inside `messages[]` as `role: "system"` (the bug) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages \ -H "x-api-key: sk-repro-local" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "messages":[ {"role":"system","content":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731."}, {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `content`: ```json [ { "type": "text", "text": "NONE" } ] ``` The model never received the codeword. --- ### TEST B — identical codeword in the top-level `system` field (control) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages \ -H "x-api-key: sk-repro-local" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "system":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731.", "messages":[ {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `content`: ```json [ { "type": "text", "text": "PINEAPPLE-7731" } ] ``` Same gateway, same model, same question — the only difference is where the system content was placed. --- ### TEST C — `/v1/chat/completions` with the same `role: "system"` message (endpoint NOT affected) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-local" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "messages":[ {"role":"system","content":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731."}, {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `choices[0].message.content`: ``` PINEAPPLE-7731 ``` So the same message shape is honoured on `/v1/chat/completions` and dropped on `/v1/messages`. `/v1/responses` was not tested. [root-cause-analysis.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31067236/root-cause-analysis.md) ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.91.4 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details @pranavh2004 / www.linkedin.com/in/pranav-hemanth

signals.title: [Bug]: `acount_tokens()` silently returns `total_tokens=0` for Vertex AI Gemini models
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? ### What happened `litellm.acount_tokens()` returns `total_tokens=0` with `error=False` for any `vertex_ai/gemini-*` model when called with `messages` (the documented usage). The messages are never sent to Vertex, and the failure is not surfaced — neither as an exception, nor via the `error` flag, nor by falling back to local counting. ### Reproduction Requires ADC for a project with Vertex AI enabled. ```python import asyncio, os import litellm os.environ["VERTEXAI_PROJECT"] = "<your-project>" os.environ["VERTEXAI_LOCATION"] = "us-central1" async def main(): result = await litellm.acount_tokens( model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello, how are you? " * 50}], ) print(result.total_tokens, repr(result.tokenizer_type), result.error) asyncio.run(main()) ``` **Expected:** ~301 (the count Vertex's `:countTokens` returns for this text), with `tokenizer_type` indicating the provider API — or, if provider counting is unavailable, the documented local-tiktoken fallback. **Actual:** ``` 0 '' False ``` That the endpoint itself is reachable and correct with the same credentials, model and location is easy to confirm — passing Gemini-format `contents` directly to the same handler works: ```python from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.count_tokens.handler import VertexAITokenCounter await VertexAITokenCounter().acount_tokens( model="gemini-2.5-flash", contents=[{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "Hello, how are you? " * 50}]}], vertex_project=os.environ["VERTEXAI_PROJECT"], vertex_location="us-central1", ) # {'totalTokens': 301, 'totalBillableCharacters': 800, # 'promptTokensDetails': [{'modality': 'TEXT', 'tokenCount': 301}]} ``` ### Root cause Three things compound, all still present on `v1.96.2`: 1. **`messages` is never converted to `contents`.** `litellm/main.py::acount_tokens` unconditionally passes `contents=None` to the provider counter ([`main.py:8753`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/main.py#L8753)), leaving conversion to the provider. 2. **The Vertex Gemini branch ignores `messages`.** `VertexAITokenCounter.count_tokens` ([`llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py:1100`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py#L1100)) splits on `is_vertex_partner_model`. The partner-model branch (Claude on Vertex) forwards `messages=messages or []` and works correctly. The Gemini branch builds `{"model": ..., "contents": contents}` ([line 1174](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py#L1174)) and never reads `messages`, so the request body posted is `{"contents": null}` ([`llms/gemini/count_tokens/handler.py:133`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/llms/gemini/count_tokens/handler.py#L133)). 3. **The empty response reads as a valid answer of zero.** Vertex accepts `{"contents": null}` with HTTP 200 and a response carrying no `totalTokens`, so `total_tokens=result.get("totalTokens", 0)` ([line 1183](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py#L1183)) yields `0`. Because the result is non-`None` and `error` is falsy, `acount_tokens` returns it immediately and the local-tiktoken fallback is never reached. The proxy endpoints are not an alternative path: `TokenCountRequest` exposes `contents` as a separate field, i.e. Google-format callers are expected to supply `contents` themselves. There is no `messages` → `contents` conversion anywhere in the token-counting code. ### Why the silent zero matters The natural use of this API is a pre-flight guard against context-window overflow. A silently-zero count inverts the guard: every payload appears to fit, and the overflow surfaces later as a provider `400` on the real request. A raised exception, or the documented fallback, would both be safe; returning `0` is not. ### Suggested fix Convert in the Vertex Gemini branch, so the SDK and the proxy are both covered: ```python else: from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.count_tokens.handler import VertexAITokenCounter from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.gemini.transformation import ( _gemini_convert_messages_with_history, ) if contents is None and messages is not None: contents = _gemini_convert_messages_with_history(messages=messages) ... ``` and treat a response without `totalTokens` as a failure rather than a zero, so the documented local fallback is reached: ```python if result is not None and "totalTokens" in result: return TokenCountResponse(...) return None ``` ### Related, lower priority **`system` and `tools` are dropped on the Vertex Gemini path.** `acount_tokens` accepts both, but the handler posts only `{"contents": ...}`. Vertex's `:countTokens` does honour the other request fields — measured on `gemini-3.6-flash`, global endpoint: | request body | `totalTokens` | | --- | --- | | `contents` only | 7 | | `contents` + `systemInstruction` | 107 | | `contents` + `tools` | 31 | So an assembled prompt is under-counted by however much its system instruction and tool declarations cost. Note that `_gemini_convert_messages_with_history` folds a `system` message into the user `contents`, which counts the text but not the `systemInstruction` framing. **The local fallback has no Gemini tokenizer.** `_select_tokenizer_helper` ([`utils.py:1945`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/utils.py#L1945)) special-cases cohere `command-r`, pre-`claude-3` Anthropic and llama-2/3; everything else falls through to tiktoken `cl100k`. For Gemini that is substantially optimistic on token-dense input, which is what makes the silent fallback in issue 3 above consequential. Measured against the API on `gemini-3.6-flash`: | input | `litellm.token_counter` (local) | Vertex `:countTokens` | error | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | prose, 72k chars | 17,939 | 19,344 | 7% optimistic | | dense numeric, 1.0M chars | 528,006 | 959,999 | **45% optimistic** | Documenting `local_tokenizer` as approximate-only for Gemini would help; a Gemini tokenizer would help more. ### Environment - litellm **1.82.3** — all behaviour above reproduced live against Vertex AI. - litellm **1.96.2** (latest at time of writing) — verified by source inspection to be unchanged in all four locations cited; not run live. - Python 3.12, Vertex AI Gemini via ADC (`gemini-2.5-flash` regional, `gemini-3.6-flash` and `gemini-3.7-flash` on the `global` endpoint — all three affected, all three counted correctly via the direct-`contents` workaround). ### User Flow See above ### Proof the bug occurs See above ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: responses() crashes with TypeError 'int object is not iterable' when input is numeric instead of returning 400
signals.text: ## Description `litellm.responses()` crashes with `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable` when `input` is a non-string, non-list type (e.g. integer, float, bool, None, dict). Instead of returning a clear validation error (HTTP 400), the TypeError propagates through `exception_type()` which has no `status_code`, falls through to `APIConnectionError`, and returns HTTP 500. ## Repro ```python import litellm response = litellm.responses( model="gpt-5.1", input=12345, # integer instead of string or list ) ``` ## Stack trace ```text File "litellm/responses/main.py", line 588, in _apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call for item in input TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable ``` ## Root cause In `litellm/responses/main.py`, `_apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call()` (both the async branch in `aresponses()` and the sync helper) checks only `isinstance(input, str)`: ```python if isinstance(input, str): client_input = [{"role": "user", "content": input}] else: client_input = [ item for item in input # ← crashes when input is not iterable if isinstance(item, dict) and "role" in item ] ``` When `input` is not a string, it assumes it is iterable. Non-string, non-list types (int, float, bool, None, dict) raise TypeError during `for item in input`. ## Expected behavior Invalid `input` types should raise `BadRequestError` with a descriptive message (e.g. "input must be a string or list of input items, got int") so the proxy returns HTTP 400 instead of HTTP 500. ## Suggested fix Add a type guard before iteration: ```python if isinstance(input, str): client_input = [{"role": "user", "content": input}] elif not isinstance(input, list): raise BadRequestError( message=f"'input' must be a string or list of input items, got {type(input).__name__}", model=model, llm_provider=custom_llm_provider or "unknown", ) else: client_input = [ item for item in input if isinstance(item, dict) and "role" in item ] ``` This applies at two locations in `litellm/responses/main.py`: 1. The async prompt-management branch (line ~472) 2. The sync `_apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call` helper (line ~583) ## Impact - Invalid client requests are misclassified as provider/system failures - Client receives retryable-looking 500 instead of non-retryable 400 - LiteLLM retry/cooldown machinery may treat this as a deployment failure, which can amplify impact ## Environment - LiteLLM version: v1.92.0 (observed in production; also present on current main) - Endpoint: `POST /v1/responses` / `POST /responses`
signals.author: LaPetiteSouris

signals.title: [Bug]: False BudgetExceededError under sustained load — 'Current cost' = max_budget + recent spend, no Redis, self-heals in ~2 min
signals.text: ### What happened During sustained batch runs (~100-130 requests over ~40 min, single client, mix of `/v1/ocr` Mistral passthrough, Gemini `generateContent` passthrough and Anthropic passthrough), the proxy starts returning `429 budget_exceeded` near the end of the run, with a reported `Current cost` that matches **no real aggregate**. The reported value is always `max_budget + (small recent spend)`, and the condition **self-heals in about 2 minutes** without any intervention: a retry with 15s/30s/60s backoff fails 3 times, then the 4th attempt succeeds. We reproduced this on **v1.88.1** and again on **v1.96.2** after upgrading, and once earlier when our global cap was 20 instead of 50 — the phantom value tracked the cap each time. ### Occurrences | Date | Proxy version | Configured cap | Error message excerpt | Real spend at that moment | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2026-07-01 | 1.88.1 | 20 (global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 20.013879769999956, Max budget: 20` | a few cents that day | | 2026-08-14 AM | 1.88.1 | 50 (key + global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Key=<hash> Current cost: 51.0512, Max budget: 50.0`, then `Current cost: 50.014505` on the two retries | key spend that day ~1.05 USD | | 2026-08-14 PM | 1.96.2 | 50 (key + global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Key=<alias> (sk-...) Current cost: 50.024508499999996, Max budget: 50.0` | key spend that day ~1.1 USD | In each case `Current cost - max_budget` equals the key's genuine recent spend (e.g. `51.0512 - 50 = 1.0512` ≈ the 1.05 USD actually spent by the run so far). It looks like an in-memory spend counter transiently gets seeded/inflated with the `max_budget` value itself. ### What the database said at the same time Checked immediately around the 2026-08-14 AM occurrence: - `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` for the key: **1.07** - `sum(spend)` in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` for that key, last 30 days: **1.59** - `sum(spend)` in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`, all keys, all time: **24.90** - No individual SpendLogs row above 0.04 - `/global/spend`: 4.24 / 50 Nothing anywhere near 50, and no row disappeared afterwards. The inflated value existed only in memory and was gone once the periodic DB resync ran (the 4th retry, ~2 min after the first 429, passed; `/key/info` afterwards reported the correct small spend). ### Setup - Docker `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, **single instance**, **no Redis** (in-memory cache only) - Postgres-backed (`database_url` set), default batch-write settings - `litellm_settings`: `max_budget: 50`, `budget_duration: 30d`, `turn_off_message_logging: true`, `drop_params: true`, `telemetry: false` - Virtual key with `max_budget: 50`, `budget_duration: 30d`, model ACL - `router_settings`: `simple-shuffle`, `num_retries: 0`, `allowed_fails: 0`, `cooldown_time: 60`, cross-provider fallbacks configured - Load pattern when it triggers: ~100+ requests spread over ~40 min through one virtual key, several requests in flight concurrently (bounded page-level concurrency). Light traffic (20 sequential probes) never triggers it. ### Expected behavior Budget checks compare against actual spend. A request should not be rejected with `Current cost ≈ max_budget + real spend` while the durable stores all agree spend is ~2% of the cap. ### Possibly related - #27735 (stale spend in BudgetExceededError while `/key/info` disagrees) — same symptom family, but our value is not stale, it is inflated by exactly `max_budget` and self-corrects - #30460 (Redis counters inflating) — we run without Redis, so the in-memory path can inflate on its own ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.96.2 (also reproduced on v1.88.1)
signals.author: gianito

signals.title: [Bug]: interactions.create() silently drops response_format when routed via litellm_proxy (Gemini)
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When `USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true` (or `litellm.use_litellm_proxy=True`) is set process-wide, `litellm.interactions.create()` for a Gemini model silently loses its `response_format` (JSON schema / mime type constraint) with no error or warning, and the model falls back to free-text output. Root cause, traced through the source: 1. `get_llm_provider()` (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/get_llm_provider_logic.py`) checks `LiteLLMProxyChatConfig._should_use_litellm_proxy_by_default()` **first, unconditionally**, before looking at any explicitly-passed `custom_llm_provider`. With `USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true` set, this forces `custom_llm_provider="litellm_proxy"` for *every* litellm call in the process, including `interactions.create()`. 2. `get_provider_interactions_api_config()` (`litellm/interactions/utils.py`) only recognizes `provider == "gemini"`. For `"litellm_proxy"` it returns `None`. 3. Back in `litellm/interactions/main.py`, when `interactions_api_config is None`, the call **silently bridges to `litellm.responses()`** via `LiteLLMResponsesInteractionsHandler` instead of raising or warning. 4. That bridge's request transform, `transform_interactions_request_to_responses_request()` (`litellm/interactions/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py`), maps `system_instruction`, `input`, `tools`, and parts of `generation_config` — but has **no handling for `response_format` at all**. It's dropped entirely, silently. Net effect: a caller who explicitly requested strict JSON-schema output via the Interactions API gets back ordinary free-text (Gemini then wraps its answer in a markdown code fence, as it typically does without an explicit JSON constraint), with no exception and no log line indicating the constraint was dropped. This is especially easy to hit by accident: `USE_LITELLM_PROXY` is a reasonable thing to set globally so that `litellm.responses()`/`litellm.completion()` route through a self-hosted LiteLLM Proxy, but doing so silently breaks the Interactions API for the same process. Confirmed present in every version I checked, `1.82.0` through the current latest `1.96.2` (checked wheel/sdist contents directly) — `litellm/llms/litellm_proxy/interactions/` does not exist in any of them, unlike `litellm/llms/litellm_proxy/{chat,responses,image_generation,image_edit,skills}/` which do. ### Steps to Reproduce ```python import os os.environ["USE_LITELLM_PROXY"] = "true" import litellm response = litellm.interactions.create( model="gemini-3.5-flash", system_instruction="Respond only with JSON matching the schema.", input=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Say hello and give a score of 1."}]}], response_format={ "type": "text", "mime_type": "application/json", "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": {"greeting": {"type": "string"}, "score": {"type": "number"}}, "required": ["greeting", "score"], }, }, generation_config={"max_output_tokens": 512}, api_base="http://localhost:4000", # a real LiteLLM Proxy instance api_key="sk-...", # a valid virtual key for that proxy ) ``` Expected: request reaches the proxy's `/interactions`-equivalent handling (or, if unsupported, the fallback should still honor `response_format`), returning clean JSON. Actual: request is silently rerouted to `/responses` with `response_format` dropped; the returned text is unconstrained free text (often markdown-fenced JSON, not raw JSON), and `json.loads()` on it fails intermittently depending on how the model chooses to format its answer. ### Relevant log output ```shell # No warning/error is logged - the drop is completely silent. Confirmed via the local proxy's # access log: with USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true, an interactions.create() call for a Gemini model never # produces a "/interactions" (or equivalent) hit on the proxy - only "/responses" hits appear, # confirming the silent bridge. ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy / Interactions API ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.0 (also reproduced on v1.96.2; confirmed present via source inspection back through v1.82.0) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
signals.author: Jeevan-threev

signals.title: [Bug]: Gemini reasoning/thinking content leaks into output_text for /responses with reasoning.effort=medium|high, breaking strict json_schema
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Calling `litellm.responses()` for a Gemini model with a strict `json_schema` output format works correctly at `reasoning.effort="low"` (or unset), returning clean, schema-conformant JSON. Raising `reasoning.effort` to `"medium"` or `"high"` breaks this: the model's raw chain-of-thought narrative is returned as the `output_text` / message content instead of the requested JSON, and the `strict: true` json_schema constraint is effectively ignored. Example actual output at `reasoning.effort="high"` (this is the full `output[0].content[0].text`, not a summary): ``` **My Approach to Crafting the JSON Response** Okay, here's how I'm approaching this. The task is straightforward: generate a JSON response that says "hello" and gives a score of 1. It needs to be perfectly formatted JSON and nothing else - no extra text, no markdown, no comments, just valid, parseable... [... continues for 400+ tokens of first-person reasoning narrative, sometimes including its own markdown code fence with a correct JSON example buried in the middle, before or without ever emitting the JSON as the actual final answer ...] ``` This strongly looks like the model's "thinking"/reasoning content is not being kept separate from the final answer content when Gemini is accessed through the Responses API surface (there's no native `litellm/llms/gemini/responses/` provider config - I believe this goes through a chat-completions-style bridge). For comparison, OpenAI's own reasoning models keep reasoning content out of the final message content (tracked only via `usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`) - Gemini's thinking content is not being handled the same way here, and it also appears to override/ignore the requested strict `json_schema` format once reasoning is engaged at higher effort. `reasoning_tokens` in the usage response does increase correctly with effort level (e.g. 0 at low, 225-400+ at medium/high), confirming the model *is* being asked to think more - the bug is specifically that that content ends up in the answer instead of being separated out, and that it overrides the structured-output constraint. Reproduced identically on both **v1.90.0** and **v1.96.0** (six minor versions apart), so this isn't a recent regression - it looks like a long-standing gap in how Gemini's thinking output is handled via the Responses API bridge. ### Steps to Reproduce ```python import litellm schema = { "type": "object", "properties": {"greeting": {"type": "string"}, "score": {"type": "number"}}, "required": ["greeting", "score"], "additionalProperties": False, } for effort in ["low", "medium", "high"]: response = litellm.responses( model="gemini-3.5-flash", instructions="You are a helpful assistant. Respond only with JSON matching the schema.", input=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Say hello and give a score of 1."}]}], max_output_tokens=512, reasoning={"effort": effort}, text={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "smoke_test", "strict": True, "schema": schema}}, api_base="http://localhost:4000", # a real LiteLLM Proxy instance, gemini-3.5-flash mapped to gemini/gemini-3.5-flash api_key="sk-...", ) text = response.output[0].content[0].text print(effort, "-> valid JSON prefix:", text.strip().startswith("{"), "| len:", len(text)) ``` Expected output: ``` low -> valid JSON prefix: True | len: ~40 medium -> valid JSON prefix: True | len: ~40 high -> valid JSON prefix: True | len: ~40 ``` Actual output: ``` low -> valid JSON prefix: True | len: 41 medium -> valid JSON prefix: False | len: 1130 high -> valid JSON prefix: False | len: 1465 ``` ### Relevant log output ```shell N/A - no error is raised; the response is returned successfully with status "completed", just with reasoning prose as the content instead of the requested structured JSON. ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Responses API / Gemini provider ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.0 (also reproduced on v1.90.0) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
signals.author: Jeevan-threev

signals.title: [Bug] Databricks provider sends internal `thinking_blocks` field instead of the documented `reasoning` content block, breaking multi-turn extended thinking
signals.text: **LiteLLM version:** v1.96.0 **Provider:** `databricks` (Azure Databricks Foundation Model API) **Models:** `system.ai.claude-opus-5`, `system.ai.claude-sonnet-5` ## What happens Multi-turn conversations with extended thinking fail as soon as an assistant message containing thinking content is replayed as history: ``` litellm.BadRequestError: DatabricksException - {"error_code":"BAD_REQUEST", "message":"{\"message\":\"messages.98.thinking_blocks: Extra inputs are not permitted\"}"} ``` The first turn always succeeds. The failing index tracks conversation length — it is whichever message is the first assistant turn carrying thinking content. ## Cause `litellm/llms/databricks/chat/transformation.py` (~line 499) extracts reasoning content from Databricks responses into LiteLLM's internal `thinking_blocks` representation. There is no corresponding conversion on the **request** path, so on the next turn `thinking_blocks` is emitted as a message-level field. Databricks validates strictly and rejects unknown message fields. ## This is not a Databricks limitation Databricks accepts reasoning content on input. I verified the wire format empirically by capturing a real reasoning block from `system.ai.claude-opus-5` and replaying it in each candidate shape. Only one is accepted: | Assistant content block shape | Result | | --- | --- | | `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": ..., "signature": ...}` (Anthropic native) | rejected, `Failed to parse ContentItem` | | `{"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"type": "reasoning_text", ...}], "encrypted_content": ...}` | rejected, `Expecting one non-null Summary` | | `{"type": "reasoning", "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": ..., "signature": ...}]}` | **accepted** | | message-level `thinking_blocks` (current behaviour) | rejected, `Extra inputs are not permitted` | So the target format is a `reasoning` content block carrying a `summary` array: ```json { "type": "reasoning", "summary": [ { "type": "summary_text", "text": "...", "signature": "<opaque provider signature>" } ] } ``` Note that Databricks' published docs for multi-turn reasoning describe `content` / `reasoning_text` with `encrypted_content`, which the endpoint actively rejects. The shape asserted by the existing test in `tests/test_litellm/llms/databricks/chat/test_databricks_chat_transformation.py` is the correct one, and matches what the provider's own response parsing already produces The `signature` must be replayed unmodified. Dropping it loses the reasoning chain even when the request is accepted ## Expected behaviour On the request path, the Databricks provider should convert LiteLLM `thinking_blocks` into the documented `reasoning` content block, mapping the Anthropic thinking `signature` to `encrypted_content` so reasoning continuity is preserved. Note that **merely stripping `thinking_blocks` is only a partial fix**: it clears the 400 but discards the reasoning chain, which is the behaviour Databricks explicitly describes as "the model can't reason over its earlier thinking." ## Control The Anthropic provider round-trips thinking correctly in the same LiteLLM version, with the same client and the same conversation — only the `databricks` provider fails. So the round trip is clearly within LiteLLM's remit. ## Related prior issues - **#15758** — same error. Closed by the reporter within a day, attributing it to Databricks (*"this is a Databricks issue and cannot be fixed with code"*). Per the documentation above, that attribution is incorrect and the bug is still present. - **#9790** — feature request for exactly this, went stale and was auto-closed. The reporter there used `summary` / `summary_text`, which is not the documented schema either, so that failure was also a format mismatch rather than a missing feature. ## Reproduction 1. Configure a `databricks` deployment for `system.ai.claude-opus-5`. 2. Send a request with extended thinking enabled. 3. Append the assistant response, including reasoning content, to the message list. 4. Send a second request with that history → 400 as above. ## Environment note Requests reach the endpoint via `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`. Separately observed on the same models: `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` are rejected with 400 by both `claude-opus-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` (Databricks documents this for Sonnet 5 only). Not related to this bug, but relevant to anyone configuring these deployments — `drop_params` handles it.
signals.author: pokepoke81

signals.title: [Bug] Databricks provider drops Anthropic prompt-cache token counts when streaming
signals.text: **LiteLLM version:** v1.96.0 (also reproduced on v1.90.2) **Provider:** `databricks` (Azure Databricks Foundation Model API, Claude models) **Model:** `system.ai.claude-opus-5` ## What happens With `stream: false`, prompt-cache token counts are returned correctly. With `stream: true`, `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` are absent from the usage object entirely — not zero, absent. Because spend is computed from the usage object, every streamed Databricks request is costed at the full input rate even when it was served from cache. For an Anthropic-format agent client that always streams and relies on prompt caching, this makes reported spend diverge sharply from actual provider cost. Importantly, **caching itself works** — only the accounting is broken. See "Caching is actually working" below. ## Reproduction Identical payload, only `stream` differs. Fallbacks and retries disabled. ```python body = { "model": "claude-opus", # -> databricks/system.ai.claude-opus-5 "max_tokens": 8, "system": [{"type": "text", "text": CORPUS, # ~9.6k tokens "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}], "disable_fallbacks": True, "num_retries": 0, } ``` **Non-streaming — correct:** ``` 1st (cold) input_tokens=11 cache_creation_input_tokens=9603 cache_read_input_tokens=None 2nd (warm) input_tokens=11 cache_creation_input_tokens=None cache_read_input_tokens=9603 ``` **Streaming — cache fields missing from every event:** ``` message_start usage: {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": ...} message_delta usage: {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 1} ``` ### Same-endpoint control, with `stream_options` To rule out `stream_options` as the cause, the following ran against `/v1/chat/completions` with `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}` on both providers — identical payload, identical proxy, only the provider differs: ``` anthropic cold prompt_tokens_details: {"cached_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 10, "cache_write_tokens": ...} anthropic warm prompt_tokens_details: {"cached_tokens": 13304, "text_tokens": 10, "cache_write_tokens": ...} databricks cold (no prompt_tokens_details) prompt_tokens: 7015 databricks warm (no prompt_tokens_details) prompt_tokens: 7015 ``` The Anthropic provider is correct in both streaming and non-streaming modes. Note also that **without** `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` the Databricks streaming response contains **no usage chunk at all**. Setting `general_settings.always_include_stream_usage: true` restores the usage chunk but still yields no cache fields — so the gap is in response parsing, not in the request or in `stream_options` handling. ## Caching is actually working A streamed request with `cache_control` was sent, then the same corpus was sent non-streaming. The non-streaming call reported `cached_tokens: 13303` on its *first* call — i.e. the preceding streaming request had populated the cache. So streaming requests participate in caching normally; the tokens are simply never surfaced in the usage object. This means reported cost for streamed Databricks traffic is inflated relative to the provider's actual metering. ## Cause In `litellm/llms/databricks/chat/transformation.py`: - **Line 643** (non-streaming) works only incidentally: ```python setattr(model_response, "usage", Usage(**completion_response["usage"])) ``` The provider's whole `usage` dict is splatted into `Usage`, so cache keys survive because they happen to be present — not because they are handled. - **Line 665**, `class DatabricksChatResponseIterator(BaseModelResponseIterator)`, has no equivalent. Grepping the entire `litellm/llms/databricks/` tree returns **zero** matches for `cache_creation`, `cache_read`, or `cached_tokens`, whereas `litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py` handles them explicitly. `DatabricksConfig` inherits from `AnthropicConfig` (`class DatabricksConfig(DatabricksBase, OpenAILikeChatConfig, AnthropicConfig)`, line 152), but the streaming response iterator is a separate class that does not inherit Anthropic's usage parsing. ## Expected `DatabricksChatResponseIterator` should extract `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` from streaming chunks and populate `usage.prompt_tokens_details`, matching both the Anthropic provider and the Databricks non-streaming path. ## Impact Spend tracking is wrong for any streaming Databricks request that uses prompt caching — which is every request from an Anthropic-format agent client. Cache-aware pricing (`cache_read_input_token_cost`, `cache_creation_input_token_cost`) is configured on the deployment and applied correctly on the Anthropic provider, but cannot take effect here because the token counts never reach the cost calculator. ## Related Separate bug in the same provider, filed as #36931 — the Databricks request path emits LiteLLM's internal `thinking_blocks` field instead of Databricks' documented `reasoning` content block, breaking multi-turn extended thinking. Independent of this issue.

signals.title: [Bug]: Required PR checks can pass when schema.prisma has no matching migration
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? A pull request can change `schema.prisma` without adding equivalent SQL under `litellm-proxy-extras/litellm_proxy_extras/migrations`, and the required GitHub Actions path can still pass The only test that asks Prisma whether the committed migration history produces the current datamodel is `tests/proxy_migration_tests/test_db_schema_migration.py`. It skips without `DATABASE_URL`, and no GitHub Actions unit job starts Postgres for it The GitHub Actions substitute, `test_aaaaaschema_compatibility`, runs `git show main:schema.prisma` but does not check the command's exit status. The reusable unit workflow uses the default depth-1 checkout, so `main` is normally absent. The missing schema becomes an empty string, the old-model map becomes empty, and the test reports no breaking changes Even with a full `main` ref, the test treats a newly added required field as informational. That is the common failure mode where the generated client expects a column that no migration creates Expected behavior is a required pull-request check that applies all committed migrations to an empty PostgreSQL database and fails when `prisma migrate diff --from-url ... --to-schema-datamodel schema.prisma --exit-code` detects drift ### User Flow Before a fix: a proxy operator upgrades to a release whose generated client expects a column that the shipped migrations never created 1. A maintainer merges a pull request after every required GitHub Actions check passes 2. The operator deploys that release and its migration Job completes because there is no new SQL migration to apply 3. The operator sends `GET https://litellm-domain/key/list` with an admin key 4. The proxy queries through the new generated client and returns a 500 database error because the expected column is missing 5. Requests that touch the affected model continue failing until the operator authors and applies corrective SQL After a fix: the same incomplete schema pull request is blocked before an operator can deploy it 1. A maintainer opens the same pull request with a `schema.prisma` field and no matching SQL migration 2. The required migration-diff job creates an empty PostgreSQL database and applies every committed migration 3. Prisma reports datamodel drift and the pull request check fails 4. The maintainer adds the missing migration and the check passes 5. The operator upgrades and `GET https://litellm-domain/key/list` returns 200 against the migrated schema ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup: ```text GitHub Actions reusable unit workflow: .github/workflows/_test-unit-base.yml Checkout: actions/checkout with no fetch-depth override Migration oracle: tests/proxy_migration_tests/test_db_schema_migration.py ``` Version / commit: ```text v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ``` Deterministic evidence from the current tree: ```python def get_schema_from_branch(branch: str = "main") -> str: result = subprocess.run( ["git", "show", f"{branch}:schema.prisma"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) return result.stdout ``` The caller parses that returned string without checking `result.returncode`. On the depth-1 checkout shape used by the workflow, the audit reproduced: ```shell $ git show main:schema.prisma fatal: invalid object name 'main' $ python -c 'from tests.proxy_unit_tests.test_db_schema_changes import get_schema_from_branch, parse_model_fields; print(repr(get_schema_from_branch("main"))); print(parse_model_fields(get_schema_from_branch("main")))' '' {} ``` The actual migration oracle is explicitly disabled without a database: ```python @pytest.mark.skipif( "DATABASE_URL" not in os.environ, reason="requires a postgres database (DATABASE_URL)", ) ``` The current GitHub Actions workflows do not set `DATABASE_URL` for that test. CircleCI has a PostgreSQL-backed `schema_migration_check`, but it is not the required GitHub Actions pull-request gate This validation did not deploy a live proxy because the defect is in pull-request assurance. The production consequence follows when an incomplete schema change is merged and deployed ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Other ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
