signals.title: [Bug]: Helm upgrade rolls new proxy pods before the migration Job completes
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? The published `helm/litellm-helm` chart defaults `migrationJob.enabled=true` and `migrationJob.hooks.helm.enabled=false`. The Deployment also forces `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true`, so application pods cannot migrate the database themselves On `helm upgrade`, the migration Job is therefore an ordinary resource rather than a pre-upgrade hook. Helm can update the Deployment and start the new image before the Job has completed. The new Prisma client then queries columns introduced by that image while the database still has the previous release's schema The default replica count is one. A normal schema-bearing upgrade can replace the only serving pod with an N+1 binary against an N schema. Readiness can still pass because it does not verify every ORM model column Expected behavior is that schema expansion completes before any N+1 proxy replica starts serving. The componentized `helm/litellm` chart already uses a `pre-install,pre-upgrade` migration hook This is not a duplicate of #7536, which reports an existing non-hook Job not being recreated, or #16190, which reports the migration Job starting before a newly deployed database is reachable ### User Flow Before a fix: a Helm operator gets a Ready N+1 pod while the database still has the N schema 1. The operator runs `helm upgrade litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm --set image.tag=<N+1>` with the chart defaults 2. Kubernetes starts the N+1 Deployment pod with `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true` 3. The migration Job has not completed yet, but `GET https://litellm-domain/health/readiness` returns 200 4. The operator sends `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` or `GET https://litellm-domain/key/list` 5. The request returns a database error for an N+1 column that does not exist yet 6. The same route starts working only after the migration Job finishes, or remains broken if that Job fails After a fix: Helm completes the schema expansion before creating any N+1 proxy pod 1. The operator runs the same `helm upgrade` command with the same image and values 2. Helm runs the migration Job as a blocking pre-upgrade hook 3. The Job applies the N+1 migration and exits successfully 4. Kubernetes then starts the N+1 Deployment pod 5. `GET https://litellm-domain/health/readiness` returns 200 only after the compatible pod is running 6. `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` and `GET https://litellm-domain/key/list` return 200 throughout the serving transition ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup: ```yaml replicaCount: 1 migrationJob: enabled: true hooks: argocd: enabled: true helm: enabled: false ``` Version / commit: ```text v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ``` Current template evidence: ```yaml {{- if .Values.migrationJob.hooks.helm.enabled }} helm.sh/hook: "pre-install,pre-upgrade" helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: "before-hook-creation" {{- end }} ``` The Deployment separately emits: ```yaml {{- if .Values.migrationJob.enabled }} - name: DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE value: "true" {{- end }} ``` With the default values, the Job has no Helm hook annotation and the proxy cannot close the schema gap. The generated Prisma models include additive fields such as `LiteLLM_Config.last_run_at` and `reload_revision`. Querying those fields against the previous schema produces PostgreSQL's `column does not exist` error The audit reproduced the database half of the transition by removing those additive columns from a migrated disposable PostgreSQL database and issuing the N+1 SELECT list: ```sql SELECT "param_name", "param_value", "last_run_at", "reload_revision" FROM "LiteLLM_Config" WHERE "param_name" = 'general_settings'; ``` ```text ERROR: column "last_run_at" does not exist ``` A Kubernetes cluster was not available in this audit, so the Helm ordering itself was confirmed from rendered-resource conditions and Helm's ordinary-resource lifecycle rather than a live `helm upgrade` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: CheckBatchCost can apply completed batch spend more than once
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? The enterprise `CheckBatchCost` poller applies the full cost of a completed managed batch before it writes `batch_processed=true`. The spend side effect and the processed flag are not atomic, the flag update is not compare-and-swap, and the poller has no cross-pod lock If the final managed-object update fails, the next poll selects the same `batch_processed=false` row and bills it again. If two proxy replicas select the row concurrently, both can emit spend before either writes the flag The emitted success callback increments live Redis budget counters and queues SQL increments for key, user, team, organization, end-user, and daily spend. A duplicate spend-log request id does not roll those other increments back Expected behavior is exactly-once accounting for each managed batch, including concurrent pollers and retry after a database timeout ### User Flow Before a fix: a batch user is charged twice when two pollers reconcile the same completed batch 1. The user uploads JSONL with `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files` and receives a managed file id 2. The user creates a batch with `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches` and receives a managed batch id 3. The provider completes the batch once 4. Two proxy replicas poll the still-unprocessed managed row and each records the full batch cost 5. The user opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and sees duplicated or inconsistent batch accounting 6. `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` reports spend increased by up to twice the provider cost 7. A later `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches` can be rejected because the duplicated increment exhausted the user's budget After a fix: only one poller can claim and account for the completed batch 1. The user uploads the same JSONL and creates the same batch 2. The provider completes the batch once 3. Two proxy replicas attempt reconciliation 4. One replica atomically claims the managed row and the other observes that it is already claimed 5. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows one billed batch 6. `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` increases by exactly the provider cost 7. Later batch creation is blocked only when real spend reaches the configured budget ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup: ```yaml general_settings: proxy_batch_polling_interval: 3600 litellm_settings: require_managed_files: true ``` Two or more proxy replicas share the same `DATABASE_URL`. `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_ENABLED` is left at its default enabled value Version / commit: ```text v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ``` Current control-flow order in `enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/common_utils/check_batch_cost.py`: ```python tracked = await self._track_completed_batch_cost(...) processed_models.append(tracked) update_data = { "status": "complete", "file_object": response.model_dump_json(), } update_data["batch_processed"] = True await self.prisma_client.db.litellm_managedobjecttable.update( where={"id": job.id}, data=update_data, ) ``` The update failure is logged and swallowed after the spend callback has run: ```python except Exception as db_err: verbose_proxy_logger.error( f"CheckBatchCost: failed to mark job {job.id} complete in DB: {db_err}" ) ``` The initial read is a normal `find_many` with `batch_processed=False`. There is no `PodLockManager`, processing lease, or conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE batch_processed=false` in this file The audit confirmed the emit line precedes the mark line and that each tracking call creates a new callback context. A live provider batch was not submitted during this audit because that would incur external cost. The race and retry are deterministic from the persisted ordering above ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: Concurrent budget reset jobs erase spend from the new window
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? Every proxy replica schedules `ResetBudgetJob.reset_budget`. The job reads due keys, users, and teams and later performs unconditional updates that set `spend=0` and advance `budget_reset_at` There is no `PodLockManager` lock around the reset tick and no compare-and-swap condition on the old `budget_reset_at`. Two replicas can read the same due row. If replica A resets it, new-window traffic increments spend, and replica B then applies its stale reset, replica B erases the new-window spend from PostgreSQL and zeros the Redis counter Both reset jobs report success. The affected key, user, or team appears to have a full budget even though it has already spent in the new window Expected behavior is that one reset wins per entity and a stale second writer cannot erase spend recorded after that reset ### User Flow Before a fix: a virtual-key user can spend past the new-window budget after two replicas reset the same key 1. The user has a virtual key with a `$10` daily budget and the previous window is due for reset 2. Two proxy replicas start their reset jobs and both read the key as due 3. Replica A commits the reset 4. The user sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and receives 200 for a request costing `$2` 5. Replica B commits its stale `spend=0` update and clears the Redis counter 6. `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` reports `spend: 0` for the new window 7. The user can send another `$10` of requests before receiving a budget rejection, exceeding the intended window by the erased amount After a fix: only one reset can advance the due row and post-reset spend remains visible 1. The user has the same virtual key and due daily budget 2. Two proxy replicas start their reset jobs 3. One replica atomically advances the due row and the second updates zero rows 4. The user sends the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and receives 200 for a `$2` request 5. `GET https://litellm-domain/key/info` reports `spend: 2` 6. A further `$8` reaches the budget, and a request that would exceed `$10` is rejected 7. Another user cannot consume budget headroom created by a stale reset ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup: ```yaml general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` Run at least two proxy replicas with `disable_reset_budget` unset. Give a key, user, or team a `budget_duration` and a due `budget_reset_at` Version / commit: ```text v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ``` Current reset tick: ```python await self.reset_budget_for_litellm_keys() await self.reset_budget_for_litellm_users() await self.reset_budget_for_litellm_teams() await self.reset_budget_for_litellm_budget_table() await self.reset_budget_windows() ``` Current queued writes in `litellm/repositories/unit_of_work.py`: ```python self.table.update( where={"token": token}, data={"spend": 0, "budget_reset_at": budget_reset_at}, ) ``` The user and team writes have the same unconditional shape. There is no lock acquisition in `reset_budget_job.py`, and the write does not require the row to remain due The deterministic database ordering is: ```text A: UPDATE spend=0, budget_reset_at=future request: UPDATE spend = spend + 2 B: UPDATE spend=0, budget_reset_at=future final spend: 0 ``` A live two-pod proxy was not started during this audit. The lost update is the direct result of two unconditional successful writes around an increment ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
signals.author: emerzon

signals.title: [Bug]: budget_limits reset clears Redis before reset_at commits
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? The multi-window budget reset path clears each Redis enforcement counter before it persists the window's new `reset_at` in PostgreSQL `_reset_expired_window` sets the in-memory and Redis counter to `0.0`, mutates the local JSON, and returns. `reset_budget_windows` performs the database update afterwards. If that update fails, the database still says the old window is due while Redis authoritatively reports zero spend The reservation path treats a Redis zero as a warm cache hit, so it does not reconstruct the old window's spend from logs. A fully spent window can receive another full budget. A later reset tick can clear the replacement spend again Expected behavior is commit first, then clear or delete the enforcement counter only for a window whose `reset_at` advance succeeded ### User Flow Before a fix: a key receives a second full budget when the reset database update fails 1. The user has a key with a `budget_limits` window of `$10/day`, has spent `$10`, and its `reset_at` is due 2. The reset job sets `spend:key:<token>:window:1d` to zero 3. The PostgreSQL update of `budget_limits.reset_at` times out, so the stored window is still due 4. The user sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` for a request costing `$1` 5. The proxy reads the warm zero counter, increments it to one, and returns 200 6. The user can spend another `$9` in the same still-due window, exceeding the original limit 7. Another caller using the same key shares that unintended headroom After a fix: a failed reset write leaves the old enforcement counter intact 1. The user has the same fully spent `$10/day` window and due `reset_at` 2. The reset job computes the future `reset_at` but the PostgreSQL update times out 3. Redis remains at `10`, or the missing counter is reconstructed from spend logs for the old window 4. The user sends the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` 5. The proxy rejects the request because the old window is still exhausted 6. After a later successful database update, Redis is cleared for the new window 7. The user can spend up to `$10` in that new window and no more ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup: ```yaml general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` Create a key or team whose `budget_limits` JSON contains a due window and whose corresponding Redis counter is already at its maximum Version / commit: ```text v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ``` Current order in `_reset_expired_window`: ```python spend_counter_cache.in_memory_cache.set_cache(key=counter_key, value=0.0) if spend_counter_cache.redis_cache is not None: await spend_counter_cache.redis_cache.async_set_cache( key=counter_key, value=0.0, ) window["reset_at"] = compute_budget_reset_at(...).isoformat() return True ``` Only after that helper returns does `reset_budget_windows` call: ```python await VerificationTokenRepository(self.prisma_client).table.update( where={"token": row["token"]}, data={"budget_limits": windows}, ) ``` The same class documents the required opposite order for ordinary key, user, and team spend counters: clear Redis only after the database write commits The audit confirmed Redis is set before the database update and that a value of `0.0` is considered a warm cache hit. A live failure injection against PostgreSQL was not run, but raising from the later update leaves the already-written Redis zero with no compensating action ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: SSO and JWT email matching can take over an existing proxy admin
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? When an SSO or JWT subject does not match an existing `user_id` or `sso_user_id`, LiteLLM falls back to a case-insensitive email lookup. A matching row is returned even if it already has a different `sso_user_id`, and LiteLLM schedules an update that overwrites that id with the new subject The SSO path then inherits the matched row's stored role when the identity provider did not supply a LiteLLM role. The JWT path checks the matched row's role directly. A different identity-provider subject that can present an existing privileged email can therefore inherit `PROXY_ADMIN` and durably rebind the victim's `sso_user_id` There is no shared requirement that the email claim is verified, no refusal when the row already has a different SSO subject, and no protection for administrative roles Expected behavior is that email linking is allowed only for a verified email on an explicitly unlinked or invited row. A row already bound to another subject, especially a proxy admin, must not be silently rebound ### User Flow Before a fix: a second identity-provider subject can become an existing proxy admin by presenting the same email 1. An administrator already has a LiteLLM dashboard account bound to SSO subject `admin-subject` 2. A different trusted identity-provider subject authenticates at `GET https://litellm-domain/sso/callback` with the administrator's email in its claims 3. LiteLLM misses by the new subject, finds the administrator row by email, and overwrites its `sso_user_id` 4. The new subject is redirected into `https://litellm-domain/ui/` with the stored `proxy_admin` role 5. The new subject can call `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate` and other administrator routes 6. The original administrator can be locked out because their row is now bound to the different subject 7. The attacker can access other users' keys and management data that their original identity should never reach After a fix: a subject mismatch cannot silently link to a privileged or already-bound row 1. The same administrator account remains bound to `admin-subject` 2. The different identity-provider subject authenticates with the same email claim 3. LiteLLM detects that the row is already bound to another subject, or that the email is not verified 4. `GET https://litellm-domain/sso/callback` returns a 403 or creates a separate non-admin user according to policy 5. The new subject cannot call `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate` 6. The original administrator remains able to sign in with `admin-subject` 7. The second subject cannot read or modify any other user's management objects ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup: ```yaml general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` Enable Generic OIDC, SAML, or JWT auth. Existing database row: ```json { "user_id": "admin-user", "user_email": "admin@example.test", "sso_user_id": "admin-subject", "user_role": "proxy_admin" } ``` Version / commit: ```text v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ``` Current shared fuzzy-link code: ```python if response is None and user_email is not None: response = await user_table.find_first( where={"user_email": {"equals": user_email, "mode": "insensitive"}}, include={"organization_memberships": True}, ) if response is not None and sso_user_id is not None: asyncio.create_task( user_table.update( where={"user_id": response.user_id}, data={"sso_user_id": sso_user_id}, ) ) ``` The repository's existing test encodes the unsafe rebinding contract. It starts with a row whose SSO id is `sso_123`, looks it up by email for `new_sso_456`, and expects the update to the new id Audit command and output: ```shell $ uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_auth_checks.py::test_get_fuzzy_user_object ============================== 1 passed ============================== ``` The current SSO role resolution uses the database role when the SSO response does not supply a LiteLLM role. The JWT auth builder also calls `get_user_object` with the presented subject and email, then treats a returned `PROXY_ADMIN` row as admin A live third-party identity provider was not used because reproducing against a real account would modify authentication state. The test and source path confirm the email match, subject overwrite, and role inheritance without external side effects ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: check_provider_endpoint: true in config.yaml has no effect when STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Setting `check_provider_endpoint: true` in `config.yaml` under `litellm_settings` has no effect on `/v1/models` wildcard expansion when `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`. Observed with `vertex_ai/*` — a provider explicitly listed as supported for model discovery in the [docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/model_discovery). The setting works correctly without `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB` (no Postgres). With it enabled, the DB-stored `litellm_settings` row (written via the Admin UI or `/config/update`) silently takes precedence over `config.yaml`, and that row typically lacks `check_provider_endpoint` entirely — causing the runtime flag to remain at its default (`False`). This is the same class of bug as #36533 (`max_budget` not applied from DB-stored config). The proxy's `_update_config_fields()` only applies `litellm_settings` keys listed in `LITELLM_SETTINGS_SAFE_DB_OVERRIDES` (`litellm/constants.py`). `check_provider_endpoint` is not on that allowlist, so even when `config.yaml` correctly sets it at initial startup, the value is effectively lost during the DB-overlay merge lifecycle. Additionally, `VertexAIModelInfo.get_models()` (in `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py`) is a bare `raise NotImplementedError("Vertex AI models are not supported yet")` stub — so even if the config flag propagated correctly, Vertex AI discovery would still silently fail (the exception is caught and swallowed by `_get_valid_models_from_provider_api`). The [Model Discovery docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/model_discovery) list Vertex AI as a supported provider without noting this limitation. ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a proxy admin enabling model discovery with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True` sees only the literal wildcard 1. Admin writes `config.yaml` with `litellm_settings.check_provider_endpoint: true` and a `model_list` entry for `vertex_ai/*` with valid Vertex AI credentials 2. Admin starts the proxy with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True` and a Postgres database 3. Admin sends `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` with their master key 4. Response contains only `{"id": "vertex_ai/*"}` — no real Vertex AI models are listed 5. Admin checks DB: `SELECT param_value FROM "LiteLLM_Config" WHERE param_name = 'litellm_settings';` shows `{"drop_params": true}` — no `check_provider_endpoint` key 6. Admin removes `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True` and restarts without a database — still no Vertex AI models discovered (second bug: the `get_models()` stub) After a (hypothetical) fix: the config setting takes effect and models are discovered 1. Same `config.yaml`, same `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`, same Postgres database 2. `check_provider_endpoint: true` persists into the runtime regardless of what the DB-stored `litellm_settings` row contains 3. Admin sends `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` with their master key 4. Response contains real models discovered from the configured provider ### Proof the bug occurs **Config:** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: vertex_ai/* litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/* vertex_project: my-gcp-project vertex_location: us-central1 litellm_settings: check_provider_endpoint: true ``` **Version:** v1.98.0 (commit `423b791ee`, `litellm_internal_staging` branch) **Bug 1 — config flag not propagated with STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True:** DB-backed proxy with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`: ```bash $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" http://localhost:4000/v1/models | jq '.data[].id | select(startswith("vertex"))' "vertex_ai/*" # Only the literal wildcard — flag not in effect ``` Verified the runtime value from inside the running container: ```python import litellm print(litellm.check_provider_endpoint) # False — should be True ``` DB row confirms the key is absent: ```sql SELECT param_value FROM "LiteLLM_Config" WHERE param_name = 'litellm_settings'; -- {"drop_params": true, "cost_discount_config": {"vertex_ai": 0.05}} -- No check_provider_endpoint key ``` **Bug 2 — VertexAIModelInfo.get_models() is a stub:** ```python from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.common_utils import VertexAIModelInfo VertexAIModelInfo().get_models() # NotImplementedError: Vertex AI models are not supported yet ``` ```python from litellm.utils import get_valid_models result = get_valid_models(check_provider_endpoint=True, custom_llm_provider="vertex_ai") # WARNING: Error getting valid models: Vertex AI models are not supported yet # result = [] ``` ### Related issues - #36533 — same root cause for config propagation (DB-stored `litellm_settings` not applied), different key (`max_budget`) ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.98.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details N/A
signals.author: NewtonChutney

signals.title: [Feature]: Auto-detect context window (max_input_tokens) for LM Studio models from its native metadata API
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature For self-hosted/local providers that expose their own richer model-metadata API (LM Studio's `/api/v0/models` and `/api/v1/models`, both distinct from the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models` LiteLLM currently calls for discovery), LiteLLM never queries or surfaces the provider's own `max_context_length` into a model's `model_info.max_input_tokens`. This affects every LM Studio model regardless of how it's added to LiteLLM — a manually written `model_list` entry, a model added via the Admin UI, or (once supported) a discovered wildcard model — because context window info for any model not in LiteLLM's built-in static cost map (`model_prices_and_context_window.json`) is simply never populated from anywhere. Since LM Studio models are arbitrary user-loaded local models, they can never be in that static map. Concretely: LiteLLM's provider-discovery interface (`BaseLLMModelInfo.get_models()`) is `list[str]` — model IDs only, no channel for per-model metadata like context length even for providers that do query a richer endpoint. Fixing this requires both (a) querying an endpoint that has the data, and (b) a place in the model-info population path to put it. ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a proxy admin adding an LM Studio model gets no context window info, and has no way to keep it in sync when they swap models locally 1. Admin adds `qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b` as a LiteLLM model pointing at their LM Studio server, either via `model_list` in `config.yaml` or the Admin UI "Add Model" form 2. They call `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/model/info` with their key 3. The model's entry shows `"max_input_tokens": null, "max_output_tokens": null` — LiteLLM has no idea the model supports a 262144-token context 4. Their workaround is to open LM Studio's own UI (or call its native API directly), read the context length off there, and hand-type it into `model_info.max_input_tokens` in their config — and remember to update it by hand every time they swap the loaded model or LM Studio changes the context settings After this feature (ideal user flow): LiteLLM reflects the real context window LM Studio reports, with no manual step 1. Admin adds the same model the same way, with no extra config 2. They call `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/model/info` 3. The model's entry shows `"max_input_tokens": 262144` — LiteLLM asked LM Studio directly and used the real value 4. If they swap the loaded model in LM Studio for one with a different context size, the next model-info refresh reflects the new value with no manual edit ### How far you got Config the proxy ran with (`config.yaml`, static entry, no discovery, no wildcards — deliberately using only currently-shipped LiteLLM behavior): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: qwen3.6-35b-a3b litellm_params: model: lm_studio/qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b api_base: http://<lm-studio-host>:1234/v1 api_key: os.environ/LM_STUDIO_KEY ``` Version: v1.96.2 (`docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm-database:latest`) Commands and full output: ```bash $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" http://localhost:4000/v1/model/info | jq '.data[] | select(.model_name == "qwen3.6-35b-a3b") | .model_info | {max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens}' { "max_input_tokens": null, "max_output_tokens": null } ``` Meanwhile, calling LM Studio's own native API for the exact same model, at the same moment, shows the real answer LiteLLM never asked for: ```bash $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LM_STUDIO_KEY" http://<lm-studio-host>:1234/api/v0/models | jq '.data[] | select(.id == "qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b")' { "id": "qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b", "object": "model", "type": "vlm", "publisher": "qwen", "arch": "qwen3_5_moe", "compatibility_type": "mlx", "quantization": "4bit", "state": "loaded", "max_context_length": 262144, "loaded_context_length": 34560, "capabilities": ["tool_use"] } ``` LM Studio also exposes an even richer, newer native endpoint (`/api/v1/models`, distinct response shape — `{"models": [...]}` not `{"data": [...]}`) with the same `max_context_length` field plus `loaded_instances`, structured `quantization`, and `capabilities`: ```bash $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LM_STUDIO_KEY" http://<lm-studio-host>:1234/api/v1/models | jq '.models[] | select(.key == "qwen3.6-35b-unsloth-code-reasoning-deepseek-v4-pro-destilled-mlx")' { "type": "llm", "publisher": "10Hen10", "key": "qwen3.6-35b-unsloth-code-reasoning-deepseek-v4-pro-destilled-mlx", "architecture": "qwen3_5_moe", "quantization": {"name": "4bit", "bits_per_weight": 4}, "max_context_length": 262144, "format": "mlx", "capabilities": {"vision": false, "trained_for_tool_use": true} } ``` What stopped me there: LiteLLM has no config option, discovery mechanism, or background refresh that queries either of LM Studio's native endpoints for `max_context_length`, and the discovery interface it does have for other providers (`BaseLLMModelInfo.get_models() -> list[str]`) has no field to carry per-model metadata even if it did. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details N/A

signals.title: [Feature]: Publish floating minor-version Docker tags for patch-only updates (e.g. 1.89 → latest 1.89.x)
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature ## Summary Please publish and maintain floating minor-version tags for the official LiteLLM Docker images, so operators can follow patch releases within a chosen minor release without automatically crossing into the next minor release. For example: - `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89.5` → immutable/exact release - `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89` → floating tag pointing to the latest published `1.89.x` - `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.90` → floating tag pointing to the latest published `1.90.x` The same convention could be applied to the corresponding official database image where appropriate. ## Current behavior LiteLLM publishes exact release tags, but a minor-family tag such as: ```yaml services: litellm: image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89 ``` is not consistently available. Docker/OCI registries do not perform semantic-version resolution themselves. Therefore an operator currently has to choose between: 1. pinning an exact patch version such as 1.89.5 and manually discovering/updating every patch release; or 2. following a broader moving channel such as main-stable, which can eventually move the deployment across minor releases. I would like the middle option: follow maintenance releases automatically while deliberately holding the feature/minor release line. ## Desired behavior When a patch release is published, for example: ``` v 1.89.6 ``` the release workflow would also update this docker compose: ``` image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89 ``` to point to the newest release in the 1.89.x family. Publishing 1.90.0 would create/update 1.90, but would NOT change 1.89. ## Conceptually: ``` 1.89.5 ─┐ 1.89.6 ├─ exact release tags 1.89.7 ─┘ 1.89 → 1.89.7 1.90.0 ─┐ 1.90.1 ├─ exact release tags 1.90.2 ─┘ 1.90 → 1.90.2 ``` Existing exact tags would remain available for operators requiring fully reproducible deployments. ## Example Docker Compose use case An operator who deliberately wants to remain on the 1.89 release line could use: ```yaml services: litellm: image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89 ``` Then: ```bash docker compose pull docker compose up -d ``` could consume a newly published 1.89.x maintenance release, but would never silently upgrade the deployment to 1.90.x. Operators requiring immutable deployments could continue using: ```yaml image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89.5 ``` ## Scope This request is specifically for publisher-maintained OCI/Docker tags. (It is NOT a request for Docker Compose to interpret semantic-version ranges; as t.m.k. Docker does not provide that behavior for image tags.) ### User Flow LiteLLM is infrastructure, and there is a useful operational distinction between accepting patch/maintenance updates and accepting a new minor release. For a long-running LiteLLM Proxy deployment, I want to: - receive maintenance and security fixes within a tested release line; - avoid unnecessarily lagging behind on patch releases; - deliberately review release notes before crossing a minor-version boundary; - retain an easy rollback path; - avoid depending on a broad moving tag that may introduce new functionality or behavioral changes. This is particularly useful for self-hosted and production-style Docker Compose deployments where LiteLLM sits between persistent clients and several providers. For example, my deployment uses LiteLLM as a central gateway for OpenWebUI and other clients, with PostgreSQL persistence and multiple upstream providers. A regression in provider behavior or database handling can affect all clients simultaneously. I therefore deliberately hold a known-good minor release line while still wanting maintenance fixes from that line. Other container projects use floating minor tags successfully for this operational model. The desired contract is simple: `1.89` = latest supported `1.89.x` while: `1.89.5` = exact release This would complement rather than replace LiteLLM's existing exact and stable release channels. If floating minor tags are intentionally not provided for release-engineering, reproducibility, or security reasons, documenting that policy and the recommended mechanism for tracking patch-only updates would also be valuable. ### How far you got using docker compose, ```yaml litellm: image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89 ``` will fail to pull the latest subversion (1.89.5 right now) within the 1.89 minor version. Only pinning the subversion will pull an image: ```yaml litellm: image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:1.89.5 ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? _No response_ ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url doesn't dedup trailing /v1 in api_base (yields /v1/v1/messages), unlike openai_like/deepseek siblings
signals.text: ### What happened `AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` appends `/v1/messages` to a custom `api_base` without deduplicating a trailing `/v1`: ```python # litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/transformation.py (~line 227) api_base = AnthropicModelInfo.get_api_base(api_base) or "https://api.anthropic.com" if not api_base.endswith("/v1/messages"): api_base = f"{api_base}/v1/messages" ``` So a deployment resolving to `custom_llm_provider: anthropic` with `api_base: https://host/v1` produces `https://host/v1/v1/messages`, which 404s at the provider. Every sibling Anthropic-messages config already handles this: - `OpenAILikeAnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` (`litellm/llms/openai_like/messages/transformation.py`) does `rstrip("/")` → return if endswith `/v1/messages` → `removesuffix("/v1")` → append, with test coverage in `tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/messages/test_openai_like_anthropic_messages_transformation.py` asserting `https://host/v1 → https://host/v1/messages`. - `DeepSeek`'s messages config (`litellm/llms/deepseek/messages/transformation.py`) has the same normalization. Only the Anthropic config lacks it. Users hit this when pointing an `anthropic/`-prefixed model at an Anthropic-compatible gateway whose base already ends in `/v1` — see discussion #36651 for a real-world report (Claude Code → LiteLLM → Groq/NIM, where a misconfigured entry surfaces exactly this shape). ### Expected behavior `api_base: https://host/v1` should yield `https://host/v1/messages`, consistent with the openai_like and deepseek configs. ### Proposed fix Mirror the openai_like normalization in `AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` (two lines), plus parametrized tests matching the openai_like test table. PR incoming.

signals.text: Hi — I run GoAnyAPI and would be interested in contributing an optional provider integration for SEO data workflows. GoAnyAPI offers pay-as-you-go APIs for SERP, keyword difficulty, keyword generation, backlink overview and top links, domain rating, traffic, AdSense relationship lookup, and Google Ads Transparency. The intended behavior would be provider selection only for compatible operations; existing providers such as DataForSEO would remain available for broader datasets. For LiteLLM, a useful first scope may be an optional tool/provider adapter that agents can call for SERP, keyword, backlink, and ad-transparency analysis. signals.title: fix: allow vllm GET passthrough by checking model in query params
signals.text: ## Description This PR enables correct routing for GET requests to the \/vllm/*\ passthrough endpoints (e.g., \/vllm/metrics\). ## Problem Previously, \ llm_proxy_route\ relied on \is_passthrough_request_using_router_model\ which only checked the request body for a \model\ field. Since LiteLLM's \get_request_body\ ignores bodies for GET requests, these requests would always fail to identify a router model and fall back to using \VLLM_API_BASE\. If \VITELLM_API_BASE\ was not set, the request would fail with a 500 error even if a valid model was provided in query parameters. ## Changes - Updated \is_passthrough_request_using_router_model\ to optionally check query parameters if the model is not found in the body. - Updated \ llm_proxy_route\ to pass query parameters to the check and use the resolved model name for routing. ## Verification Created a reproduction script that: 1. Starts a LiteLLM proxy with a vLLM model. 2. Calls \GET /vllm/metrics?model=my-vllm\. 3. Verified that the request is correctly routed to the vLLM server and returns 200 OK. Fixes #22101

signals.title: Cache Azure token providers
signals.text: Previously, get_azure_ad_token_from_{entra_id,username_password} constructed a new credential and called get_bearer_token_provider on every invocation, returning a new provider callable every time (and unnecessary overhead, since the new callable would generate new credentials when used). signals.title: fix(s3_v2): URL-encode object keys to prevent SigV4 signature mismatch
signals.text: S3 object keys containing special characters like '=' (from base64 padding in Responses API composite IDs) caused 403 Invalid signature errors on S3-compatible endpoints (Garage, MinIO). botocore's SigV4Auth URL-encodes the path in the canonical request (turning '=' into '%3D'), but httpx sends the literal '=' on the wire. The server computes its signature using the unencoded path, causing a mismatch. Fix: apply urllib.parse.quote() to the object key before embedding it in the URL, so both the SigV4 signature and the HTTP request agree on the path encoding. ## Relevant issues Fixes https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/24583 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [X] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [X] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [X] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? signals.title: [WIP] fix(mcp): do not prefix tool names when listing via scoped /mcp/{server_name} endpoint for stdio servers (#22670)
signals.text: Fixes #22670 ## Summary When an MCP `list_tools` request arrives via the URL-scoped path `/mcp/{server_name}` the client has already disambiguated the server by the URL. In that case the returned tool names should **not** be prefixed with the server name. Today LiteLLM prefixes them unconditionally regardless of transport, so a stdio-backed server named `github_onprem` returns tools like `github_onprem-get_repo` instead of `get_repo` even when the caller explicitly scoped the request to that server. The issue reporter (NetApp) uses the following config: ```yaml github_onprem: command: /usr/local/bin/github-mcp-server transport: "stdio" ``` and observed prefixed names from `/mcp/github_onprem`, while other servers behaved as expected. ## Scoped vs aggregated distinction - `/mcp` (aggregated) — tools **remain prefixed** with the server name. This keeps names globally unique when tools from many servers are merged. - `/mcp/{server_name}` (scoped) — tools are returned **without** the server-name prefix, because the URL path already picks the server. The existing tool-call path already resolves both prefixed and unprefixed tool names (`server.py:2020-2027` and `_create_prefixed_tools` registers both forms in the mapping), so no changes are needed there. ## Implementation - Add a transport-agnostic ContextVar `_mcp_request_scoped_to_single_server` in `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_context.py`. - Set the flag in `extract_mcp_auth_context` whenever the request path resolves to exactly one server (`/mcp/{server_name}` and the `/{server_name}/mcp` alias). - Honour the flag in all four list-fetch sites in `server.py` so stdio, SSE and HTTP-streamable MCP servers behave consistently: - tools (`_fetch_and_filter_server_tools`) - prompts (`_get_prompts_from_mcp_servers`) - resources (`_get_resources_from_mcp_servers`) - resource templates (`_get_resource_templates_from_mcp_servers`) The change is surgical: it only swaps `add_prefix=True` → a value that reads the ContextVar. The ContextVar defaults to `False` so any non-scoped code path (including all existing unit tests that call `_get_tools_from_mcp_servers` directly) continues to prefix as before. ## Tests - Added `test_list_tools_scoped_via_url_path_does_not_prefix_stdio_server` in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_mcp_server.py` — it models the reporter's stdio `github_onprem` server, sets the scoped ContextVar, and asserts the returned tool name is `get_repo` (not `github_onprem-get_repo`). - All existing MCP unit tests still pass (518 passed after the change, excluding one unrelated failure due to a missing optional `semantic_router` dependency). ## Files changed - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_context.py` — new ContextVar. - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py` — set ContextVar for scoped path requests and honour it when fetching tools/prompts/resources. - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_mcp_server.py` — regression test.

signals.title: Fix qdrant semantic cache
signals.text: ## Relevant issues fix(caching): handle list-based responses and message key variations in QdrantSemanticCache When the semantic cache attempted to store or retrieve responses that were structured as lists (e.g., list-based content), the system encountered a `TypeError` during the caching process, resulting in the following error: `LiteLLM: ERROR: caching.py:647 - LiteLLM Cache: Exception add_cache: can only concatenate str (not "list") to str` Additionally, some callers were passing the prompt content using a singular 'message' key instead of the expected plural 'messages' key, leading to further inconsistencies. Finally, the use of `str(value)` for serialization generated Python-specific representations (single quotes) incompatible with standard JSON parsing, forcing a reliance on fragile `ast.literal_eval` fallbacks. - Updated `QdrantSemanticCache` to ensure list-type responses are correctly serialized to JSON strings using `json.dumps` before storage, ensuring consistent retrieval. - Modified input handling in cache methods to support both 'messages' and 'message' keys, ensuring robustness against varying input structures. - Added comprehensive unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/caching/test_qdrant_semantic_cache.py` to validate list-type response caching and confirm the fix for the reported concatenation and serialization errors. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix

signals.title: fix(proxy): handle client-side unique-ID suffixes in MCP semantic tool filter
signals.text: ## Problem MCP clients like LibreChat append a unique-ID suffix to tool names (e.g. `fc_web_search-firecrawl_scrape_a1b2c3d4`) to avoid naming collisions across multiple connected MCP servers. The `_name_matches_canonical` method in `SemanticMCPToolFilter` only handled the **prefix** case (`<alias><sep><canonical>`) introduced in #26117. The symmetric **suffix** case (`<canonical><sep><uid>`) fell through all existing checks, causing the filter to drop every tool and forward `tools: []` with `tool_choice: auto`, which strict upstream providers reject with a 400 error. **Concrete example from the issue:** | form | value | |---|---| | MCP registry canonical (proxy side) | `fc_web_search-firecrawl_scrape` | | Incoming `tools[].name` from LibreChat | `fc_web_search-firecrawl_scrape_a1b2c3d4` | | Router top-k match returns | `fc_web_search-firecrawl_scrape` | | `_name_matches_canonical` result | `False` — `endswith(canonical)` is `False` because the name ends in `_a1b2c3d4` | | `_get_tools_by_names` result | `[]` | ## Root Cause `_name_matches_canonical` only checked if `client_name.endswith(canonical)` (prefix case). It never checked if `client_name.startswith(canonical)` followed by a separator (suffix case). ## Solution Add a symmetric suffix-matching branch to `_name_matches_canonical`: - If `client_name.startswith(canonical)`, check that the remainder is a single `<sep><unique_id>` segment - The remainder after the separator must contain no `MCP_TOOL_PREFIX_SEPARATOR`, preventing `svc-search-extra_tool` from falsely matching canonical `svc-search` - Both `_` and `-` are accepted as separators (same as the prefix case) - The existing `MCP_TOOL_PREFIX_SEPARATOR in canonical` guard still applies — unprefixed canonicals won't trigger suffix matching ## Testing Added 7 new test cases to `TestGetToolsByNames`: - `test_client_suffix_with_underscore_separator` — LibreChat pattern - `test_client_suffix_with_dash_separator` — dash variant - `test_suffix_does_not_match_another_namespaced_tool` — prevents false positives - `test_suffix_without_separator_in_canonical_does_not_match` — safety guard - `test_exact_match_preferred_over_suffixed` — exact match wins - `test_prefix_and_suffix_both_match_same_canonical` — both patterns resolve - `test_name_matches_canonical_suffix_static` — direct static-method tests All existing prefix-match tests continue to pass unchanged. ## Does not break - The fix is purely additive — a new `if` branch after the existing prefix check - No changes to `_get_tools_by_names`, `filter_tools`, or any other method - The suffix-match guard (`MCP_TOOL_PREFIX_SEPARATOR not in rest`) is strictly more conservative than the prefix-match guard — it rejects remainders that look like another namespaced tool Fixes #26507

signals.title: fix(deepseek): DeepSeek V4 support - model registry, multi-turn thinking fix, no-prefix routing
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/26395 ## Changes **Model registry** (`model_prices_and_context_window.json` + backup): - Add `deepseek-v4-flash` — $0.14/1M input, $0.28/1M output, 1M ctx, 384K output, supports reasoning/tools/caching - Add `deepseek-v4-pro` — $0.435/1M input, $0.87/1M output, same capabilities - Both added with and without the `deepseek/` prefix entry **Multi-turn thinking mode fix** (`litellm/llms/deepseek/chat/transformation.py`): - DeepSeek V4 in thinking mode returns `reasoning_content` on assistant messages and requires it to be passed back on every turn - `Message.__init__` drops the field when `None`, causing HTTP 400 "reasoning_content must be passed back" - Fix: `_ensure_reasoning_content_on_assistant_messages()` injects `reasoning_content: ""` on assistant messages that are missing it, **guarded to thinking-mode conversations only** — it first checks if any prior assistant message has `reasoning_content` (i.e. DeepSeek already returned it on a prior turn). If none do, the conversation is not in thinking mode and the messages are left untouched. This avoids polluting payloads for regular `deepseek-chat`/`deepseek-reasoner` calls. **Provider routing** (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/get_llm_provider_logic.py`): - Add `elif model in litellm.deepseek_models:` so `deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro` resolve without needing the `deepseek/` prefix ## Validation evidence Full report with screenshots: https://gist.github.com/ishaan-berri/80d84bb15be22ec90589add7c96a2323 **Multi-turn live test against DeepSeek API:** ``` === TURN 1: User asks about weather === Tool call: get_weather reasoning_content value: 'The user wants to know the weather in Tokyo. I hav...' === TURN 2: Follow-up (tests multi-turn fix) === SUCCESS: The weather in Tokyo is **Sunny** with a temperature of **28 degrees C**. HTTP 400 'reasoning_content must be passed back' = NOT TRIGGERED ``` **Provider routing:** ``` deepseek-v4-flash in deepseek_models: True deepseek-v4-pro in deepseek_models: True deepseek-v4-flash -> provider=deepseek deepseek-v4-pro -> provider=deepseek ``` **Unit tests: 18/18 pass** (added 2 new tests for the guarded injection behavior) ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] Added test in `tests/litellm/` - [x] `make test-unit` passes - [x] No breaking changes to existing model entries - [x] Live API validation: multi-turn tool+thinking works end-to-end ## Type - Bug fix - New feature (model registry entries)

signals.title: feat(proxy): proactive model deprecation alerts and `/model/deprecations` endpoint
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Provider sunset dates ship in the registry but stay invisible - Operators find out a model died when calls fail - No lead time to test and migrate replacements How it solves it: - New `GET /model/deprecations` buckets configured models by urgency - Daily Slack alert lists deprecated and imminent models - Per deployment `model_info.deprecation_date` overrides the registry ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin running a fleet of deployments has no way to see which of them a provider is about to sunset 1. They hit GET http://localhost:4000/model/info with the master key and read back pricing, context windows, and modes 2. The payload carries no provider sunset dates, only whatever they typed into `model_info` themselves, so they keep routing traffic to a dying model 3. The provider retires it and their app starts getting hard failures on POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with no prior warning After: the same admin gets the sunset dates up front, and Slack nags them daily while there is still time to migrate 1. They hit GET http://localhost:4000/model/deprecations with the master key 2. They get back three lists, `deprecated`, `imminent`, and `upcoming`, each entry naming the model as they configured it, the date, days remaining, and the provider 3. They re-bucket without touching config by hitting GET http://localhost:4000/v1/model/deprecations?warn_within_days=90, which pulls anything sunsetting inside 90 days into `imminent` 4. With Slack alerting turned on they also get a daily message titled "Model Deprecation Warning" listing the deprecated and imminent models, at High severity once any date has passed 5. For a model whose sunset date is not in the registry yet, they set `deprecation_date` under `model_info` on that deployment and it shows up in the same lists ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2701 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The user flow above was QA'd before and after on a live proxy, recorded and posted in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0B302ZJU05/p1786400555199479?thread_ts=1786400555.199479&cid=C0B302ZJU05). The before half runs `litellm_internal_staging` at 19c914066b, where `/model/deprecations` 404s and `/model/info` carries no registry sunset dates, and the after half runs 4e7e2f53b9 off the same config. Per step screenshots are in a comment below Captured at 8f1aea5e0a (the endpoint is unchanged since) against a live proxy with five deployments: `claude-opus-4-1` (registry date already passed), `gemini/imagen-4.0-generate-001` (7 days out), `openai/sora-2` (45 days out), an Azure deployment whose `base_model` carries no date, and one deployment with a hand set `model_info.deprecation_date` ```shell $ curl -s -X GET "http://localhost:4000/model/deprecations" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" { "deprecated": [ { "model_name": "opus-4-1", "litellm_model": "claude-opus-4-1", "deprecation_date": "2026-08-05", "days_until_deprecation": -5, "status": "deprecated", "litellm_provider": "anthropic" } ], "imminent": [ { "model_name": "imagen-4", "litellm_model": "gemini/imagen-4.0-generate-001", "deprecation_date": "2026-08-17", "days_until_deprecation": 7, "status": "imminent", "litellm_provider": "gemini" }, { "model_name": "internal-legacy", "litellm_model": "openai/gpt-4o", "deprecation_date": "2026-08-20", "days_until_deprecation": 10, "status": "imminent", "litellm_provider": null } ], "upcoming": [ { "model_name": "sora-2", "litellm_model": "openai/sora-2", "deprecation_date": "2026-09-24", "days_until_deprecation": 45, "status": "upcoming", "litellm_provider": "openai" } ], "warn_within_days": 30, "checked_at": "2026-08-10T23:01:31.944560Z" } ``` `internal-legacy` is the override case: the registry has no date for `openai/gpt-4o`, the date comes from `model_info.deprecation_date` on that deployment. The Azure deployment is correctly absent because neither its `base_model` nor its model string carries a date Widening the window moves `sora-2` from `upcoming` into `imminent`, no restart needed ```shell $ curl -s "http://localhost:4000/v1/model/deprecations?warn_within_days=90" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"deprecated": ["opus-4-1"], "imminent": ["imagen-4", "internal-legacy", "sora-2"], "upcoming": [], "warn_within_days": 90, "checked_at": "2026-08-10T23:01:40.790791Z"} ``` Auth is enforced the same way as the rest of the model management routes ```shell $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" "http://localhost:4000/model/deprecations" 401 ``` Bugbot's startup race concern (the daily loop can start from config load before the router exists, then skip the boot-time alert and silently sleep a full day) was QA'd live with a tiny local HTTP sink standing in for the Slack webhook and a config containing one already-deprecated model. On the before leg at 4e7e2f53b9 the boot-time alert still arrived seconds after startup: on a stock config nothing between the loop starting and the router being assigned truly yields the event loop, so the race needs an unusual config that actually suspends in that window. The fix is still worth having as deterministic hardening, and after it at 2278118493 the loop polls for the router every 30 seconds instead of reading it once, with the boot-time alert reaching the webhook 3 seconds after the proxy reported healthy ```shell $ python3 sink.py 41735 & $ SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=http://127.0.0.1:41735/webhook litellm --config qa_deprecation_config.yaml --port 41733 & $ until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:41733/health/liveliness; do sleep 2; done; date +%H:%M:%S 08:35:00 $ cat sink_head.log 2026-08-12T08:35:03 POST /webhook {"text": "Alert type: `model_deprecation_warnings`
Level: `High`
...
Message: *Model Deprecation Warning*

*Already deprecated:*
• `dead-alias` (provider: unknown, deprecates 2020-01-01, already deprecated 2415d ago)

Plan migrations to a supported model. ..."} ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Coverage is only as good as the registry dates - Slack alert fires daily, enabled by default with alerting on - Deployments sharing a model group and date report once - Alert loop re-reads router and alert types every pass - First alert waits for the router in 30 second polls Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/680cda1b74c34159899de6c6ae064ef6 Requested by: @mateo-berri <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 4e7e2f53b98f5737e43a27c5137e9ad6567c71ac. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: Fix Prometheus remaining rate limit metrics
signals.text: ## Summary Prometheus virtual-key remaining request/token gauges only read metadata keys, while the proxy rate limiter writes the per-key model values into hidden response headers. This adds a fallback that reads `x-ratelimit-model_per_key-remaining-requests` and `x-ratelimit-model_per_key-remaining-tokens` from `hidden_params.additional_headers`, preserving existing metadata behavior and zero values. ## Repro Call the Prometheus success logging path with a model group in metadata, no `litellm-key-remaining-*` metadata values, and hidden additional headers containing per-key remaining request/token counts. Before the fix, the gauges fall back to the sentinel value instead of the header values. ## Evidence Terminal transcript: ```text $ pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_prometheus_custom_metadata_label_counts.py -vv 5 passed in 0.15s ``` ## Tests - Added regression tests in `tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_prometheus_custom_metadata_label_counts.py` for header-sourced remaining request/token values and zero-value preservation. - Confirmed the new tests fail before the code change and pass after it. - `pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_prometheus_custom_metadata_label_counts.py -vv` - passed. - `pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations --tb=short -vv -n 2 --durations=20` - 871 passed, 1 skipped, 1 unrelated live-provider authentication failure in `websearch_interception/test_websearch_chat_completion.py`. - `uv lock --check` - passed. - `black --check --exclude '/enterprise/' .` from `litellm/` - passed. - `ruff check .` from `litellm/` - passed. - `mypy .` from `litellm/` - passed. - Circular import check - passed. - Import safety check - passed. - Hardcoded secret scan unit test - passed. ## CI - Pull-request workflow runs: all registered PR-event checks passed, including linting, integrations, proxy/API groups, MCP, UI build, Semgrep, and code quality checks. - Push workflow runs: security and proxy DB checks passed; caching workflow reported a startup failure before creating jobs and appears unrelated to this code path. ## Review - No automated Greptile review was posted after polling the PR reviews/comments; no actionable review threads were available to address. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Changes - Added a Prometheus helper to read per-key model remaining rate-limit values from hidden additional headers when metadata values are absent. - Added regression coverage for non-zero and zero header values so gauges no longer report the sentinel when the proxy rate limiter already supplied real values.

signals.title: wire managed_agents into POST /v2/sessions/{sid}/runs
signals.text: ## Summary Connects `litellm/managed_agents/` to Epic A's run-creation endpoint. After `POST /v2/sessions/{sid}/runs` inserts the queued row, a fire-and-forget asyncio task drives the LLM tool loop via the managed_agents primitives (`ClaudeSDKAgentRuntime` + `LocalSandbox` defaults) and persists every emitted event to `LiteLLM_AgentRunEvent` so the existing SSE stream surfaces them. Gated by `agent_settings.managed_agents_enabled` (default `True`). Tests opt out via the `LITELLM_DISABLE_MANAGED_AGENTS_RUN_DRIVER` env var, set in the agent_session_endpoints conftest, so legacy daemon-driven test scenarios keep working unchanged. Smoke test (full flow against a local proxy with anthropic + Postgres): - `POST /v2/agents` → agent created - `POST /v2/sessions` → session in `provisioning` - `POST /v2/sessions/{sid}/runs` → queued row, returned immediately - Background `drive_run` task ran the tool loop end-to-end and persisted 17 events: `run_started`, multiple `system`, `thinking`, `assistant_message`, `run_finished`. Run flipped to `finished`. - SSE `GET /v2/sessions/{sid}/runs/{rid}/events?starting_seq=N` streamed the events as expected. ## Notes - Wiring imports from `litellm.managed_agents` are deferred to call-time so `litellm.proxy` keeps importing cleanly even while the parent branch is still adding pieces to the `managed_agents` package. - We use the lower-level `AgentRuntime` / `Sandbox` / `AgentConfig` / `SessionState` primitives rather than `Session.send` because the endpoint already inserted the run row — `Session.send` would create a duplicate. - PR targets the parent branch `litellm_lit-2879-managed-agents`; will be merged into that branch before the parent opens its own PR. ## Test plan - [x] Local proxy smoke test: events stream end-to-end after run create - [x] Existing `agent_session_endpoints/test_*` unit tests unchanged (env-var disable preserves legacy semantics) - [ ] Pre-existing FakePrismaClient bugs (unrelated `agent_id=None` Pydantic errors) tracked separately

signals.title: feat(a2a): support x- prefixed extension fields in agent_card_params
signals.text: ## Title Support custom x- prefixed extension fields in agent_card_params for A2A agent registration ## Relevant issues Closes #27371 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/litellm/` directory, Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement - [x] My PR passes all unit tests - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## What this PR does The [A2A protocol specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) supports custom extension properties with namespace prefixes (e.g., `x-provider-org`, `x-routing-hints`) on AgentCards. However, when registering agents via `POST /v1/agents`, these extension fields are **silently stripped** because Pydantic's TypedDict validation drops unknown fields during request parsing. ### Root Cause The `AgentCard` TypedDict in `litellm/types/agents.py` defines only known A2A fields. When FastAPI parses the request body against the `AgentConfig` TypedDict, Pydantic v2 removes any fields not defined in `AgentCard` — including valid A2A extension fields. Confirmed with Pydantic v2: ```python from pydantic import TypeAdapter ta = TypeAdapter(AgentConfig) result = ta.validate_python(data_with_x_fields) # x-provider-org is MISSING from result['agent_card_params'] ``` ### Fix This PR adds a minimal, backward-compatible recovery mechanism: 1. **`_extract_extension_fields(raw_body)`** — Extracts all `x-` prefixed keys from the raw JSON request body's `agent_card_params` 2. **`_merge_extension_fields(agent, extension_fields)`** — Merges recovered extension fields back into the typed request's `agent_card_params` 3. The `create_agent`, `update_agent`, and `patch_agent` endpoints now accept the raw `Request` object alongside the typed body, recover extension fields, and merge them before storage The storage layer (`agent_card_params` is serialized to JSON via `safe_dumps()`) and retrieval layer (`AgentResponse.agent_card_params` is `Dict[str, Any]`) already handle arbitrary keys — this fix only bridges the gap at the request parsing step. ### Changes | File | Change | |------|--------| | `litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/endpoints.py` | Add `_extract_extension_fields()` and `_merge_extension_fields()` helpers; modify `create_agent`, `update_agent`, `patch_agent` to recover and merge x- extension fields | | `tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_extension_fields.py` | 12 tests covering helper functions (8 unit tests) and endpoint integration (2 integration tests with mocked DB) | ### Testing All 12 new tests pass. Existing endpoint tests show the same pass/fail ratio as `main` (no regressions): ``` tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_extension_fields.py 12 passed tests/test_litellm/proxy/agent_endpoints/test_endpoints.py 25 passed, 7 failed (pre-existing) ``` ### Example After this fix, the following request preserves `x-provider-org` and `x-routing-hints`: ```bash curl -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1/agents" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "agent_name": "billing-agent", "agent_card_params": { "url": "http://my-agent:9999/", "name": "Billing Agent", "description": "Enterprise billing assistant", "x-provider-org": { "business": "telecom", "domain": "customer-service" }, "x-routing-hints": { "priority": "high", "region": "in-west" }, "skills": [{"id": "billing", "tags": ["billing"]}], "protocolVersion": "1.0" } }' ``` The extension fields are then returned in: - `GET /v1/agents` (agent list) - `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}` (single agent) - `GET /a2a/{agent_id}/.well-known/agent-card.json` (A2A discovery) - `GET /public/agent_hub` (public discovery)

signals.title: [Fix] Team-based model name corruption on PATCH
signals.text: ## Relevant issues ## Summary ### Failure Path (Before Fix) For team-scoped ("Team-BYOK") models, the backend stores two names: - `model_name` (DB column): an internal routing key `model_name_{team_id}_{uuid}`, used by the in-memory router's primary `model_name → deployment` index. Two teams with the same public name need distinct routing keys here. - `model_info.team_public_model_name`: the user-facing public name (e.g. `gpt-4o`). The internal name was leaking into `/v1/model/info` and `/v2/model/info` API responses. The UI bound the model edit form to that field, so any non-rename edit (e.g. changing TPM) PATCHed the model with the internal name as `model_name`. The PATCH endpoint then treated it as a new public name, overwrote `team_public_model_name`, and rewrote the team's `models[]` list with the mangled string — breaking team-based routing for that model. ### Fix 1. Add `_translate_model_name_for_response` in `proxy_server.py`. For team-scoped rows, swap `model_name` to the public name held in `model_info.team_public_model_name` before returning. Apply at `_get_proxy_model_info` (covers `/v1/model/info`, `/model/info`) and in `/v2/model/info` before pagination. The DB column and router index keep the internal name as the routing key — the swap is presentation-layer only. 2. Harden `_get_public_model_name` in `model_management_endpoints.py`. When `patch_data.model_name` matches the internal mangled shape `model_name_{team_id}_{uuid}` or equals the existing DB column, treat it as "no rename intent" and fall through to the existing `team_public_model_name`. This protects against any client (UI, scripts, future code) that round-trips the leaked internal name. 3. Standardize `AgentBuilderView` selection on `model_info.id` instead of `model_name`. Once response translation lands, two team-scoped agents can share a public name; the lookup needs a stable id to avoid collisions. ## Testing Verified end-to-end against a local proxy with a regression harness exercising three PATCH scenarios on fixtures including a deliberate cross-team public-name collision: - TPM-only edit on a team model — `team_public_model_name` and the team's `models[]` list are unchanged after the PATCH; only `litellm_params.tpm` updates. - Genuine rename on a team model — still works; team's `models[]` list updates correctly. - Defensive case: client PATCHes with a fabricated `model_name_{team_id}_{uuid}` payload — treated as a no-op for the public name; no corruption. Across all scenarios, the DB `model_name` column for team rows is unchanged (router invariant preserved). Two fresh captures on the fixed backend produce zero diffs against each other (determinism). ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Screenshots

signals.text: ## Linear ticket Resolves [LIT-2920](https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-2920), [LIT-2921](https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-2921), [LIT-2922](https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-2922), [LIT-2923](https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-2923) (project: [Cursor SDK on LiteLLM v2 — opencode-based](https://linear.app/litellm-ai/project/cursor-sdk-on-litellm-v2-opencode-based-086de0f4a993)) ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] Tests added in `tests/test_litellm/managed_agents/` (75+ unit tests + 3 integration tests against real opencode) - [x] Unit tests pass locally - [x] PR scope: only the 5 happy-path endpoints (POST /v2/agents, GET /v2/sessions/:id, POST/GET /v2/sessions/:id/messages, GET /v2/sessions/:id/events). Krrish owns POST /v2/sessions in a follow-up. - [ ] Greptile review — will request after CI is green ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Ships the sandbox-agnostic public API the Cursor SDK migration is built on. Three happy-path flows from the design doc all work end-to-end against a local opencode server. **Endpoints (5 of 6 — Krrish's POST /v2/sessions follows separately):** - `POST /v2/agents` — create agent definition - `GET /v2/sessions/:id` — fetch session (sandbox_url/metadata stripped from response) - `POST /v2/sessions/:id/messages` — send a user message (async, returns 202) - `GET /v2/sessions/:id/messages` — list messages (normalized from opencode's parts shape) - `GET /v2/sessions/:id/events` — SSE stream (normalized from opencode's bus) **Layout:** - `litellm/managed_agents/types.py` — Pydantic models - `litellm/managed_agents/adapters/opencode.py` — opencode HTTP adapter (httpx-based) - `litellm/managed_agents/adapters/normalization.py` — opencode message + event normalization - `litellm/managed_agents/endpoints/{agents,sessions,messages,events}.py` — handlers - `litellm/managed_agents/router.py` — composite router; registered in `proxy_server.py` - `litellm-proxy-extras/.../migrations/20260507120000_add_managed_agent_tables/` — hand-written SQL migration **Schema:** - `LiteLLM_ManagedAgent` (id, name, config Json, created_by, ...) - `LiteLLM_ManagedAgentSession` (id, agent_id, sandbox_type/size/timeout/idle/image, sandbox_url, sandbox_metadata, status, repos, env_vars, ...) - Added to all three `schema.prisma` copies (root, proxy/, proxy-extras/) byte-identical. **Testing strategy** (no Krrish dependency): ```bash opencode serve --port 1234 & OC_SID=\$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:1234/session -d '{}' | jq -r .id) psql -d litellm -c "INSERT INTO \"LiteLLM_ManagedAgentSession\" (id, agent_id, sandbox_type, sandbox_url, sandbox_metadata, status, ...) VALUES ('ses_test', 'agt_test', 'opencode', 'http://127.0.0.1:1234', '{\"opencode_session_id\":\"\$OC_SID\"}', 'ready', ...);" # now hit /v2/sessions/ses_test/messages — same code path as Krrish's prod sandbox ``` The `tests/test_litellm/managed_agents/test_happy_paths.py` integration suite spins up real opencode + a real uvicorn server and runs all three contract flows. ## Known follow-ups (separate commits coming on this branch) 1. **Adapter normalization deltas.** The preflight agent that hit a real opencode server found the contract's assumed message shape was wrong: opencode messages are `{info, parts}` not flat, fields are camelCase (`sessionID`, `messageID`, `modelID`), timestamps are epoch ms not ISO, text deltas use `message.part.delta` not `message.part.updated`, and the `model` field on `prompt_async` is an object `{providerID, modelID}` not a string. The handlers and tests are correct against the contract; the adapter normalization needs updating. 2. **`SandboxSpec.idle_timeout_minutes` upper bound.** Currently `ge=1` only — needs a Pydantic `field_validator` to enforce `idle_timeout_minutes <= timeout_minutes`. 3. Adapter unit tests assert against the (currently-wrong) normalized output. They'll need to update with #1. ## Out of scope (deferred from MVP) The contract listed 13 endpoints. We cut to 6 to ship the happy paths first. Deferred: agent get/list/patch/delete, sessions list, sessions delete, single-message GET. See contract §8.

signals.title: docs(cookbook): add Agent Threat Rules detection callback example
signals.text: This adds a small cookbook example showing how to plug Agent Threat Rules into LiteLLM as a CustomGuardrail. ATR is an open detection standard for AI agent threats (prompt injection, tool poisoning, MCP attacks, skill compromise) released under Apache-2.0 at https://github.com/Agent-Threat-Rule/agent-threat-rules. The new file cookbook/atr_detection_callback/atr_detection_callback.py defines ATRDetectionGuardrail, a CustomGuardrail subclass whose async_pre_call_hook runs each user message through six ATR-inspired regex patterns covering instruction override, system prompt exfiltration, role-play jailbreak, base64-wrapped payloads, MCP tool override, and file:// SSRF. On match, the callback logs the rule id and raises ValueError, which LiteLLM surfaces as a blocked request. The patterns embedded in the file are illustrative copies. The full ruleset and the YAML schema live in the ATR repository, and the README in the cookbook directory shows the proxy_config.yaml wiring snippet plus a one-paragraph note on extending the example to load live rule files at startup. Both files are net-new and additive. No existing cookbook example or core module is modified. Why this is useful: existing LiteLLM guardrail examples cover provider-specific moderation (OpenAI moderation, Bedrock guardrails, Lakera) but there is no minimal pattern-based example focused on agent-specific threat categories. This fills that gap with a self-contained, dependency-free starting point.

signals.title: fix(router): resolve model_group_alias in pre-routing hook
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #27473 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/test_litellm/` directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit` - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Type Bug Fix ## Changes `Router.async_pre_routing_hook` looks up `model` in `self.complexity_routers`, `self.auto_routers`, `self.quality_routers`, and `self.adaptive_routers` -- but when the caller passes a `model_group_alias` name (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-6`) instead of the actual group name (e.g. `internal-ai`), none of the maps match. The hook returns `None`, the raw `auto_router/complexity_router` deployment is selected as-is, and `litellm.acompletion(model="auto_router/complexity_router")` fails with `BadRequestError: Unmapped LLM provider`. The fix adds alias resolution via `self._get_model_from_alias(model)` at the top of `async_pre_routing_hook`, before any router map lookups. This is the same utility already used in `_common_checks_available_deployment` for the sync path. ### Test plan Added 6 unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/router_utils/test_pre_routing_hook_alias_resolution.py`: - Alias resolves to complexity_router - Alias resolves to auto_router - Alias resolves to quality_router - Non-alias model still matches directly (no regression) - Unknown model with no alias returns None - Dict-format alias (with `hidden` key) resolves correctly
