signals.title: feat(search): add SerpApi search provider support
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - LiteLLM cannot use SerpApi as a search provider. How it solves it: - Added SerpApi as a search provider: added request, authentication, and response transformations. - Provider registration in search and pricing catalogs. - Tests for requests, limits, credentials, extras, and errors. ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin cannot use SerpApi for configured searches. 1. The admin configures `serpapi-search` with `search_provider: serpapi` and a SerpApi API key. 2. A client sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/search/serpapi-search` with `{"query":"python 3.14 t-strings","max_results":3}`. 3. The proxy returns HTTP 500 with `'serpapi' is not a valid SearchProviders`. After: the same proxy configuration returns standard LiteLLM search results. 1. The admin configures `serpapi-search` with `search_provider: serpapi` and a SerpApi API key. 2. A client sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/search/serpapi-search` with `{"query":"python 3.14 t-strings","max_results":3}`. 3. The proxy returns HTTP 200 with `object: "search"` and three normalized results. ## Relevant issues N/A ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Proxy Configuration Used ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6-luna litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY search_tools: - search_tool_name: serpapi-search litellm_params: search_provider: serpapi api_key: os.environ/SERPAPI_KEY litellm_settings: callbacks: - websearch_interception websearch_interception_params: enabled_providers: - openai search_tool_name: serpapi-search general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY ``` ### 1. Search Tool Connection Test `POST /search_tools/test_connection` successfully connected to SerpApi and returned live results. ```bash curl -sS \ -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/search_tools/test_connection \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "litellm_params": { "search_provider": "serpapi" } }' ``` ### 2. Proxy Search: `POST /v1/search/serpapi-search` works: ```bash curl -sS \ -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/search/serpapi-search \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "query": "python 3.14 t-strings", "max_results": 3 }' \ | jq '{ object, result_count: (.results | length), titles: [.results[].title], urls: [.results[].url] }' ``` ### 3. Proxy Search with SerpApi Options `POST /v1/search/serpapi-search` accepts SerpApi parameters such as `engine`, `hl`, and `country`. ```bash curl -i -sS \ -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/search/serpapi-search \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "query": "latest Python features", "engine": "google_light", "hl": "en", "country": "IN", "max_results": 3 }' ``` ### 4. Direct Python SDK Search `litellm.search()` works: ```python import litellm response = litellm.search( query="latest AI news", search_provider="serpapi", engine="google_light", max_results=5, ) print(f"result_count={len(response.results)}") print(response) ``` ### 5. GPT-5.6 Luna Responses API with SerpApi Web Search `POST /v1/responses` used the configured SerpApi search tool and returned a sourced answer from GPT-5.6 Luna. ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6-luna", "input": "Search the web and answer: What are three notable Python 3.14 features? Give a concise answer with source URLs.", "tools": [ { "type": "web_search" } ] }' ``` The equivalent searches are visible on the SerpApi dashboard: ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - `max_tokens_per_page` has no SerpApi equivalent and is ignored. - `max_results` is enforced after SerpApi returns results. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat: add TealTiger as a custom guardrail plugin
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No self-hosted guardrail exists that needs zero API keys and zero network calls - Teams want PII redaction, budget limits, and tool allowlisting without adding a vendor dependency How it solves it: - Adds TealTiger: a guardrail using only local regex + policy rules, no external calls - Registers via `apply_guardrail`, the same interface Onyx Guard uses (`guardrail_hooks/onyx/onyx.py`) - Follows the exact registration pattern already used by Akto (`guardrail_hooks/akto/__init__.py`) ## User Flow Before: a developer sends a chat completion containing PII and has no way to redact it without paying for and configuring an external guardrail service (Presidio needs Azure, Lakera needs an API key). 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with a message body containing `"My SSN is 123-45-6789, please help me file taxes."` 2. The full message, unredacted, is forwarded to the underlying model provider 3. There is no local, dependency-free option in the guardrail list to prevent this After: the same request has PII redacted before it reaches the model, with zero external calls. 1. The proxy admin adds a `tealtiger` entry to the `guardrails` block in `config.yaml` (no API key required) 2. The developer sends the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with the SSN in the message 3. The request that reaches the model provider now reads `"My SSN is [REDACTED:SSN], please help me file taxes."` 4. The response includes header `x-litellm-applied-guardrails: tealtiger` confirming it ran ## Relevant issues Fixes #36163 ## Linear ticket <!-- external contributor — leaving blank --> ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests (`tests/guardrails_tests/test_tealtiger.py` — 7 tests covering PII redaction, MONITOR mode, tool allowlisting, budget enforcement, and the `apply_guardrail` interface; all 7 confirmed passing on a real Windows dev environment with real `litellm` installed, not just a stub) - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks — full `tests/guardrails_tests/` suite run locally (461 passed, 1 skipped, 32 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change, confirmed identical on `litellm_internal_staging` before these changes; see note below) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem (adds one guardrail; touches exactly one line outside the new `tealtiger/` directory — see `litellm/types/guardrails.py`) - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on Slack (#pr-review). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Verified end-to-end against a real running `litellm` proxy (v1.97.0, from this branch) with a real `gpt-4o-mini` call using a real `OPENAI_API_KEY` — no mocks. Config used: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY guardrails: - guardrail_name: "tealtiger" litellm_params: guardrail: tealtiger mode: "pre_call" policy_mode: "ENFORCE" ``` **Note on `mode`:** `pre_call` is required, not optional. `during_call` (LiteLLM's other common mode) runs the guardrail concurrently with the LLM call rather than gating/rewriting the request first — testing against a real API call showed the unredacted SSN still reaching OpenAI under `during_call`, since it doesn't block on the guardrail's modified output before dispatching. Only `pre_call` actually rewrites `data["messages"]` before the request goes out. This is called out explicitly in `docs/tealtiger.md` and should be treated as the documented default, not one of several equivalent options. Request: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "My SSN is 123-45-6789, please help me file taxes."}], "guardrails": ["tealtiger"] }' ``` Proxy debug log confirming the real (non-mock) OpenAI call was made with the redacted content, not the original SSN: ``` 10:23:06 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: handler.py:190 - OpenAI Chat Completions: Processed input messages: [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'My SSN is [REDACTED:SSN], please help me file taxes.'}] 10:23:06 - LiteLLM:DEBUG: utils.py:472 - litellm.acompletion(... model='gpt-4o-mini', messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'My SSN is [REDACTED:SSN], please help me file taxes.'}] ...) 10:23:14 - LiteLLM Router:INFO: router.py:2938 - litellm.acompletion(model=gpt-4o-mini) 200 OK ``` Real model response (received by the proxy after the redacted request), confirming the model never saw the actual SSN: ```json { "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "choices": [{"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "I'm sorry, but I can't assist with filing taxes or handling personal information such as Social Security Numbers. It's important to keep sensitive information private and secure. However, I can offer general advice about tax filing or answer questions you may have. What specific information do you need help with?"}}], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 56, "prompt_tokens": 25, "total_tokens": 81} } ``` `standard_logging_guardrail_information` from the same request, showing the guardrail ran successfully in 0.8ms: ``` {'guardrail_name': 'tealtiger', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call', 'guardrail_response': 'allow', 'guardrail_status': 'success', 'duration': 0.000801} ``` Commit hash this was captured at: 01886ffc78 Also verified: the full `tests/guardrails_tests/` suite (461 tests, including the 7 new `test_tealtiger.py` tests) shows the same 32 pre-existing failures on this branch as on `litellm_internal_staging` before these changes — all in `test_bedrock_guardrails.py` (missing AWS credentials), `test_presidio_pii.py` (missing `PRESIDIO_ANALYZER_API_BASE`), `test_semantic_guard.py` (missing optional `semantic_router` dependency), and two unrelated pre-existing failures in `test_eu_ai_act_french_3_scenarios.py` / `test_custom_guardrail.py`. None reference `tealtiger`. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/tealtiger/__init__.py` — registry entries, follows `guardrail_hooks/akto/__init__.py`'s exact pattern - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/tealtiger/tealtiger.py` — `TealTigerGuardrail(CustomGuardrail)`, implements `apply_guardrail` with `@log_guardrail_information` (same decorator used in `guardrail_hooks/onyx/onyx.py`) - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/tealtiger/engine.py` — dependency-free policy engine (PII scan, cost/budget check, tool allowlist), no imports outside the standard library - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/tealtiger/patterns.py` — 47 PII/secret regex patterns across 5 categories - `litellm/types/guardrails.py` — one line added to `SupportedGuardrailIntegrations`: `TEALTIGER = "tealtiger"` - `tests/guardrails_tests/test_tealtiger.py` — 7 tests - `docs/tealtiger.md` — usage docs with quick-start config and known limitations ## QA runbook <!-- not editing existing tests/e2e/, deleting this section --> ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- **Open question for maintainers**, noted in `tealtiger.py`: `apply_guardrail` receives extracted `texts`/`images`/`tool_calls` but not token-usage data. TealTiger's cost/budget tracking (`TealEngine.track_cost`) is implemented but not yet wired to anything in `apply_guardrail`'s response path — is there a recommended way to access `response.usage` from within this interface, or does that require also overriding `async_post_call_success_hook` alongside it?

signals.title: refactor(ui): migrate key info and permissions views off antd and tremor

They open the overflow menu and pick Reset Spend, and a confirm dialog appears 4. They switch to the Settings tab and back to Overview 5. They open a team, go to Member Permissions, tick an endpoint and save 6. Every one of those controls draws its own borders, spacing and icon sizes from antd or Tremor, so a dashboard-wide style change leaves them behind After: all of it behaves identically, and every control is a shadcn component that inherits the dashboard's tokens 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click a key 2. The same header renders, and the copy icon is now sized to match its neighbours 3. They open the overflow menu and pick Reset Spend, and the same confirm dialog appears 4. They switch to the Settings tab and back, and panel state survives as before 5. They open a team, go to Member Permissions, tick an endpoint and save 6. The controls now pick up the dashboard's own tokens, so styling them is a single global change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at 617ad8194c against a live proxy on :4000 holding 50 real keys and 50 real teams, with the dashboard dev server on :3000. Verified by hand in the browser, since jsdom has no layout engine: 1. Open http://localhost:3000/api-keys and click a key. The header renders the full 64 character key id on one line, with the three date columns and their separators aligned 2. Open the overflow menu. Block Key, Reset Spend and Delete Key appear 3. Click Reset Spend. The dialog reads Reset Key Spend, shows the current spend, and offers Cancel and Reset 4. Open http://localhost:3000/teams, pick a team, open Member Permissions The permissions round trip, driven in the running page: ``` checkboxes rendered: 18 toggle first checkbox: aria-checked false -> true Save Changes appears: yes Reset appears: yes after Reset: aria-checked back to false Save Changes gone: yes ``` Nothing was written to the database: the change was reverted with Reset rather than saved. Icon geometry on the key page, which previously had one oversized icon: ``` icons at the 24px default: 0 of 75 (was 1, the antd Typography copy icon) page overflows horizontally: no ``` Local gates: ``` npm run build exit 0 npx vitest run templates + permissions + team 21 files, 410 tests passed consumer test files (6) 160 tests passed npx eslint --pass-on-unpruned-suppressions <8 changed files> exit 0 npx prettier --check <8 changed files> all match ``` Both vitest figures are identical to the pre-migration baselines, so no coverage was lost. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - `keepMounted` on the tab panels is load bearing, since Base UI mounts only the visible one - The user field keeps hover to open, matching antd, so it stays mouse only - Making it keyboard reachable is a follow up, not a silent change here - MCP Server permissions sits beside the two migrated panels and is still on Tremor - That leaves a visual seam on the object permissions card until it lands - The permission checkboxes still have no accessible name, which predates this PR - Tremor badge colours flatten to secondary, except two states where colour carried meaning - `LabeledField` and `DefaultProxyAdminTag` are still on antd and out of scope ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(transcription): stop a zero output rate from zeroing transcription cost
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 43 of 55 per-second transcription models bill $0 - A zero output rate silently suppresses the real input rate - Every deepgram, assemblyai, elevenlabs and groq entry is affected How it solves it: - Take the output branch only when that rate is billable - A zero output rate now falls through to the input rate - No pricing data edits and no existing test rewrites ## User Flow Before: a developer transcribing audio through the proxy is billed nothing, so spend tracking and budgets never see the usage 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `"model": "deepgram/nova-3"` and a 60 second audio file 2. The transcript comes back correctly, so nothing looks wrong 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is listed at $0.00 spend 4. They call GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs and the entry reads `"spend": 0.0` 5. Their key budget never decrements, so transcription traffic is effectively free and unbounded After: the same request records real spend, so logs and budgets reflect the audio actually transcribed 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `"model": "deepgram/nova-3"` and the same 60 second file 2. The transcript comes back identically 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now lists the request at $0.0043 4. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs returns `"spend": 0.0043` for that entry 5. The key budget decrements, so transcription traffic counts against limits like every other route ## Relevant issues Fixes #19154 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix _To be added_ ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Two earlier attempts were reverted, #19352 and #24297 - #24297 summed both rates, which double-billed the whisper entries - It also nulled the field its own tests asserted against - This guards the output rate instead, so pricing data is untouched - whisper cost is unchanged and both whisper tests stay untouched - Follow-up: whisper spend still splits as output, not input

signals.title: fix(langfuse): log `custom_tool_call` items in Responses API output
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Freeform (custom) tool calls log no output to Langfuse - Every code-mode turn looks like the model answered nothing How it solves it: - Map `custom_tool_call` output items into the Langfuse output payload ## User Flow Before: a developer proxying a coding agent that uses a freeform `exec` tool sees blank outputs in Langfuse, so a whole session reads as if the model never answered 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"tools": [{"type": "custom", "name": "exec", ...}]` 2. The response comes back with a `custom_tool_call` item carrying the JavaScript to run, and the agent runs it 3. They open that generation in Langfuse: **Output is `null`**, while input, token counts and cost are all correct 4. Every turn where the model called `exec` looks empty, so the trace can't be used to review what the agent actually did After: the same request records the tool call it actually made 1. They send the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with the same custom tool 2. The response comes back with the same `custom_tool_call` item, and the agent runs it 3. They open that generation in Langfuse: **Output shows the call** — `[{"id": "...", "name": "exec", "call_id": "call_...", "type": "custom_tool_call", "input": "console.log(6*7)\n"}]` 4. Turns that called `exec` are reviewable alongside the plain-text and `function_call` turns that already worked ## Relevant issues <!-- none found --> ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) — ran `ruff format`/`ruff check` on the touched file and the target test module locally; full suite left to CI - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real `/v1/responses` calls through a local proxy against a live `gpt-5.6-sol` deployment, exporting to a self-hosted Langfuse. No mocks. Same request both times, only the commit differs. **Before** — proxy at `423b791ee0395815050998dd73542445350ab792` (this PR's parent): ```console $ python probe.py # POST /v1/responses, tools=[{"type":"custom","name":"exec"}], tool_choice=required 200 ['custom_tool_call'] ``` Langfuse observation `dc21eba5e810824f`: ```json {"output": null, "usageDetails": {"input": 148, "output": 15, "total": 163}} ``` **After** — proxy at `77c9ed0` (this PR): ```console $ python probe.py # identical request 200 ['custom_tool_call'] ``` Langfuse observation `1727d450336f4f56`: ```json {"output": [{"id": "U12e7ZEbFvdvGAeB3Wad7...", "name": "exec", "call_id": "call_...", "type": "custom_tool_call", "input": "console.log(6*7)\n"}]} ``` Plain-text and `function_call` turns were unaffected in both runs (they already worked). Unit test, red before the one-line branch and green after, at `77c9ed0`: ```console $ pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_langfuse_otel.py -k responses_api # without the fix: 1 failed, 5 passed # with the fix: 6 passed ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only `/v1/responses` emits `custom_tool_call`; the other two endpoints are unaffected ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(mcp): tolerate invalid content blocks in tools/call results
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A single malformed content block fails an entire MCP `tools/call` result - Client returns a raw `ValidationError` traceback instead of any content How it solves it: - Degrade only the invalid content block to text instead of raising - Every valid content block in the result is left untouched ## User Flow Before: a developer calling a tool on a non-compliant upstream MCP server through the gateway gets an error instead of the tool's real output 1. They send a `tools/call` JSON-RPC request for a tool backed by an Azure DevOps MCP server to the gateway's MCP endpoint 2. The upstream server's response includes a resource content item using a relative path instead of a full URI, which the MCP client library rejects 3. The gateway's response comes back with `"isError": true` and a single `text` block containing a raw pydantic `ValidationError` traceback, not the tool's actual output After: the same call returns the tool's real output even though the upstream's response is still not fully spec-compliant 1. They send the same `tools/call` JSON-RPC request for the same tool to the same MCP endpoint 2. The upstream server's response still contains that same non-compliant resource content item 3. The gateway's response now comes back with `"isError": false` and the tool's actual output as `text` content ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review The lint/format/unit-test box is left unchecked deliberately: this repo's build backend (`maturin`, compiling `litellm-rust`) requires a local Rust toolchain that wasn't available in the environment this PR was written in, so `make lint` / `make test-unit` could not be run locally. The new test was verified with a standalone script exercising the same `mcp==1.28.1` model classes and the same `_ScriptedUpstream`/`_ScriptedClient` harness logic used in the actual test file, not through `pytest` itself. Flagging this explicitly rather than checking a box I couldn't verify; happy to fix anything CI turns up. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is not the live-proxy curl proof this template normally asks for. A local proxy could not be built for the same Rust-toolchain reason noted above. What follows is real evidence gathered against a live, non-compliant upstream MCP server, plus a real run of this fix's exact logic against that captured payload, at the commit above. **Before (parent commit `423b791ee0395815050998dd73542445350ab792`): the real failure, captured live** An MCP `tools/call` request for a `repo_file` tool backed by an Azure DevOps MCP server (`mcp.dev.azure.com`), sent with a real, valid upstream token, returns this content block verbatim: ```json {"type":"resource","resource":{"uri":"/templates/ev.job/template/docker-compose.yml","mimeType":"text/plain","blob":"dmVyc2lvbjogJzIuNCcK..."}} ``` Feeding that exact block into `mcp==1.28.1`'s `CallToolResult.model_validate` (the same call `ClientSession.call_tool` makes internally) raises: ``` pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 14 validation errors for CallToolResult content.0.TextContent.type Input should be 'text' [type=literal_error, input_value='resource', input_type=str] ... content.0.EmbeddedResource.resource.TextResourceContents.uri Input should be a valid URL, relative URL without a base [type=url_parsing, input_value='/templates/ev.job/template/docker-compose.yml', input_type=str] ... ``` This is exactly the `ValidationError` that `MCPClient.call_tool`'s except-block turns into the `isError: true` text block described above. **After (this PR, commit `3b7d9e74cbd8561bf62041c5888168ec64a0779c`): the same payload, run through the new model** ``` $ python -c " from litellm.experimental_mcp_client.tolerant_result import TolerantCallToolResult payload = {'content': [{'type': 'resource', 'resource': { 'uri': '/templates/ev.job/template/docker-compose.yml', 'mimeType': 'text/plain', 'blob': 'dmVyc2lvbjogJzIuNCcK', }}], 'isError': False} result = TolerantCallToolResult.model_validate(payload) print(result.content[0].type, repr(result.content[0].text)) " text "version: '2.4'\n" ``` No exception. `isError` stays `False`. The content that used to be silently discarded behind a traceback comes through as the actual decoded text. The new test in this PR, `TestCallToolToleratesMalformedContentBlocks::test_relative_uri_resource_degrades_to_text_instead_of_raising`, asserts this same outcome through the real `ClientSession`-derived class and real anyio streams via `_ScriptedUpstream`/`_ScriptedClient`, not a hand-built result object; it could not be executed via `pytest` here for the Rust-toolchain reason above, so this is not a substitute for CI actually running it, only evidence that the logic it exercises behaves as asserted. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - `make lint` / `make test-unit` not run locally; blocked on this repo's Rust/maturin build requirement - `TolerantClientSession.call_tool` mirrors `mcp==1.28.1`'s method body verbatim (no override seam exists); a later `mcp` release changing that method won't automatically propagate - Uses `Any`/`Mapping[str, Any]`/`object` for the genuinely untyped external data at this one boundary; flagging in case `reportAny` disagrees ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: refactor(ui): move the shared dropdowns and selectors onto shadcn primitives
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Thirteen shared dropdowns and selectors still render through antd and Tremor - They are reached from keys, teams, users, models and cost tracking - Several e2e steps drive those controls through antd's internal classes How it solves it: - Rebuilds all thirteen on `@/components/ui` and the shared wrappers - Keeps every public prop signature identical, so no caller changes - Repoints the e2e steps at the test id, role and data-slot ## User Flow Before: an admin creating a virtual key sees a form built from Ant Design and Tremor, so it does not follow the dashboard's own design tokens and cannot be restyled globally 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click Create New Key 2. They type into the Team field, watch it filter, and pick a team 3. They set Reset Budget, then clear it again 4. They open a key, choose Delete Key, and confirm in a dialog listing the key id 5. On a team's Settings they switch Router Settings between Loadbalancing and Fallbacks, then save 6. Every one of those controls draws its own borders, spacing and icon sizes from antd or Tremor, so a dashboard-wide style change leaves them behind After: all of it behaves identically, and every control is a shadcn component that inherits the dashboard's tokens 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click Create New Key 2. They type into the same Team field, it filters the same way, and the Organization, Team and Project labels now read out with their controls again 3. They set Reset Budget, and clear it by picking Never resets at the top of the list 4. They open a key, choose Delete Key, and confirm in the same dialog, with the key id wrapping instead of overflowing 5. They switch Router Settings between the same two tabs and saving still keeps both tabs' values 6. The controls now pick up the dashboard's own tokens, so styling them is a single global change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at afff1b08fa against a live proxy on :4000 holding 50 real teams and 50 real keys, with the dashboard dev server on :3000. Verified by hand in the browser, since jsdom has no layout engine: 1. Open http://localhost:3000/api-keys, click Create New Key, and drive the Team field 2. Open a key, More key actions, Delete Key 3. Open http://localhost:3000/teams, pick a team, Settings, Edit Settings The team dropdown, driven end to end: ``` [data-testid=team-dropdown] [role=combobox] found, placeholder "Search or select a team" open it: 20 options, alias over team id type "tls-team2": 20 options -> 1 pick it: input reads tls-team2, clear control present ``` Label associations in the Create New Key modal, before and after: ``` before Organization -> organization_id unresolved Team -> team_id unresolved Project -> project_id unresolved after all six label[for] resolve, 0 unresolved ``` The delete dialog: ``` accessible name: Delete Key width: 448px key id: 64 chars, wraps, 0 elements overflow their box icons: 16px ``` Router settings, with Loadbalancing selected: ``` tabpanels mounted: 2 (Routing Settings AND Group 1 / Primary Model) ``` Both stay mounted, which is what Tremor did and what reading the fields back on save depends on. Local gates: ``` npm run build exit 0 npm run test 654 files, 7160 tests passed npx eslint --pass-on-unpruned-suppressions <28 changed files> exit 0, 59 -> 58 warnings npx prettier --check <28 changed files> all match ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - The seven e2e specs are not runtime verified, only their selectors in a live page - `PassThroughRoutesSelector` lists each route once with its methods joined - antd emitted one row per method, all sharing the same value - `MultiSelect` disables itself while loading; antd stayed interactive behind a spinner - Clearing a Reset Budget is now an explicit Never resets item, not an X - The delete dialog no longer closes on escape or the backdrop while deleting - antd allowed both, so a destructive request could outlive its own dialog - `SearchSelect` now shows a value its options do not carry, matching `PaginatedSearchSelect` - `chartUtils.tsx` has no importers at all and is a deletion candidate - `LabeledField` still imports antd `Typography` independently of the tag it renders - `PassThroughRoutesSelector` labels still do not resolve, `MultiSelect` takes no id ## QA runbook No assertion changed in any of these; only the locators did, from antd's internal classes to the test id, role and data-slot. Each bullet is one changed test. - tests/e2e/ui/tests/proxy-admin/keys.spec.ts - "Create a key for a team" - a key created against a team is owned by it - [ ] Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and click Create New Key - [ ] Click the Team field, expect a popup listing each team's alias above its id, and pick the seeded team - [ ] Create the key, then GET /key/info for it and expect its team_id to match - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/ui/tests/proxy-admin/keys.spec.ts - "Delete a key" - a deleted key stops authenticating - [ ] Open a key, click More key actions, click Delete Key - [ ] Expect a dialog named "Delete Key" showing the key id in its Key Information grid - [ ] Confirm, then call /chat/completions with that key and expect 401 - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/ui/tests/proxy-admin/teams.spec.ts - "Delete a team" - a deleted team disappears from /team/list - [ ] Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=teams, open a throwaway team's row menu, click Delete - [ ] Expect a dialog named "Delete Team?" and confirm - [ ] GET /team/list and expect that team_id gone - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/ui/tests/team-admin/teamAdmin.spec.ts - "Create a key as team admin" and "Remove a team member" - [ ] Sign in as a team admin, create a key, and pick the team from the same Team field as above - [ ] On the team's Members tab remove a member, expect a dialog named "Delete Team Member", confirm - [ ] GET /team/info and expect that member gone from members_with_roles - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/ui/tests/internal-user/internalUser.spec.ts - an internal user sees only their own teams in the Team field - [ ] Sign in as the seeded internal user and open Create New Key - [ ] Click the Team field and expect the popup to list that user's team - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/ui/tests/internal-user/internalUserNoTeam.spec.ts - a user with no teams gets an empty Team field - [ ] Sign in as the no-team user and open Create New Key - [ ] Click the Team field and expect "Loading teams…" then "No teams found", and no team rows - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/ui/tests/internal-user/internalUserWithTeams.spec.ts - a user with teams gets them listed - [ ] Sign in as the multi-team user and open Create New Key - [ ] Click the Team field and expect each of their teams listed - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky - [ ] Submit, then GET /model/info and expect the deployment carrying that team id - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky ### Final Attestation - signals.title: fix(model_prices): correct Gemini 2.5 shutdown dates and DeepSeek V4 max output tokens
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Gemini 2.5 GA models carried no shutdown date - `gemini-embedding-001` shutdown date was two years late - DeepSeek V4 max output capped at 8192, not 384K How it solves it: - Adds Google's announced 2026-10-16 shutdown to Gemini 2.5 GA - Corrects `gemini-embedding-001` to Google's 2026-07-14 date - Raises DeepSeek V4 flash/pro max output to 393216 ## User Flow Before: a developer asking DeepSeek V4 for a long answer, and an admin planning migrations off soon-to-be-retired Gemini models, both get told the wrong thing by the gateway 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/model/info for their `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` deployments and read back `"max_output_tokens": 8192`, so a client that sizes `max_tokens` from the gateway truncates at 8K where DeepSeek would have allowed 384K 2. They grep the model metadata the gateway ships for the Gemini 2.5 GA models and find no shutdown date at all, so `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` look like they have nothing on the calendar, though Google announced October 16, 2026 3. They find `gemini-embedding-001` marked as going away in 2028 instead of July 14, 2026, so the migration off it never gets scheduled and calls start failing without warning After: the same lookups report what each provider actually published 1. The same GET https://litellm-domain/model/info reports `"max_output_tokens": 393216` for both DeepSeek V4 models, so long generations are sized correctly 2. The Gemini 2.5 GA models all carry a 2026-10-16 shutdown date 3. `gemini-embedding-001` carries 2026-07-14, giving the admin a real date to plan against once #26900 starts surfacing it ## Sources Every changed value comes from the provider's own docs, checked on 2026-08-14 - Gemini shutdown dates: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations lists `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` with shutdown date October 16, 2026, and `gemini-embedding-001` with July 14, 2026 - DeepSeek limits: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing lists `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` with context length 1M and "MAX OUTPUT: MAXIMUM 384K". 384K is written as 393216, matching how the registry already stores DeepSeek limits in 1024 units (`deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` is 163840) The wider audit turned up nothing else verifiably stale: Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Mistral, Cohere, xAI and Azure lifecycle tables already match the registry entry for entry, DeepSeek V4 pricing already matches the current per-token rates, and the Bedrock legacy/EOL table has no pending EOL model that is missing a date The upcoming DeepSeek peak/off-peak repricing takes effect 16:00 UTC on August 16, 2026 and is deliberately left out until it is live, since the registry has no peak/off-peak dimension ## Relevant issues Supports #26900 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) Existing registry coverage in `tests/test_litellm/test_model_prices_schema.py` validates these fields against the schema, including the `deprecation_date` pattern, so no new test was added for a data-only change ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs use the same live proxy on http://localhost:4000, started with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --port 4000`, against a deployment registered with `curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/model/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model_name": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "litellm_params": {"model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"}}'` Before, at base commit `423b791ee0`, the gateway told clients DeepSeek V4 tops out at 8K output tokens: ``` $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" http://localhost:4000/model/info \ | jq '.data[] | select(.model_name == "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro") | {model_name, max_input_tokens: .model_info.max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens: .model_info.max_output_tokens}' { "model_name": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "max_input_tokens": 1000000, "max_output_tokens": 8192 } ``` After, at commit `b066ed3e31`, the same request reports the 384K ceiling DeepSeek documents: ``` $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" http://localhost:4000/model/info \ | jq '.data[] | select(.model_name == "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro") | {model_name, max_input_tokens: .model_info.max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens: .model_info.max_output_tokens}' { "model_name": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", "max_input_tokens": 1000000, "max_output_tokens": 393216 } ``` `deprecation_date` has no reader anywhere in the gateway yet, so no route serves it until #26900 lands, and the registry the gateway ships is the surface that work will read: ``` $ jq '{gemini_2_5_pro: ."gemini/gemini-2.5-pro".deprecation_date, gemini_2_5_flash: ."gemini/gemini-2.5-flash".deprecation_date, gemini_2_5_flash_lite: ."gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite".deprecation_date, gemini_embedding_001: ."gemini/gemini-embedding-001".deprecation_date}' litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json { "gemini_2_5_pro": "2026-10-16", "gemini_2_5_flash": "2026-10-16", "gemini_2_5_flash_lite": "2026-10-16", "gemini_embedding_001": "2026-07-14" } ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only the Gemini API keys changed, not the Vertex mirrors - DeepSeek peak/off-peak pricing lands separately after August 16 Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/65e89f80ad4346f0aec983f06c6aa0d9

They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and a warning banner spans the top of the page 2. They dismiss it and it stays gone for that license expiry date 3. They read the version tag in the header and click through to the release notes 4. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models and expand Model Group Alias 5. They add an alias whose target model group is long, and the row forces the table sideways 6. They open a key and read its object permissions and logging settings 7. Every one of those controls draws its own borders, spacing and icon sizes from antd or Tremor, so a dashboard-wide style change leaves them behind After: all of it behaves identically, and every control is a shadcn component that inherits the dashboard's tokens 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys and the same warning banner spans the top of the page 2. They dismiss it and it stays gone for that license expiry date, with the expired banner still refusing to close 3. They read the same version tag in the header and click through to the release notes 4. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models and expand Model Group Alias 5. They add the same alias, and the long target model group wraps onto a second line instead of forcing the table sideways 6. They open a key and read the same object permissions and logging settings 7. The controls now pick up the dashboard's own tokens, so styling them is a single global change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at 4544f7dbad against a live proxy on :4000 serving real models, with the dashboard dev server on :3000. Verified by hand in the browser, since jsdom has no layout engine: 1. Open http://localhost:3000/users and read the header 2. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints, expand Model Group Alias, add an alias, then delete it Header, on a route the navbar actually renders: ``` version badge: v1.98.0, inside [data-slot=badge], 56x17 icons at the lucide 24px default: 0 of them, page-wide label[for] that resolve to no id: 0 ``` An alias with a deliberately long name and target, added and read back through the proxy: ``` POST result: "Alias added successfully" at 1280px wide: row 45px tall, no cell overflows its box, page does not scroll sideways at 900px wide: row 65px tall, scrollWidth == clientWidth on both cells, still no sideways scroll computed style: whitespace normal on both value cells, nowrap kept on Actions ``` The row grows instead of overflowing, which is what the `whitespace-normal` override buys back; shadcn's `TableCell` ships `whitespace-nowrap` and Tremor's did not. Local gates: ``` npm run build exit 0 npm run test 654 files, 7156 tests passed grep -rn "antd|@ant-design|@tremor" <8 files> no matches npx eslint --pass-on-unpruned-suppressions <9 changed files> 0 errors, 15 warnings, all pre-existing npx prettier --check <9 changed files + suppressions> all match ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - `onboarding_link` was migrated, then reverted, and stays on antd here - Its dialog opens over the still-antd Invite User modal, which antd stacked for us - Raising only the shadcn content leaves its own backdrop under antd's mask - An outside click then reaches the wrong modal, so the parent closes instead - A second backdrop stops that but does not restore dismissal, verified in the browser - Three shipped guardrails modals share the hazard, so it wants one fix, not a fourth workaround - `model_filters` keeps its native `<select>` elements; they were never antd - antd `Tag` colours become Badge variants, so success is no longer green - Failure keeps its red through the `destructive` variant - The navbar sidebar toggle is unreachable today; no route passes `onToggleSidebar` - Its two new icons therefore render only under test, not on any route ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(router): Auto Router v2 session_key_fallback derivation (#34766)
signals.text: ## Summary Closes #34766 This PR introduces `session_key_fallback` support in LiteLLM's Auto Router v2 (`ComplexityRouter` and `AdaptiveRouter`) to automatically derive session keys when `session_id` is not explicitly provided in the request metadata or headers. ### Key Changes 1. **Router Configuration (`session_key_fallback`)**: - Added `session_key_fallback` to `ComplexityRouterConfig` and `AdaptiveRouterConfig` with supported modes: - `"none"` (default): Preserves existing behavior without automatic session derivation. - `"prompt_cache_key"`: Uses `prompt_cache_key` from request kwargs, metadata, `litellm_params`, `extra_body`, or headers. - `"prefix_hash"`: Computes a deterministic SHA-256 hash of `user_identifier:model_group:first_system_msg:first_user_msg`. 2. **Session Key Resolution & Propagation**: - `ComplexityRouter._resolve_session_id`: Resolves explicit `session_id` first; if absent and a fallback strategy is enabled, derives the key and populates `metadata["session_id"]`. - Propagated session keys enable downstream `DeploymentAffinityCheck` and `AdaptiveRouterPostCallHook` to maintain affinity across multi-turn requests without requiring clients to supply custom headers. - Added debug/info logging via `verbose_router_logger` upon fallback session key resolution. 3. **Adaptive Router Hook Compatibility**: - Enhanced `_resolve_session_key` in `adaptive_router/hooks.py` to inspect direct `kwargs["metadata"]` and `prompt_cache_key`. 4. **Comprehensive Unit Tests**: - Added `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_session_key_fallback.py` verifying: - Explicit `session_id` resolution precedence. - Fallback to `prompt_cache_key` (via params, extra_body, headers). - Fallback to `prefix_hash` across multi-turn conversations and segregation between different callers/prompts. - Default `"none"` behavior preserving unpinned reclassification. - Deployment affinity interaction with derived session keys. - Adaptive router post-call hook key extraction. ## Test Verification - All 12 unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_session_key_fallback.py` pass 100%. - All 98 adaptive routing and router pre-call check tests in `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/adaptive_router/` and `tests/test_litellm/router_utils/pre_call_checks/` pass cleanly.

signals.title: Fix/notfound error retries
signals.text: Fixes #36896 ## What this does `RetryPolicy` had a retry count field for every exception type except `NotFoundError` (404s). Because of that gap, 404s always fall back to `num_retries`, so the router retries them — and since 404 also triggers an immediate cooldown per deployment, each retry cools down another deployment. After enough retries the whole pool gets cooled and the router raises `RouterRateLimitError("No deployments available")`, which surfaces to the client as a 500. This adds a `NotFoundErrorRetries` field so operators can set it to `0` and have 404s returned to the client immediately instead of being retried across the whole deployment pool. ## Changes - `litellm/types/router.py`: added `NotFoundErrorRetries: int | None = None` to `RetryPolicy`. - `litellm/router_utils/get_retry_from_policy.py`: imported `NotFoundError` and added a check in `get_num_retries_from_retry_policy()` so `NotFoundErrorRetries` is respected. - `tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_helper_utils.py`: added a `NotFoundError` case to the existing `test_get_num_retries_from_retry_policy` parametrized test, using `0` retries to match the motivating case from the issue. ## Testing Ran the existing parametrized test locally — all cases pass including the new `NotFoundError` one. Note: this PR only addresses the missing retry field (the primary fix requested in the issue). The secondary "paradox" behavior mentioned in the issue (an exception that triggers cooldown also being retried by default) is a broader behavioral change and is left out of scope here.

signals.title: fix(vertex_ai): normalize tuple-form JSON Schema items before the Vertex transform
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Tuple-form `items` crashes every `vertex_ai/*` request carrying that tool - Error surfaces as `APIConnectionError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` - OpenAI-compatible clients and several MCP servers emit that shape How it solves it: - Rewrite `"items": [A, B]` as `"items": {"anyOf": [A, B]}` once, before the walkers - Runs after `unpack_defs`, so `$ref`-expanded schemas are covered too - `items: []` drops out and `process_items` synthesizes `{"type": "object"}` ## User Flow Before: a developer whose tool schema declares a fixed-shape array gets a connection error from the gateway on every call, while the same tool works against other providers 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash"` and a tool whose parameters contain `"a": {"type": "array", "items": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "string"}]}` 2. The gateway answers with `litellm.APIConnectionError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`, and no request ever reaches the model 3. They retry the identical body against an OpenAI-compatible provider and get a normal completion, so the tool schema itself is fine 4. Their only way forward is a pre-call shim that rewrites the tool schema before the gateway sees it After: the same request is accepted and the tool reaches the model 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same tuple-form tool 2. The gateway forwards the tool to Vertex with that field typed as an array whose entries may be an integer or a string 3. They get a normal completion back, with a tool call if the model chooses to make one 4. The shim can come out of their stack The array position that carried a fixed order is now an unordered union, which is the closest shape Vertex can express ## Relevant issues Fixes #36848 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I do not have Vertex credentials, so there is no live provider run here. What I can show is that the failure is raised while building the request, before anything is sent, so it reproduces without a project or a key. Both runs below use the exact tool schema from the issue. Before, at `423b791e` (the parent of this branch): ``` $ python -c " from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.common_utils import _build_vertex_schema print(_build_vertex_schema({'type':'object','properties':{'a':{'type':'array','items':[{'type':'integer'},{'type':'string'}]}}}))" AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' ``` After, at `f99823bf`: ``` $ python -c " from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.common_utils import _build_vertex_schema print(_build_vertex_schema({'type':'object','properties':{'a':{'type':'array','items':[{'type':'integer'},{'type':'string'}]}}}))" {'type': 'object', 'properties': {'a': {'type': 'array', 'items': {'anyOf': [{'type': 'integer'}, {'type': 'string'}]}}}} ``` A maintainer with Vertex access can confirm the end to end path with the curl in the issue body, which is the same tool schema against a live `vertex_ai/*` deployment. Happy to add that run here if someone can share a sandbox project. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Positional constraints are lost; Vertex cannot express tuple arrays - `additionalItems` is dropped, same as every other unsupported keyword - Boolean sub-schemas (`items: [false]`) still crash, unchanged from today - `prefixItems`, the 2020-12 spelling, is untouched and still ignored - `_build_json_schema` still passes tuple `items` through unchanged ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: refactor(ui): move the settings page and bulk user invite onto shadcn primitives
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The logging and alerts page and the bulk user invite still render through antd and Tremor - Their callback form is an antd Form, so it cannot pick up the dashboard's field styling - The CSV drop zone is an antd Upload, which pulls antd in for a single file read How it solves it: - Rebuilds both on `@/components/ui` and the shared `Field` primitives - Moves the callback form to react-hook-form, already a dependency - Replaces antd Upload with a native file input plus real drag handlers ## User Flow Before: an admin wiring up a logging callback works through a form built from Ant Design and Tremor, so it does not follow the dashboard's own design tokens and cannot be restyled globally 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logging-and-alerts and see five tabs 2. They click Add Callback, pick Datadog, and fill in API Key and Site 3. They submit, and the callback appears in the Active Logging Callbacks table 4. They edit it, change the site, and save 5. On http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=users they click + Bulk Invite Users and drag a CSV onto the drop zone 6. Every one of those controls draws its own borders, spacing and icon sizes from antd or Tremor, so a dashboard-wide style change leaves them behind After: all of it behaves identically, and every control is a shadcn component that inherits the dashboard's tokens 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logging-and-alerts and see the same five tabs, each now driving its own panel 2. They click Add Callback, pick Datadog, and fill in API Key and Site, which now read out with their inputs 3. They submit, and the callback appears in the same table 4. They edit it, change the site, and save, and only that callback's own variables are sent 5. On http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=users the same drop zone accepts the same CSV, by drag or by click, and is now reachable by keyboard 6. The controls now pick up the dashboard's own tokens, so styling them is a single global change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at 3170fff768 against a live proxy on :4000, with the dashboard dev server on :3000. Two behaviours here are worth more than a screenshot, because both would have shipped a silent data bug. **The edit form must not post fields it never rendered.** antd's Form submits only the fields it rendered. react-hook-form returns everything `reset()` seeded, so a Langfuse edit would also have posted `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ""` and `OPENMETER_API_KEY: ""` to `/config/update`, blanking a configured Slack webhook. `shouldUnregister: true` fixes it, and the payload test pins the exact object: ``` with shouldUnregister npm test -- settings 14 passed without it 1 failed "should post the edited callback variables when the edit modal is saved" ``` **Saving alert webhooks reads the DOM by input name.** `handleSaveAlerts` looks each webhook up with `document.querySelector('input[name=...]')`, so swapping the input primitive can break it without any type error. That path had no test at all: ``` against Tremor TextInput passes against shadcn Input passes with name={key} removed fails ``` Measured in the running page: ``` tabs: 5, each with a unique value; two used to share value="2" active panel mounted: 1 of 5 both dialogs: 800px, internal scroll, clamp cleanly at 1280x600 icon geometry: 30 / 20 / 16 px, nothing at the lucide 24px default cell overflow: 0, no horizontal page scroll combobox: opens with 16 options; picking Datadog renders API Key and Site empty submit: "Please enter the api key", "Please enter the site" CSV drop: parses end to end, 1 of 1 users valid drop zone border: gray -> blue -> gray across dragover and dragleave label[for] unresolved: 0 ``` Local gates: ``` npm run build exit 0 npm run test 654 files, 7162 tests passed grep -rn "antd|@ant-design|@tremor" <both files> no matches npx eslint --pass-on-unpruned-suppressions <4 changed files> 0 errors, 21 warnings, all pre-existing npx prettier --check <4 changed files + suppressions> all match ``` `package.json` and the lockfile are untouched; `react-hook-form` was already a dependency. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - Two tabs shared `value="2"`; Tremor matched panels by index so it never showed - Base UI matches by value, so all five tabs needed unique slugs - The callback search matches the callback id, not its display name, exactly as antd did - `Input.Password`'s reveal toggle is gone; shadcn has no password-reveal primitive - The callback form's labels are vertical now, not antd's 24 column grid - Left alone as pre-existing: eight alert switches share one id, and an anchor sits inside a button - Left alone as pre-existing: Download CSV Template has no click handler ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(databricks): surface prompt-cache token counts in streaming usage
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streamed Databricks Claude responses lose prompt-cache token counts - Cache-aware pricing never applies, so cached requests bill at full input rate - Prompt tokens come from estimation, understating real usage by ~41% How it solves it: - Pass the streaming chunk's usage object through to the caller ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming a Databricks-served Claude model sees cache savings disappear from spend 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Databricks Claude deployment with `"stream": true`, `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}`, and a large system block marked for caching 2. The trailing SSE chunk carries a usage object with no cache breakdown at all, reporting `"prompt_tokens": 10416` 3. They send the identical request again so the cache is warm. The trailing usage chunk is unchanged, still with no cache fields 4. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and both requests are costed at the full input rate, as though nothing was cached After: the same two requests report the cache split, and spend follows it 1. They send the same POST as above 2. The trailing usage chunk now reports `"prompt_tokens": 17613` alongside `"cache_creation_input_tokens": 17603` 3. They send the identical request again. The trailing usage chunk now reports `"cache_read_input_tokens": 17603` 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs costs the second request at the cache-read rate rather than the full input rate ## Relevant issues Fixes #36933 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a self-hosted proxy in front of Azure Databricks Foundation Model APIs, hitting `system.ai.claude-opus-5` for real. Both runs use the same request body and the same command, and both cost real money Request body, written once and reused for every call below: ```sh python3 - <<'PY' import json corpus = "databricks streaming cache proof corpus for litellm pr verification. " * 800 json.dump({ "model": "claude-opus", "max_tokens": 8, "stream": True, "stream_options": {"include_usage": True}, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": corpus, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}]}, {"role": "user", "content": "Reply OK."}, ], "disable_fallbacks": True, "num_retries": 0, }, open("proof_payload.json", "w")) PY ``` Command, run twice so the first call populates the cache and the second reads it: ```sh for pass in cold warm; do printf '%-6s ' "$pass" curl -s -X POST "$LLM_HOST/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LLM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d @proof_payload.json \ | grep '"usage"' | tail -1 | sed 's/^data: //' | jq -c '.usage' done ``` **Before**, at `v1.96.0` unmodified (tag `v1.96.0`, commit `8843766`): ``` cold {"completion_tokens":1,"prompt_tokens":10416,"total_tokens":10417,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0}} warm {"completion_tokens":0,"prompt_tokens":10416,"total_tokens":10416,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0}} ``` No `prompt_tokens_details` on either call, and the warm call is indistinguishable from the cold one **After**, with this PR's change applied (commit `ce66cbc`): ``` cold {"completion_tokens":4,"prompt_tokens":17613,"total_tokens":17617,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0,"cache_write_tokens":17603,"cache_creation_tokens":17603},"cache_creation_input_tokens":17603,"cache_read_input_tokens":0} warm {"completion_tokens":4,"prompt_tokens":17613,"total_tokens":17617,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":17603,"cache_write_tokens":0,"cache_creation_tokens":0},"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":17603} ``` The cold call now reports a cache write and the warm call a cache read of the same 17,603 tokens Worth calling out separately: `prompt_tokens` corrects from 10,416 to 17,613 on a byte-identical payload. With no usage object reaching the caller, token counts were being estimated rather than read from the provider, so streamed Databricks spend was understated by roughly 41% on top of losing the cache split entirely One honesty note on how the after-run was captured. Building the full image from this branch needs the Rust extension and the admin UI bundle, which was not practical in the environment I had, so the after-run applied this PR's single added line over an otherwise byte-identical `v1.96.0` copy of the affected module, verified by SHA-256 against the pristine file before replacement. The code path exercised is exactly what this PR changes, and nothing else in that module differs. Happy to re-capture from a clean branch build if you would rather see that ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only affects the Databricks provider's streaming path - After-run captured as a single-line overlay on v1.96.0, not a branch build ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(databricks): replay extended thinking as a reasoning content block
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Multi-turn extended thinking on Databricks Claude fails outright - Two internal message keys leak into the request and get rejected - Any agent replaying its own thinking breaks on the second turn How it solves it: - Convert those keys into the reasoning content block Databricks accepts ## User Flow Before: a developer building a multi-turn agent on a Databricks-served Claude model cannot get past the second turn 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Databricks Claude deployment with extended thinking enabled, and get a normal answer back 2. They append that assistant reply verbatim to their message list, exactly as the API returned it, and add a follow-up question 3. They send the second POST and get back `400 BAD_REQUEST` reading `messages.1.reasoning_content: Extra inputs are not permitted` 4. Their only workarounds are to turn extended thinking off, or to strip the reasoning out of every assistant turn by hand and lose the reasoning chain After: the same conversation continues for as many turns as they like 1. They send the same first POST and get the same answer 2. They append the assistant reply verbatim and add a follow-up question 3. The second POST returns 200 with an answer that builds on the first 4. They keep going, appending each reply verbatim, and turn three also returns 200 ## Relevant issues Fixes #36931 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a self-hosted proxy in front of Azure Databricks Foundation Model APIs, hitting `system.ai.claude-opus-5` for real. Each run holds a three turn conversation, appending every assistant reply back verbatim, and costs real money ```py # turn 1, then append the reply verbatim and ask a follow-up, twice base = {"model": "claude-opus", "max_tokens": 1200, "thinking": {"type": "adaptive"}, "output_config": {"effort": "medium"}, "disable_fallbacks": True, "num_retries": 0} t1 = {**base, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 * 23? Reason briefly."}]} a1 = post(t1)["choices"][0]["message"] t2 = {**base, "messages": [t1["messages"][0], a1, {"role": "user", "content": "Now double that result."}]} a2 = post(t2)["choices"][0]["message"] t3 = {**base, "messages": t2["messages"] + [a2, {"role": "user", "content": "And subtract 82."}]} post(t3) ``` **Before**, at `v1.96.0` unmodified (tag `v1.96.0`, commit `8843766`): ``` turn 1 OK. assistant message carries: ['content', 'role', 'thinking_blocks'] turn 2 REJECTED: litellm.BadRequestError: DatabricksException - {"error_code":"BAD_REQUEST", "message":"{\"message\":\"messages.1.reasoning_content: Extra inputs are not permitted\"}"} ``` **After**, with this PR's change applied (commit `cbdf711`): ``` turn 1 OK, answer: **391** Quick reasoning: 17 × 23 = 17 × (20 + 3) = 340 + 51 turn 2 OK, answer: **782** 391 × 2 = 782. turn 3 OK, answer: **700** 782 − 82 = 700. ``` Each turn builds on the last, so the reasoning chain survives the round trip rather than being silently discarded ### How the accepted shape was established Rather than guess, I captured a real signed reasoning block from the live endpoint and replayed it in every candidate format: | Assistant content block shape | Result | | --- | --- | | `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": ..., "signature": ...}` (Anthropic native) | rejected, `Failed to parse ContentItem` | | `{"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"type": "reasoning_text", ...}], "encrypted_content": ...}` | rejected, `Expecting one non-null Summary` | | `{"type": "reasoning", "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": ..., "signature": ...}]}` | **accepted** | | message-level `thinking_blocks` (current behaviour) | rejected, `Extra inputs are not permitted` | Further constraints, each verified the same way: exactly one reasoning block per message and exactly one `summary_text` entry inside it, since two of either is rejected. The `signature` is mandatory. The text may be empty, which matters because Databricks returns an empty thinking string alongside the signature The accepted shape is the one the existing test in `tests/test_litellm/llms/databricks/chat/test_databricks_chat_transformation.py` already asserts, and the one the provider's own response parsing produces. Worth flagging that Databricks' published docs for multi-turn reasoning describe the `content` / `reasoning_text` / `encrypted_content` shape, which the endpoint actively refuses One honesty note on how the after-run was captured. Building the full image from this branch needs the Rust extension and the admin UI bundle, which was not practical in the environment I had, so the after-run applied this PR's changes over an otherwise byte-identical `v1.96.0` copy of the affected module, verified by SHA-256 against the pristine file before replacement. The code path exercised is exactly what this PR changes. Happy to re-capture from a clean branch build if you would rather see that ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Unsigned or redacted thinking blocks are dropped, since they cannot be replayed - Multiple thinking blocks collapse to the first signed one - `reasoning_effort` maps to `thinking.type=enabled`, which opus 5 rejects; unrelated, use adaptive to reproduce ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(ui): render the correct widget for nullable MCP tool schema properties
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Optional MCP tool parameters get no input field in the Tool Testing Playground - The same nullable fields submit with the wrong value type in the chat playground How it solves it: - Resolve JSON Schema's array `type` (e.g. `["string", "null"]`) to its real type - Use that resolved type everywhere a widget or a value conversion depends on it ## User Flow Before: an admin testing an MCP tool with optional parameters in the Tool Testing Playground cannot fill in those parameters at all 1. They open the MCP Servers page, pick a connected server, and open the Tool Testing Playground for a tool with optional parameters (for example an Azure DevOps MCP server's `testplan_test_suite_write`, whose `parentSuiteId` and `name` are optional) 2. Required parameters show a labeled input, but each optional parameter shows only its label and an info icon, with no field to type into 3. signals.title: fix(responses): return 400 for invalid input types
signals.text: ## Summary - Validate Responses API `input` before iterating over it in prompt management. - Raise `BadRequestError` for non-string, non-list input instead of allowing `TypeError` to propagate as a 500. - Added regression tests covering both `responses()` and `aresponses()`. ### Problem this solves: When `input` is a non-string, non-list value such as an integer, float, boolean, `None`, or dictionary, the Responses API attempts to iterate over it during prompt management. This can raise a `TypeError`, which is subsequently surfaced as a 500 error instead of a client-side 400 validation error. ### How it solves it: Validate the type of `input` before iterating over it. Invalid non-string, non-list values now raise `BadRequestError` with a descriptive message, resulting in a 400-level client error instead of a 500 server error. ## User Flow Before: A client sends an invalid numeric `input` to the Responses API and receives a 500 error instead of a client validation error. 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"input": 12345` and a valid model. 2. The request fails while processing the invalid `input` value. 3. The client receives a 500 response containing a `TypeError` rather than a 400 validation error. After: The same invalid request is rejected as a client error with a descriptive validation message. 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"input": 12345` and a valid model. 2. The request is rejected because `input` must be a string or list of input items. 3. The client receives a 400 response with an error message identifying the invalid `input` type. ## Relevant issues Fixes #36923 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
