signal.title: fix(proxy): make /cursor/chat/completions work with Cursor agent mode
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Cursor BYOK against litellm 400d on real Ask and agent requests - OpenAI custom (grammar) tools crashed or silently vanished on litellm's chat surface - gpt-5.4+ function tool chat requests 400d when reasoning defaulted on How it solves it: - cursor endpoint normalizes each tool shape level to canonical chat format - core chat surface gains first-class custom tool call types - responses bridge auto-fires for gpt-5.4+ function tools with reasoning active ## Relevant issues - `/cursor/chat/completions` now handles both request shapes Cursor BYOK sends, so Cursor agent mode works against litellm: Responses-shaped agent-mode bodies (`input`, flat tool defs, custom tools, `reasoning`) and genuine chat-completions bodies (`messages`), always answering in chat completions format - streaming through the endpoint was fully broken (500 on every streaming request) and router-served streams leaked raw Responses API events (including request metadata) instead of chat chunks; both fixed - custom (grammar) tool calls, e.g. Cursor's ApplyPatch, now surface as chat `tool_calls` in both streaming and non-streaming responses, and multi-turn tool round trips complete - Cursor Ask mode sends a genuine chat completions body whose `tools` array mixes nested function tools with a flat Responses-style custom tool (ApplyPatch); the messages arm forwarded that verbatim so OpenAI 400d (`Missing required parameter: 'tools[N].custom'`), and even a correctly nested custom tool failed on the way back: litellm's response parsing 500d non-streaming and silently dropped the tool call when streaming. The messages arm now nests flat tool defs, and OpenAI chat custom tool calls are first-class across litellm's chat surface (non-streaming, streaming deltas, chunk rebuild) - ApplyPatch is grammar-constrained: Cursor ships a Lark grammar in the Responses flat format shape ({"type":"grammar","definition","syntax"}) while chat completions wraps the same fields one level deeper ({"type":"grammar","grammar":{...}}), so the nested envelope alone still 400d (`tools[N].custom.format.grammar`); format shapes and named tool_choice objects now translate across surfaces in both directions. Live captures further show the dialects mix PER LEVEL (Cursor sends a chat-nested envelope whose inner format is still Responses-flat), so the cursor arm normalizes each level independently and idempotently; a parametrized test pins the full envelope x format matrix. Separately, real Cursor gpt-5.6 requests exposed a routing gap in core litellm: OpenAI enables reasoning by default for gpt-5.4+ and Chat Completions rejects function tools whenever reasoning is on, but the existing responses-bridge heuristic only fired when the caller explicitly sent reasoning_effort, so tools requests without it 400d on chat instead of auto-bridging; the heuristic now treats unset effort as reasoning-active and keeps the documented reasoning_effort "none" escape hatch on chat Reference behavior studied from the community Cursor-OpenAI-BYOK-Bridge (`src/byok`): Cursor agent mode POSTs Responses-API-shaped bodies to the chat/completions path while expecting chat-completions SSE back, so the bridge routes those to a Responses upstream and converts the stream back; bodies with `messages` pass through as genuine chat completions ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4395 Resolves LIT-4396 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on `127.0.0.1:4396` backed by Postgres, real provider calls. Before runs captured at `214945a223` (`origin/litellm_internal_staging`), after runs at `90283fab70`. The before runs used real OpenAI; the account ran out of quota mid-verification, so the after runs use real Anthropic through the same pipeline (the streaming and conversion defects are provider-independent; the two OpenAI-specific probes are marked) A. Agent-mode Responses-shaped body with `stream_options` (Cursor sends `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`) ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4396/cursor/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6", "input": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say OK"}], "stream_options": {"include_usage": true} }' # BEFORE (real OpenAI): {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - ... "Unknown parameter: 'stream_options.include_usage'." ...","code":"400"}} # AFTER (claude-sonnet-5): {"finish_reason": "stop", "content": "OK", "object": "chat.completion"} ``` B. Genuine chat-completions body with tool history (what Cursor sends for models whose BYOK it already fixed) ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4396/cursor/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "claude-sonnet-5", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "read a file"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_hist1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": "{"path": "a.py"}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_hist1", "content": "print(42)"}, {"role": "user", "content": "what does it print? answer with just the number"} ], "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}}}}] }' # BEFORE (real OpenAI): {"error":{"message":"... "Invalid type for 'input[1].content': expected one of an array of objects or string, but got null instead." ...","code":"400"}} # AFTER: {"finish_reason": "stop", "content": "42", "model": "claude-sonnet-5", "usage_total": 485} ``` C. Agent-mode streaming with a function tool ``` curl -sN -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4396/cursor/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "claude-sonnet-5", "input": [{"role": "user", "content": "Read the file a.py using the read_file tool."}], "stream": true, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}, "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "read_file", "description": "Read a file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path"]}}], "tool_choice": "required" }' # BEFORE: {"error":{"message":"cursor_chat_completions.<locals>.cursor_data_generator() got an unexpected keyword argument 'request'","code":"500"}} # AFTER: 6 chat.completion.chunk SSE events, then [DONE]: # data: {..."choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","tool_calls":[{"id":"toolu_01GcJXm9WhT3Y6Tq23KthKAS","function":{"arguments":"","name":"read_file"},"type":"function","index":0}]}...} # data: {..."delta":{"tool_calls":[{"function":{"arguments":"{"path": ""},"type":"function","index":0}]}...} # data: {..."delta":{"tool_calls":[{"function":{"arguments":"a"},"type":"function","index":0}]}...} # data: {..."delta":{"tool_calls":[{"function":{"arguments":".py"}"},"type":"function","index":0}]}...} # data: {..."finish_reason":"tool_calls"...} # data: [DONE] ``` The tool call opens at index 0 with the role on the first delta. On the intermediate broken state (generator signature fixed but the class-identity stream gate still in place) this same curl returned raw `response.created` / `response.output_item.added` / `response.completed` Responses events to the client, including litellm request metadata inside `response.created` D. Multi-turn tool round trip (Cursor echoes `function_call` and `function_call_output` items keyed by `call_id`) ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4396/cursor/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "claude-sonnet-5", "input": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Read the file a.py using the read_file tool, then tell me what it prints. Answer with just the number."}, {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "toolu_01GcJXm9WhT3Y6Tq23KthKAS", "name": "read_file", "arguments": "{"path": "a.py"}"}, {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "toolu_01GcJXm9WhT3Y6Tq23KthKAS", "output": "print(42)"} ], "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "read_file", "description": "Read a file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path"]}}] }' # BEFORE: {"error":{"message":"Unknown items in responses API response: [GenericResponseOutputItem(type='message', ..., content=[OutputText(type='output_text', text='42', ...)], ...)]","code":"500"}} # AFTER: {"finish_reason": "stop", "content": "42", "usage_total": 518} ``` E. Custom (grammar) tool call, the shape Cursor agent mode uses for ApplyPatch (real OpenAI, non-streaming; captured before quota ran out) ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4396/cursor/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6", "input": [{"role": "user", "content": "Create hello.txt containing hello world using the ApplyPatch tool."}], "reasoning": {"effort": "low"}, "tools": [{"type": "custom", "name": "ApplyPatch", "description": "Apply a file patch in V4A diff format"}], "tool_choice": "required" }' # BEFORE: the model called the tool upstream (real tokens billed) but the client received {"finish_reason": null, "content": null, "tool_calls": null} # AFTER (real OpenAI, live gateway running this branch): 200, finish_reason "tool_calls", tool call {"function": {"name": "ApplyPatch", "arguments": "*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: main.py
@@
+def hello():
..."}, "type": "function"}; the owed live re-run of this probe is done ``` F. Ask-mode messages body with a flat custom tool def (the exact shape a real Cursor Ask request sent through a live gateway running the pre-fix branch; request IDs in the gateway logs) ``` curl -s -X POST $PROXY/cursor/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "use ApplyPatch to add a hello() function to main.py"}], "tools": [ {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "description": "Read a file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path"]}}}, {"type": "custom", "name": "ApplyPatch", "description": "Apply a V4A format patch to a file"} ], "tool_choice": "required" }' # BEFORE (real OpenAI): {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Missing required parameter: 'tools[1].custom'.. ...","param":"tools[1].custom","code":"400"}} # AFTER: 200, tool_calls: [{"id": "call_...", "type": "custom", "custom": {"name": "ApplyPatch", "input": "*** Begin Patch..."}}], finish_reason "tool_calls" ``` G. Correctly nested custom tool through plain `/v1/chat/completions` (proves the response-side break is core litellm, not endpoint-specific) ``` curl -s -X POST $PROXY/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "use ApplyPatch to add a hello() function to main.py"}], "tools": [{"type": "custom", "custom": {"name": "ApplyPatch", "description": "Apply a V4A format patch to a file"}}], "tool_choice": "required" }' # BEFORE (real OpenAI): {"error":{"message":"litellm.InternalServerError: ... TypeError: ChatCompletionMessageToolCall.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'function' (convert_dict_to_response.py:650)"}} # AFTER: 200 with the custom tool call intact ``` H. Same body with `"stream": true` (the worst pre-fix behavior: silent data loss, not an error) ``` # BEFORE (real OpenAI): 200 SSE stream with finish_reason "tool_calls" and ZERO tool_call deltas; usage reports 68 completion tokens that never reached the client # AFTER: first delta carries {"id", "type": "custom", "custom": {"name": "ApplyPatch", "input": ""}}, continuation deltas carry {"custom": {"input": ...}} fragments, then finish_reason "tool_calls" and [DONE] ``` I. Grammar-constrained ApplyPatch (the real Cursor Ask-mode shape: flat grammar format inside the flat custom tool) ``` curl -s -X POST $PROXY/cursor/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "use ApplyPatch to add hello() to main.py"}], "tools": [{"type": "custom", "name": "ApplyPatch", "description": "Apply a V4A patch", "format": {"type": "grammar", "syntax": "lark", "definition": "start: begin_patch ..."}}], "tool_choice": "required" }' # BEFORE (real OpenAI, gateway at the previous commit): {"error":{"message":"... Missing required parameter: 'tools[0].custom.format.grammar'...","code":"400"}} # Contract control (real OpenAI, same gateway): manually moving definition/syntax under format.grammar returns 200 with a proper grammar-constrained ApplyPatch tool call # AFTER: the gateway performs that exact rewrite; re-run the curl above on the redeployed branch to confirm 200 ``` Named tool_choice objects follow the same surface split (Responses flat {"type":"custom","name"} vs chat nested {"type":"custom","custom":{"name"}}); the cursor arm nests flat ones, and both bridges translate them alongside the tool defs they reference (unit-pinned; live probe rides the same redeploy) J. The exact shape real Cursor Ask mode sends (live-captured): pre-nested envelope carrying a FLAT grammar format ``` curl -s -X POST $PROXY/cursor/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "use ApplyPatch to add hello() to main.py"}], "tools": [{"type": "custom", "custom": {"name": "ApplyPatch", "description": "Apply a V4A patch", "format": {"type": "grammar", "definition": "start: begin_patch ...", "syntax": "lark"}}}], "tool_choice": "required" }' # BEFORE (real OpenAI, gateway at the prior commit): 400 Missing required parameter: 'tools[0].custom.format.grammar' (the prior commit translated format only on the flat-envelope path) # AFTER: the format level is normalized regardless of which envelope shape it arrived in; re-run on the redeployed branch to confirm 200 ``` The reference community BYOK bridge was checked as prior art and performs no tool normalization on its chat path (messages bodies forward verbatim), so these hybrid shapes have no reference handling to mirror; the per-level matrix test is the contract K. Function tools on gpt-5.6 without an explicit reasoning_effort (real Cursor agent shape; reproduces on plain /v1/chat/completions, so this was a core litellm gap, not a cursor-endpoint one) ``` curl -s -X POST $PROXY/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "read a.py"}], "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}}}}] }' # BEFORE (real OpenAI): 400 Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-5.6 ... use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to 'none' # (litellm forwarded to chat completions because the bridge heuristic required an explicit reasoning_effort; OpenAI applies reasoning by default server-side) # AFTER: the responses bridge auto-activates for gpt-5.4+ with tools unless reasoning_effort is explicitly "none"; the request is served via /v1/responses with reasoning intact and returns chat-shaped output; re-run on the redeployed branch to confirm 200 ``` Control (stays green before and after): history round trip with a nested custom tool_call plus its tool result through `/v1/chat/completions` returns 200 (litellm forwards custom tool_calls in request history untouched; OpenAI accepts them) Raw wire shapes these fixes encode were captured live through the `/openai` passthrough (non-streaming message and the streaming delta sequence) and are pinned verbatim in the regression tests Negative control: every other `/cursor/*` path still reaches the Cloud Agents passthrough ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4396/cursor/v0/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" # BEFORE and AFTER: {"detail":"Cursor API key not found. Add Cursor credentials via the UI ..."} ``` Spend note: SpendLogs rows land for every request above; the Responses-pipeline rows log zero cost, which is pre-existing and tracked in #30126 with open PR #30277 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - route (`cursor_chat_completions`): bodies with `messages` run through the standard chat completions pipeline untouched (the old blind `messages` to `input` rename broke tool history and chat tool defs); Responses-shaped bodies keep the `aresponses` pipeline with chat-completions-only `stream_options` stripped - `cursor_data_generator` accepts the `request` kwarg the processor passes (every streaming request 500d without it) and detects streams by `__anext__` instead of a class check that the router's `HiddenParamsAsyncIteratorWrapper` defeats (which leaked raw Responses events, metadata included, to clients) - streaming converter: `custom_tool_call` output items and `custom_tool_call_input.delta` events become chat `tool_calls` deltas; tool_call indices are remapped per-stream to 0-based sequential (Responses `output_index` counts reasoning and message items, so the first tool call of a reasoning model arrived at index 1 or higher and strict SSE accumulators misplace it); `response.completed` reports `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` for `custom_tool_call` items too. The finish check deliberately covers exactly the item types the stream converter emits tool_call deltas for; reporting tool_calls for item types never streamed (e.g. the native apply_patch tool, unhandled in the stream converter before and after this PR) would hand the client a tool_calls finish with an empty tool_calls array - non-streaming converter: typed `ResponseCustomToolCall` items and litellm's own `GenericResponseOutputItem` pydantic items (what the completion bridge emits for non-Responses-native providers behind the router) convert to chat output instead of being dropped; dropping the latter raised "Unknown items in responses API response" on every router-bridged non-streaming completion through this endpoint - messages arm (`cursor_chat_completions`): flat Responses-style tool defs in a chat body are nested into the chat completions shape (`{"type": "custom", "name", ...}` to `{"type": "custom", "custom": {...}}`, same for flat function defs) and published through `_safe_set_request_parsed_body` so the delegated `chat_completion` reads the normalized body from the request-scope cache; bodies whose tools are already chat-shaped skip the cache write entirely - core chat surface: OpenAI chat completions custom tool calls are now first-class. New `ChatCompletionMessageCustomToolCall` / `ChatCompletionDeltaCustomToolCall` sibling types mirror the installed openai SDK union (separate classes so function tool call dumps gain no `custom` key and custom dumps carry no `function` key), a single `chat_completion_tool_call_from_dict` dispatch feeds the three provider-dict sinks (`Message.__init__`, `convert_to_model_response_object`, `_transform_choices`), and `Delta.__init__` dispatches streamed dicts on the `custom` key so both stream re-parse sites (`chunk_creator`, `return_processed_chunk_logic`) stop swallowing custom deltas via their except branches - consumers that assume `.function` were audited and the unguarded ones now skip custom entries: the json-mode gate `_should_convert_tool_call_to_json_mode` (single chokepoint for all three json-mode callers), `_handle_invalid_parallel_tool_calls`, helicone and lunary logging; the chunk builder accumulates `custom.input` fragments so spend logging and `stream_chunk_builder` rebuild the full custom call - chat to responses bridge (`_convert_tools_to_responses_format`): nested chat custom tools are flattened to the Responses flat shape instead of being forwarded nested (the mirror-image gap, hit when a chat body with custom tools targets a Responses-bridged model) - the cursor messages arm normalizes tool shapes PER LEVEL, not per whole-tool template: the envelope level (flat def nested under `custom`/`function`) and the format level (flat grammar wrapped as `format.grammar`) are normalized independently and idempotently, so hybrids like a pre-nested envelope with a flat grammar inside land canonical; every envelope x format combination is pinned by a parametrized test - custom tool `format` shape translation: shared helper pair in `prompt_templates/common_utils` (`convert_custom_tool_format_to_chat_shape` / `convert_custom_tool_format_to_responses_shape`) wraps or unwraps the grammar object; applied on the cursor messages arm (flat to chat) and the chat to responses bridge (chat to flat); `{"type": "text"}` is identical on both surfaces and passes through, as does anything unrecognized - named tool_choice translation follows the tool defs on every surface: the cursor messages arm nests flat Responses-style tool_choice objects, `_normalize_tool_choice_for_responses_api` flattens chat custom tool_choice exactly like its existing function arm, and `_transform_tool_choice` on the responses to chat bridge maps custom tool_choice to a function tool_choice because that bridge downgrades custom tools to function tools (a custom choice would reference a tool type absent from the converted request) - core responses-bridge heuristic (`responses_api_bridge_check`): for gpt-5.4+ on openai/azure with FUNCTION tools, unset `reasoning_effort` now bridges to the Responses API (OpenAI defaults reasoning on server-side, so the chat request was unservable) and explicit `"none"` stays on chat completions (OpenAI's documented escape hatch; the old code over-bridged that cell). The gate requires a function-type tool specifically: custom-only requests are served natively by chat completions with reasoning on (live-proven 200) and keep the native custom tool_call response shape rather than the bridge's function-shaped mapping; the pre-existing arm shared the any-tools coarseness and is fixed by the same leg. Two prior test pins asserting tools-without-reasoning stays chat encoded the unservable behavior and are flipped with the rationale in their docstrings - cursor input arm gains the mirror of the messages-arm normalization: chat-nested tool envelopes, chat-nested grammar formats, and chat-nested object tool_choice are flattened to the Responses dialect before dispatch (previously an object-form tool_choice in a Responses-shaped body reached OpenAI in the wrong nesting); the mirror envelope x format matrix is pinned parametrically - the bridge gate resolves the effective OpenAI base exactly as the chat handler does (call arg, then `litellm.api_base`, then `OPENAI_BASE_URL`/`OPENAI_API_BASE`, then the default) through one shared `_resolve_openai_api_base`, so a custom base configured only via the global or env is no longer invisible to the gate and misread as the default endpoint; only requests that would actually hit the default OpenAI endpoint (or Azure) are auto-bridged - custom-vs-function classification of a tool-call dict goes through one shared `is_custom_tool_call_dict` (explicit custom type, or a custom payload present) used by both the non-streaming `chat_completion_tool_call_from_dict` and the streaming `Delta` coercion, and the stream assembler classifies from the accumulated custom payload rather than a `type` field continuation chunks never carry; previously the same payload could parse as a custom tool call mid-stream, raise TypeError on the completed message, and be silently dropped from the assembled message. The tool envelope converter now extracts payload fields from both the nested dict and the top level (nested first) instead of treating a present nested dict as the exclusive source, so an empty nested envelope no longer drops a top-level name, and a nameless envelope passes through unchanged What does not change: every other `/cursor/*` path still passes through to the Cursor Cloud Agents API; the `/v1/responses` endpoints are untouched; the tool-index remap only activates when the per-stream map is passed, so the stateless guardrail caller of the same translate function keeps its existing behavior; function tool call parsing, serialization, and streaming shapes are byte-identical to before (pinned by the pre-existing exact-dict tests, all green); the Responses-arm mapping of custom tool calls to function-shaped chat tool calls is unchanged; the bridge heuristic for pre-5.4 GPT-5 names and the reasoning-summary arm are unchanged. One consequence worth noting: the auto-bridge applies only when the resolved base is the default OpenAI endpoint (or the provider is Azure); OpenAI-compatible backends reached through a custom api_base, whether passed per-call or configured via `litellm.api_base` or `OPENAI_BASE_URL`/`OPENAI_API_BASE`, are never auto-bridged, and reasoning_effort "none" remains the per-request escape hatch on the default endpoint ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches core chat/Responses bridging, proxy routing, and gpt-5.4+ auto-routing; behavior changes are broad but heavily test-covered, with the main regression risk being mis-routing OpenAI-compatible backends or altering tool-call shapes clients depend on. > > **Overview** > **Cursor BYOK** on `/cursor/chat/completions` now branches on body shape: real `messages` bodies delegate to normal chat completions (with per-level normalization of flat Responses-style `tools` / `tool_choice` and grammar `format` into chat shapes); Responses-shaped `input` bodies still go through `aresponses` with `stream_options` stripped without mutating the cached request body. Streaming fixes include accepting the `request` kwarg, detecting streams via `__anext__` (not a brittle class check), and converting Responses events to chat SSE. **`GET /cursor/models`** and **`/cursor/v1/models`** delegate to the standard model list so BYOK key verification works. > > **Custom (grammar) tools** are first-class on the chat surface: new custom tool call types, `chat_completion_tool_call_from_dict` / `is_custom_tool_call_dict`, streaming delta assembly and chunk rebuild for `custom.input`, and Responses↔chat bridges for `custom_tool_call` items (including sequential tool_call index remapping and `custom_tool_call_input.delta`). Helicone/Lunary logging and related paths handle custom payloads. > > **gpt-5.4+ routing:** `responses_api_bridge_check` shares `_resolve_openai_api_base` with the chat handler and auto-bridges **function** tools when reasoning is active (including unset effort on real OpenAI/Azure), while **custom-only** tool sets stay on chat and `reasoning_effort: "none"` remains the chat escape hatch. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit eea9bb1497d69ed16fcc022a51bc81d6048da735. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: feat(lint): exempt TypedDict-annotated dict literals from LIT002
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Building a TypedDict value as a dict literal tripped LIT002 - Escapes were `MyTD(a=1)` calls or `# mutable-ok` suppressions - Constructor calls cannot express keys that are not identifiers How it solves it: - Exempts dict literals assigned with a TypedDict annotation, like `x: Final[MyTD] = {...}` - Bare `x: Final = {...}` names no type and stays flagged - Nested dict literals share the exemption; other construction inside still counts - Detection is name-based: Final/ClassVar/Optional/Annotated unwrap, PEP 604 unions qualify through either arm, mutable heads and Mapping/Any/object never qualify - Ratchets the LIT002 budget down by the 234 violations this clears ## User Flow Before: a contributor who builds a fixed-shape TypedDict payload with a dict literal gets an LIT002 lint failure and must suppress or rewrite 1. They add `x: Final[MyTD] = {"a": 1}` to a file under `litellm/`, where `MyTD` is a TypedDict 2. They stage the file and run `make check` 3. The type-discipline gate fails with `LIT002 mutable dict literal: this builds a collection that can be grown or rewritten`, pointing at the annotated line; pushing anyway turns the CI lint job red with the same message 4. To land the change they either append `# mutable-ok: <reason>` to the line or rewrite the payload as `MyTD(a=1)`, which cannot express keys that are not valid identifiers After: the same annotated dict literal passes lint, while an unannotated `Final` dict literal still fails 1. They add `x: Final[MyTD] = {"a": 1}` to a file under `litellm/`, where `MyTD` is a TypedDict 2. They stage the file and run `make check` 3. The type-discipline gate reports `OK: every LIT rule is within its codebase ceiling`, and the CI lint job stays green 4. A sibling line `y: Final = {"a": 1}` still fails with LIT002, whose message now also names the fix: `a TypedDict-annotated dict literal (x: Final[MyTD] = {...})` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? signal.title: fix(langfuse): restrict trace steering keys to real langfuse trace fields
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A team member can pull the team's Langfuse credentials out of a trace - `update_trace_keys` lets the caller name any request-metadata key - The named value is copied onto the trace unfiltered How it solves it: - `update_trace_keys` does nothing unless an operator enables it - `langfuse_enable_update_trace_keys`, default off - Enabling it restores the previous behaviour exactly ## User Flow Before: any holder of a team key can read the team's Langfuse credentials out of a trace they create 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"metadata": {"existing_trace_id": "t-1", "update_trace_keys": ["user_api_key_auth"]}` and get a normal 200 2. They open that trace in the Langfuse project their team already logs to 3. The trace carries a `user_api_key_auth` field holding the resolved auth object, including the team's `callback_vars`, its hashed key token, budgets and team config 4. A member with no admin rights on the gateway now holds the team's logging destination credentials After: the same request succeeds and copies nothing 1. They send the same POST and get the same 200 2. The trace is created or continued as before, with no `user_api_key_auth` field on it 3. An operator who wants trace continuation sets `langfuse_enable_update_trace_keys: true` under `litellm_settings`, and every previously documented key works again ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5484 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, real Postgres, real Gemini calls, Langfuse pointed at a local sink that records the outbound bytes. A marker credential sits in the team row's `callback_vars`. The same request is sent to both legs, naming the auth object and a documented continuation key together. ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4483/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAMKEY" \ -d '{"model":"gemini-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}], "metadata":{"existing_trace_id":"t-1", "update_trace_keys":["user_api_key_auth","trace_release"], "trace_release":"v9"}}' ``` Default, at `3ec42fbad2`: ``` HTTP 200 auth_copied=False release=None secret_on_trace=False ``` With `litellm_settings: langfuse_enable_update_trace_keys: true`: ``` HTTP 200 auth_copied=True release='v9' secret_on_trace=True ``` The second leg is the old behaviour, unchanged, now reachable only by operator choice. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Trace continuation is off until an operator opts in - Enabling it restores the credential exposure, by design - Independent of #36744, which closes the same leak on the payload channel ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 3ec42fbad2747568b9844310189c7189467bb0ee. signal.title: feat(bedrock): forward LiteLLM identity and metadata into Bedrock requestMetadata
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock spend cannot be attributed to a LiteLLM key or team - LiteLLM identity is never forwarded into Bedrock request metadata - Invoke has no request-metadata support at all How it solves it: - Opt-in allow-list forwards identity into Bedrock request metadata - Converse body plus a signed header on both Invoke paths - Identity gets its slots first, caller keys fill the rest ## User Flow Before: a platform team paying one shared AWS bill for Bedrock cannot tell which LiteLLM team spent what, so chargeback stalls 1. A developer on the `platform-eng` team sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bedrock-converse"` using their virtual key, and attaches `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"cost_center":"cc-42"}` 2. The call returns 200 and a normal completion 3. The finance owner opens AWS Cost Explorer, groups Bedrock cost by request metadata, and finds nothing to group on: no key, no team, no cost centre reaches AWS 4. The same request on `"model": "bedrock-invoke"` and on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages behaves identically, so no Bedrock surface carries attribution 5. Reconciling the AWS bill against LiteLLM's own spend report means exporting proxy logs and joining them by timestamp After: the same requests carry the key alias, the team alias and the caller's cost centre into the AWS billing record, so Cost Explorer can group Bedrock spend by team 1. The proxy admin adds `bedrock_request_metadata_fields` to `litellm_settings` naming the fields to forward, then restarts the proxy 2. The same developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bedrock-converse"` and the same `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` header 3. The call still returns 200 and a normal completion 4. The finance owner groups Bedrock cost in AWS Cost Explorer and sees `user_api_key_alias=chargeback-demo-key`, `user_api_key_team_alias=platform-eng` and `cost_center=cc-42` on that spend 5. The same request on `"model": "bedrock-invoke"` and on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages produces the same attribution, so every Bedrock surface reconciles 6. A developer who tries to pass `user_api_key_org_alias` in their own metadata header cannot: that name is reserved, their value is dropped, and it never reaches the billing record ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5327 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs captured at `eb71df5cbe`. No AWS credentials are reachable from this environment (`grep -ic aws .env` returns 0 against a positive control of 2 for `api_key`), so a local HTTP server stood in for the Bedrock runtime endpoint and recorded every outbound request in full. What is MEASURED here is the real wire body, the real outbound headers and the real SigV4 `SignedHeaders` list produced by the proxy. What is SIMULATED is only Bedrock's acceptance of them. Setup, identical for both runs, with a Postgres on a namespaced port so the key and team aliases are real rows rather than fixtures: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/team/new \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5327-master" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_alias":"platform-eng"}' # -> {"team_id":"3a300c89-dcfb-4258-a13a-93c1905c9dc0","team_alias":"platform-eng",...} curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/key/generate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5327-master" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"key_alias":"chargeback-demo-key","team_id":"3a300c89-dcfb-4258-a13a-93c1905c9dc0","models":["bedrock-converse","bedrock-invoke"]}' # -> {"key":"sk-A-ExK5ZiL4IJh01UW7PQIg",...} ``` The three requests, driven identically against both configs. Note the caller deliberately tries to forge a proxy-namespaced key in leg 1: ```bash # 1. Converse, /v1/chat/completions (metadata variable name is `metadata` on this route) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-A-ExK5ZiL4IJh01UW7PQIg" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"cost_center":"cc-42","user_api_key_org_alias":"forged-by-caller"}' \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-converse","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"user":"end-user-7"}' # 2. Invoke, /v1/chat/completions curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-A-ExK5ZiL4IJh01UW7PQIg" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"cost_center":"cc-42"}' \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-invoke","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' # 3. Invoke, /v1/messages (metadata variable name is `litellm_metadata` on this route) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4327/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-A-ExK5ZiL4IJh01UW7PQIg" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -H 'x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata: {"cost_center":"cc-42"}' \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-invoke","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` BEFORE, no `bedrock_request_metadata_fields` in `litellm_settings`. All three return `http=200` and nothing is forwarded, which is the negative control for default-off: ``` PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1%3A0/converse [Converse body] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = None SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0/invoke [Invoke, /v1/chat/completions] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = None SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0/invoke [Invoke, /v1/messages] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = None SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date ``` AFTER, with the allow-list set: ```yaml litellm_settings: bedrock_request_metadata_fields: - user_api_key_alias - user_api_key_team_alias - user_api_key_end_user_id - spend_logs_metadata ``` ``` PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1%3A0/converse [Converse body] body.requestMetadata = {"user_api_key_alias": "chargeback-demo-key", "user_api_key_team_alias": "platform-eng", "user_api_key_end_user_id": "end-user-7", "cost_center": "cc-42"} X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = None SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0/invoke [Invoke, /v1/chat/completions] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = {"user_api_key_alias":"chargeback-demo-key","user_api_key_team_alias":"platform-eng","cost_center":"cc-42"} SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date;x-amzn-bedrock-request-metadata PATH /model/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0/invoke [Invoke, /v1/messages] body.requestMetadata = null X-Amzn-Bedrock-Request-Metadata = {"user_api_key_alias":"chargeback-demo-key","user_api_key_team_alias":"platform-eng","cost_center":"cc-42"} SigV4 SignedHeaders = content-type;host;x-amz-date;x-amzn-bedrock-request-metadata ``` Three things to read off that capture. The header lands inside the SigV4 signature on both Invoke legs, which is what Bedrock requires for `X-Amzn-Bedrock-*`. Leg 3 works at all only because the resolver reads `litellm_metadata`, since `/v1/messages` is a `LITELLM_METADATA_ROUTES` route where the plain `metadata` key does not exist. And the `user_api_key_org_alias` the caller tried to forge in leg 1 is absent from the outbound body, so the reserved namespace holds on the wire and not just in unit tests. The full recorded Converse body, so the field is visible in place rather than as a summary: ```json { "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "hi"}]}], "inferenceConfig": {}, "requestMetadata": { "user_api_key_alias": "chargeback-demo-key", "user_api_key_team_alias": "platform-eng", "user_api_key_end_user_id": "end-user-7", "cost_center": "cc-42" } } ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Cost Explorer grouping is advisory on client keys, trustworthy on identity - Shared Vertex and Bedrock billing-label helper is deliberate follow-up - A concurrent PR edits the same import block - No admin UI: no generic editor for `litellm_settings` exists ## Notes for the reviewer Security bounds, since this forwards caller-influenced strings into an AWS billing record. `spend_logs_metadata` arrives from the `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` request header and is fully caller-controlled, so any virtual key holder can write chosen strings into CloudTrail and into the dimension AWS bills on, which is a different retention, access and deletion boundary than LiteLLM's own spend logs. The bounds are that the whole feature defaults off, the forwarded field set is an operator allow-list, the entire `user_api_key_` prefix is reserved against caller keys rather than only the fields the proxy happens to set, the client slot budget is capped explicitly at 16 minus the reserved count so the ordering invariant survives a refactor that reorders the merge, auto-injected values that violate Bedrock's constraints are dropped rather than sanitised or rejected, and `user_api_key_user_email` is separately opt-in because it is PII crossing into an audit store the AWS account retains on its own schedule. Cost Explorer grouping should be read as trustworthy on the reserved identity keys and advisory on every client key, since the caller cannot be relied on for uniqueness or truthfulness of anything they supply. Drop rather than raise, for auto-injected values only. `_validate_request_metadata` raises `BadRequestError`, which stays exactly as it is for a value the caller typed. Applying it to auto-injected identity would turn a working request into a 400 the moment an operator flips the setting on, for something as ordinary as a team alias with an apostrophe. Sanitising is worse than dropping, because a silently rewritten attribution key still looks authoritative in the billing report. No admin UI, deliberately. Repo convention is that a new user-facing setting should be reachable from the dashboard. This one is a global `litellm_settings` key and there is no generic editor for arbitrary `litellm_settings` keys today, so the alternative would be a purpose-built field for a single boolean-ish list. Reading this as a missed requirement would be wrong. Bedrock-local resolver rather than a shared Vertex and Bedrock lift, deliberately. Vertex does something structurally similar in `vertex_request_labels_from_litellm_params`, but it forwards only client-supplied `requester_metadata` and no proxy identity at all, which `grep -rl user_api_key --include="*.py" litellm/llms/vertex_ai/` confirms returns zero files against a control of two for `requester_metadata`. Lifting the resolver would therefore start a brand new PII-into-a-provider-billing-store path for Vertex as a side effect of a refactor, which deserves its own review rather than riding along here. The constraint models do not rhyme either: GCP labels are lowercase-only, 63 characters, up to 64 of them, while Bedrock allows 16 pairs of 256 characters over a class that permits uppercase and `@$#=/+`. The shared lift is real follow-up work, just not this PR. One coordination note: a concurrent PR edits the import block at the top of `litellm/llms/bedrock/messages/invoke_transformations/anthropic_claude3_transformation.py`. This PR only appends one import line there and reorders nothing, but whoever merges second should check the imports by hand rather than trusting a green auto-merge. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(mcp): include server_name and alias in /v1/mcp/server/health response
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #31233 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## What this fixes `GET /v1/mcp/server/health` returned entries with only the opaque SHA-256-derived `server_id` and a `status` — no human-readable identifier. Operators could not tell which server was unhealthy from the API response without reverse-engineering the hashes (see #31233). Both return paths of `health_check_servers` (the `view_all` path and the scoped auth-context path) now include `server_name` and `alias` alongside `server_id`. Both fields are included because each is `Optional` on `LiteLLM_MCPServerTable` — returning both guarantees a human-readable handle whichever one the operator configured. The change is additive, so existing consumers are unaffected. **Before:** ```json [{"server_id": "a3f1bc29d74e8012...", "status": "healthy"}] ``` **After:** ```json [{"server_id": "a3f1bc29d74e8012...", "server_name": "github_onprem", "alias": "github_onprem", "status": "healthy"}] ``` ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Deterministic before/after shown above (shape change on a management endpoint; values come straight from the `LiteLLM_MCPServerTable` records the health-check manager already returns — no inference or LLM call is involved on this endpoint). Tests: 2 new cases in `test_mcp_management_endpoints.py` covering both return paths (`view_all` and scoped auth-contexts, including the de-dup map). Both fail on the unpatched endpoint and pass with the fix. The rest of the file: 139 passed; 1 pre-existing failure (`test_delete_mcp_oauth_user_credential_invalidates_when_record_already_gone`) that also fails on a pristine checkout of the base branch — unrelated to this change. *Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and verified by the author.*

signal.title: fix(access groups): sync assigned_team_ids from the team write paths
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Clearing a team's access groups left it under Attached Teams - The stale entry kept granting that group's models to the team's keys - Only the access-group side ever wrote the team assignment How it solves it: - Team create, update and delete now mirror the change back - The mirror reads the committed team row, so retries heal - Set-based statements under a per-team lock, so concurrent writers converge ## User Flow Before: an admin who removes an access group from a team on the Teams page sees the team still attached to that group, and keys on the team keep the group's models 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=access-groups, open the "premium" group, and add the "accounting" team under Attached Teams 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, edit "accounting", clear its Access Groups field and save 3. They go back to the "premium" group's page and Attached Teams still shows "accounting" 4. The same disagreement is visible over the API: GET https://litellm-domain/v1/access_group/{id} returns `assigned_team_ids: ["<accounting id>"]` while GET https://litellm-domain/team/info?team_id=<accounting id> returns `access_group_ids: []` 5. Deleting "accounting" outright does not clear it either, so the "premium" group lists a team that no longer exists 6. A key issued on "accounting" that carries the "premium" group can still call the models "premium" grants, even though the admin revoked the group from the team After: the removal takes effect on both pages, and the surviving grant goes with it 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=access-groups, open the "premium" group, and add the "accounting" team under Attached Teams 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, edit "accounting", clear its Access Groups field and save 3. They go back to the "premium" group's page and Attached Teams is now empty 4. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/access_group/{id} returns `assigned_team_ids: []` and GET https://litellm-domain/team/info?team_id=<accounting id> returns `access_group_ids: []`, so the two agree 5. Re-adding "premium" to the team from the Teams page puts "accounting" back under Attached Teams, so the sync runs both ways, and deleting the team clears it from every group 6. A key issued on "accounting" that carries the "premium" group no longer receives the models "premium" grants once the admin has revoked the group from the team ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4916 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on port 4916 against a dedicated Postgres 16, same script every leg, master key `sk-1234`. Both legs return 200 with real objects at every step, so the two runs differ only where the fix lands Reproduce with, in order: ``` curl -s -X POST localhost:4916/team/new -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_alias":"accounting"}' curl -s -X POST localhost:4916/v1/access_group -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"access_group_name":"premium","access_model_names":["fake-model"],"assigned_team_ids":["<TEAM_ID>"]}' curl -s -X POST localhost:4916/team/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_id":"<TEAM_ID>","access_group_ids":[]}' curl -s localhost:4916/v1/access_group/<AG_ID> -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' | jq -c .assigned_team_ids curl -s "localhost:4916/team/info?team_id=<TEAM_ID>" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' | jq -c .team_info.access_group_ids curl -s -X POST localhost:4916/team/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_id":"<TEAM_ID>","access_group_ids":["<AG_ID>"]}' curl -s -X POST localhost:4916/team/delete -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_ids":["<TEAM_ID>"]}' ``` BEFORE, captured at 262ed530f8, current `litellm_internal_staging`. `grep -c sync_team_access_group_membership litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py` returns 0 on that tree, so the leg really ran without the fix ``` ### 3. both sides agree after attaching access group assigned_team_ids: ["97b919b2-dc08-4e35-ad13-707649e02407"] team access_group_ids: ["a777ceca-3bd4-4d27-9917-c467436622c0"] ### 4. admin clears Access Groups on the team (Teams page -> Save) {"team_id":"97b919b2-dc08-4e35-ad13-707649e02407","access_group_ids":null} ### 5. the two views after clearing access group assigned_team_ids (Attached Teams): ["97b919b2-dc08-4e35-ad13-707649e02407"] One team is lost on all three runs, while both teams' own rows say they are attached, so the group under-grants silently ``` === RMW run 1 === Attached Teams: ["b41af4aa-989e-4d9a-bac6-3bddacf0cc75"] team A access_group_ids: ["a8bc5879-c378-4941-b4db-8ada2411c52a"] team B access_group_ids: ["a8bc5879-c378-4941-b4db-8ada2411c52a"] === RMW run 2 === Attached Teams: ["c541e715-aaf1-41bc-b2e8-32330f5f3a75"] === RMW run 3 === Attached Teams: ["2365651a-21f7-4e6d-9d94-15caf46a261f"] ``` At 9bb0ed2f0f, this PR's head. Both teams survive on all three runs ``` === run 1 === Attached Teams: ["70197048-81d7-4146-b8e3-87f78cda3522","b755f46b-bb79-4796-be68-565e5a00f7ae"] === run 2 === Attached Teams: ["55dfb75b-9379-42b3-a8ce-555dc5dcf5fe","615f8802-5080-488e-a47f-67040ab5cd82"] === run 3 === Attached Teams: ["a3fd4c7b-a210-4cda-aac2-319f0013098f","bd45acf7-2628-429c-bb89-c397f3f0d405"] ``` CREATE PATH, re-run at 5399f0df5f after the create insert and its mirror moved into one transaction, and after merging current staging. A team created with an access group already set shows up under Attached Teams, clearing it on update removes it, and deleting the other team removes that one too ``` curl -s -X POST localhost:4916/team/new -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_alias":"created-with-group","access_group_ids":["<AG_ID>"]}' curl -s localhost:4916/v1/access_group/<AG_ID> -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' | jq -c .assigned_team_ids curl -s -X POST localhost:4916/team/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_id":"<NEW_TEAM>","access_group_ids":[]}' curl -s -X POST localhost:4916/team/delete -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_ids":["<TEAM>"]}' ``` ``` --- team/new with the group set at create time --- assigned_team_ids: ['ef8f5d12-6beb-4889-ab5d-cbeef0a1d286', 'f1a7b186-186d-41c3-a927-7c8ea629b3c0'] --- team/update clearing the groups --- assigned_team_ids: ['ef8f5d12-6beb-4889-ab5d-cbeef0a1d286'] --- team/delete of the first team --- assigned_team_ids: [] ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `assigned_key_ids` has the same hole via `/key/update` - A cache drop that fails leaves that entry stale until a later write retries it - A team-side and access-group-side edit can still interleave across the two - A mirror failure after team delete waits for that id to be reused - The detach scans the access group table, which is admin-sized - Deriving attached teams instead would hide a live grant ## Review notes Four things worth knowing before reading the diff. First, `assigned_team_ids` is not a display-only mirror. `get_authorized_resources_from_key_access_groups` in `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py` reads it directly to decide whether an access group carried on a key is authorized for that key's team, and there is a test pinning that behavior with the team's own `access_group_ids` left empty on purpose. So the stale row was granting models, MCP servers and agents that the admin had already revoked, which makes this a correctness fix on an authorization input rather than a UI cleanup, and it is why the sync invalidates the group's cache entry instead of only writing the row. Second, the mirror takes no desired-state argument at all. It locks the team with `pg_advisory_xact_lock` and reads the team row as committed, inside the same transaction as its writes. Reconciling against the committed row rather than a before/after delta is what lets a retry heal a half-applied sync, because the team row commits first and a retry's delta is empty. Holding the lock across the read is what makes two writers on the same team converge, rather than the slower one replaying its own stale snapshot over the newer one. Worth noting that both properties made the diff smaller. The signature lost `previous_access_group_ids` and then `access_group_ids` too, so all three call sites now pass just a team id, and team deletion needs no special case: a team with no row reconciles to the empty set and detaches everywhere. On why an advisory lock rather than folding the team write into the mirror transaction or taking `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the team row, which is the more obvious reading of the review comment. The access-group endpoints already run a transaction that locks an access group and then a team. A mirror that locks the team and then access groups is the reverse order, and the two deadlock. I checked rather than reasoned about it, and Postgres aborts one side: ``` team_side: RawQueryError: ERROR: deadlock detected DETAIL: Process 81 waits for ShareLock on transaction 998; blocked by process 82. ag_side: committed ``` The advisory lock is never taken by the access-group endpoints, so it cannot join their lock order to form a cycle, and the same probe reports no deadlock with it in place. It serializes per team, which is the property actually needed. Third, the mirror is set-based statements inside one transaction, not a per-group read-modify-write loop. Greptile flagged the loop as a lost-update risk and it was right, so the concurrency leg above reproduces it three times out of three against the earlier revision and shows it fixed. `array_append` and `array_remove` mutate the array inside the statement, so a concurrent write for another team cannot clobber it, the pair commits together, and the statement count no longer scales with how many group ids a caller sends. `COALESCE` is load-bearing here because the column is nullable in Postgres, and without it both guards evaluate to NULL and the row is silently skipped. Fourth, the sync helper deliberately lives in `management_helpers` rather than in `access_group_endpoints`. That module is a lazily registered feature router, and its routes reach the schema through the committed snapshot that `inject_lazy_stubs` injects for features it believes are unloaded. That check is `module_path in sys.modules`, so importing the module eagerly from `team_endpoints` marks the feature loaded while its router was never included, and every one of its paths and schemas disappears. This is a live `/openapi.json` defect, not only a CI gate: a running proxy would serve a spec missing those routes until some request happened to warm the router, so Swagger and any generated client lose them. Counting `access_group` paths off `app.openapi()` in one interpreter shows it directly, 10 with the helper extracted and 6 with the eager import restored. The first revision of this PR had the eager import, which is what turned the schema check red. On the one review point I did not act on. Team deletion commits before the mirror runs, and a retry of `/team/delete` is rejected at validation with a 404 before it reaches the mirror, so a mirror that failed after a successful delete leaves the team id behind on its groups. That is accurate, and I checked the 404 against a live proxy rather than reading for it. I left it alone because the remedies are worse and the residual is narrower than it looks. Detaching before the delete means a delete that fails partway leaves a live team stripped of its access groups, which is an outage for a team still in use, traded against a stale row for a team that no longer exists. Putting the delete in the mirror's transaction means replacing `delete_data` with raw SQL inside a function that also deletes that team's keys, models and memberships. Neither is a good trade for this. The residual also only bites if the team id is reused, since a stale id grants nothing while no team holds it, and team ids are caller-suppliable so reuse is possible. But reuse is exactly the moment `POST /team/new` runs the reconcile, which clears it. Seeding a dangling id directly in the database and then recreating the team with that id: ``` --- seeded a DANGLING id: the team does not exist --- {"team_id":"reused-team-id-probe","access_group_ids":[]} --- team recreated with the SAME id; does it inherit the grant? --- {"assigned_team_ids":[]} ``` So the stale row is cleaned before anything can be issued against it. Worth saying plainly that this path is strictly better than before this PR either way: team deletion previously never cleaned the mirror at all, so what is left here is the old behavior surviving in a failure case rather than anything new. The create path had a milder version of the same shape, and that one is now fixed rather than argued down. `POST /team/new` used to commit the team row and then mirror it, so a mirror that failed left a team whose groups never learned about it while the retry was rejected as a duplicate `team_id`. The insert and the reconcile now share one transaction, so the team row goes away with the failed mirror and the retry is a clean create. `tests/proxy_admin_ui_tests/test_access_group_team_sync.py` pins that against a real Postgres: raise inside the transaction after the reconcile and both the groups and the team table come back untouched. Cache invalidation is now driven by desired state rather than by which rows the current attempt changed. The mirror reads the groups the team should be on plus the groups that currently list it, before its writes, and the caller drops all of them. That is what makes a failed drop retryable: the retry's `UPDATE`s match nothing because the database is already reconciled, and it still finds the same set to invalidate. Every drop is attempted even when one raises, so one unreachable cache cannot leave the rest of the groups serving a revoked grant, and the error is re-raised afterward so the caller sees the failure. On the merge with current staging, #36819 reworked team delete to evict the team cache and sweep dangling references after the row delete. The mirror now runs last on that path, after both, so it still reconciles against a team that is gone and nothing fallible sits between the delete and the eviction that comment asks to keep adjacent. On completeness of the writer set, `team.access_group_ids` is only ever written by `POST /team/new`, `POST /team/update`, and team delete. `PATCH /team/{team_id}` is not a fourth writer: it builds an `UpdateTeamRequest` and calls `update_team`. Every one of those three now calls the same helper, so a reviewer can check completeness by grepping for writes to that column rather than trusting the list. Two notes on the tests. The three unrelated-looking edits in `test_team_endpoints.py` are a harness artifact: those tests build the team row as `MagicMock(spec=LiteLLM_TeamTable)`, and pydantic v2 model fields are not class attributes, so a spec'd mock does not carry them and reading `access_group_ids` off it raises `AttributeError`. Each edit is a single `access_group_ids = None` on the mock. Separately, the raw SQL needs a real database to mean anything, since a mocked prisma has to reimplement the array semantics in Python and then passes whatever the SQL says. I confirmed that by mutating the detach guard to `AND TRUE` and watching the unit test stay green. `tests/proxy_admin_ui_tests/test_access_group_team_sync.py` runs the statements against a real Postgres and dropping either `NOT (... = ANY(...))` guard fails it 4/4. Be aware that this file is a local harness rather than a CI gate today. `tests/proxy_admin_ui_tests/` is only referenced by `.circleci/config.yml`, and CircleCI is no longer connected to this repository, so no job on a pull request runs that directory. No PR workflow provides a Postgres service at all. Run it by hand with a database up: ``` DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... python -m prisma db push --schema litellm/proxy/schema.prisma --skip-generate cd tests/proxy_admin_ui_tests && DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... python -m pytest test_access_group_team_sync.py -q ``` Giving that directory a home in GitHub Actions is worth doing, and it would light up five other files that have not run since the migration, but it is CI infrastructure work that does not belong in a bug fix. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2113173845894b95ab154df03e2d7637 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signal.title: feat(lint): exempt TypedDict-annotated dict literals from LIT002
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - LIT002 flags `x: MyTd = {...}` but not the `MyTd(...)` spelling - Same value and type either way, so the count is a spelling tax - TypedDicts with non-identifier keys can't use the call spelling at all How it solves it: - Exempts dict literals assigned to names annotated with a TypedDict defined at the file's top level - Only if the name is bound exactly once in the file - Only if every declared or inherited field is `ReadOnly` - Only the outer display: nested mutable literals still count ## User Flow Before: a contributor who builds a TypedDict payload as an annotated dict literal fails the lint gate and must respell or suppress 1. They write `payload: Final[RequestKwargs] = {"model": m, "max_tokens": 128}` with `RequestKwargs` a TypedDict defined in the same module 2. They stage the change and run `make check` 3. The type-discipline gate fails: the line is reported as `LIT002 mutable dict literal` and the codebase count lands one over its ratcheted ceiling 4. To land the PR they respell the value as `RequestKwargs(model=m, max_tokens=128)` or add `# mutable-ok: <reason>`, though neither changes what the value is at runtime After: the same literal passes the gate untouched 1. They write the same `payload: Final[RequestKwargs] = {"model": m, "max_tokens": 128}` line 2. They stage the change and run `make check` 3. The type-discipline gate passes: the literal now has the same standing as the `RequestKwargs(...)` call, and the LIT002 count is unchanged 4. When some other line does trip LIT002, its message now also names the annotated-literal spelling as a blessed fix ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Demo snippet `td_snip.py` (a TypedDict-annotated dict literal, the pattern this PR legalizes): ```python from typing import Final, ReadOnly, TypedDict class RequestKwargs(TypedDict): model: ReadOnly[str] max_tokens: ReadOnly[int] payload: Final[RequestKwargs] = {"model": "gpt-5.5", "max_tokens": 128} ``` Before, at base commit 7fcca523aa: ``` $ python scripts/check_type_discipline.py td_snip.py td_snip.py:9: LIT002 mutable dict literal: this builds a collection that can be grown or rewritten. ... 1 violation(s). $ echo $? 1 ``` After, at bbb5c9420d the same command prints nothing and exits 0 Gates and tests at bbb5c9420d, on top of `litellm_internal_staging`: ``` $ python scripts/type_discipline_gate.py OK: every LIT rule is within its codebase ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) $ python scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py OK: every strict rule is within its codebase ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) $ python scripts/type_check_gate.py OK: every rule is within its basedpyright limit or no higher than base (145568 errors total) $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_check_type_discipline.py -q 97 passed in 0.29s ``` False-negative audit at bbb5c9420d: running the base checker and this branch's checker over `litellm/ tests/ enterprise/ scripts/` produces the identical set of 162,952 LIT002 lines, so no existing site gains the exemption today and `make lint-budget-update` moves no ceilings ("Ratcheted LIT-rule limits down by 0"). Exempted sites are also frozen by construction: the annotation must name a module-top-level TypedDict bound exactly once whose every declared and inherited field is `ReadOnly`, so a writable or `# writable-ok`'d TypedDict still counts ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats (if any) - Top-level same-module TypedDicts only; imported ones still count, matching LIT012's reach, and one nested inside a def or class never qualifies since its name does not resolve outside its scope - TypedDicts with any writable field still count, even where LIT012 was suppressed - Names the file also binds in any other form (def, assignment, import, loop or walrus or unpacking target, parameter, capture) still count, and a `from x import *` anywhere in the file disqualifies every name in it - Dotted annotations (`x: mod.Td = {...}`) never match, since they cannot name a local class - String forward-reference annotations (`x: "MyTd"`) are not recognized ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Lint-only change to an internal checker with conservative guards and broad negative tests; no runtime or auth/data paths touched. > > **Overview** > **LIT002** no longer flags dict literals on annotated assignments when they are the same one-shot shape as a `TypedDict(...)` call. The type-discipline checker adds `_typeddict_assigned_value_ids` (plus helpers for annotation names and file-wide bindings) and unions that set into the existing LIT002 exemptions alongside annotation internals and freezing-wrapper arguments. > > The exemption is **narrow**: module-top-level TypedDict whose name is bound exactly once, every field (including inherited) is `ReadOnly[...]`, bare or `Final[...]` annotation only—no dotted types, imported/nested TypedDicts, writable fields, `from x import *`, or rebound names. Nested mutables inside the literal still trip LIT002. Rule docs and the violation fix message now describe this path; tests cover happy paths and the conservative false-negative guards. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit bbb5c9420d267a22bdec3233a6dba2f6eec96af3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
