signal.title: [Bug]: False BudgetExceededError under sustained load — 'Current cost' = max_budget + recent spend, no Redis, self-heals in ~2 min
signal.text: ### What happened During sustained batch runs (~100-130 requests over ~40 min, single client, mix of `/v1/ocr` Mistral passthrough, Gemini `generateContent` passthrough and Anthropic passthrough), the proxy starts returning `429 budget_exceeded` near the end of the run, with a reported `Current cost` that matches **no real aggregate**. The reported value is always `max_budget + (small recent spend)`, and the condition **self-heals in about 2 minutes** without any intervention: a retry with 15s/30s/60s backoff fails 3 times, then the 4th attempt succeeds. We reproduced this on **v1.88.1** and again on **v1.96.2** after upgrading, and once earlier when our global cap was 20 instead of 50 — the phantom value tracked the cap each time. ### Occurrences | Date | Proxy version | Configured cap | Error message excerpt | Real spend at that moment | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2026-07-01 | 1.88.1 | 20 (global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 20.013879769999956, Max budget: 20` | a few cents that day | | 2026-08-14 AM | 1.88.1 | 50 (key + global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Key=<hash> Current cost: 51.0512, Max budget: 50.0`, then `Current cost: 50.014505` on the two retries | key spend that day ~1.05 USD | | 2026-08-14 PM | 1.96.2 | 50 (key + global) | `Budget has been exceeded! Key=<alias> (sk-...) Current cost: 50.024508499999996, Max budget: 50.0` | key spend that day ~1.1 USD | In each case `Current cost - max_budget` equals the key's genuine recent spend (e.g. `51.0512 - 50 = 1.0512` ≈ the 1.05 USD actually spent by the run so far). It looks like an in-memory spend counter transiently gets seeded/inflated with the `max_budget` value itself. ### What the database said at the same time Checked immediately around the 2026-08-14 AM occurrence: - `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` for the key: **1.07** - `sum(spend)` in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` for that key, last 30 days: **1.59** - `sum(spend)` in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`, all keys, all time: **24.90** - No individual SpendLogs row above 0.04 - `/global/spend`: 4.24 / 50 Nothing anywhere near 50, and no row disappeared afterwards. The inflated value existed only in memory and was gone once the periodic DB resync ran (the 4th retry, ~2 min after the first 429, passed; `/key/info` afterwards reported the correct small spend). ### Setup - Docker `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, **single instance**, **no Redis** (in-memory cache only) - Postgres-backed (`database_url` set), default batch-write settings - `litellm_settings`: `max_budget: 50`, `budget_duration: 30d`, `turn_off_message_logging: true`, `drop_params: true`, `telemetry: false` - Virtual key with `max_budget: 50`, `budget_duration: 30d`, model ACL - `router_settings`: `simple-shuffle`, `num_retries: 0`, `allowed_fails: 0`, `cooldown_time: 60`, cross-provider fallbacks configured - Load pattern when it triggers: ~100+ requests spread over ~40 min through one virtual key, several requests in flight concurrently (bounded page-level concurrency). Light traffic (20 sequential probes) never triggers it. ### Expected behavior Budget checks compare against actual spend. A request should not be rejected with `Current cost ≈ max_budget + real spend` while the durable stores all agree spend is ~2% of the cap. ### Possibly related - #27735 (stale spend in BudgetExceededError while `/key/info` disagrees) — same symptom family, but our value is not stale, it is inflated by exactly `max_budget` and self-corrects - #30460 (Redis counters inflating) — we run without Redis, so the in-memory path can inflate on its own ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.96.2 (also reproduced on v1.88.1)

signal.title: feat(guardrails): add new upstream presidio pii entities including german set
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Presidio upstream added 37 recognizers litellm's entity list doesn't expose - German identifiers (Steuer-ID, Personalausweis, KFZ, ...) can't be masked or blocked - Korea, Canada, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, Nigeria, Philippines, South Africa also missing How it solves it: - Adds the 37 entities to `PiiEntityType` with 9 new categories - Analyzer payload, config validation, and Admin UI pick them up automatically - Exact-set tests pin every category to upstream recognizer names ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin in Germany cannot protect German identifiers 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=guardrails, click Add Guardrail, and pick Presidio PII 2. The entity picker's category filter offers USA, UK, Spain and others, but no Germany 3. A user sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with "Meine Steuer-ID ist 65929970489" 4. The tax ID reaches the LLM provider in readable plain text After: the same admin masks tax IDs and blocks license plates 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=guardrails, click Add Guardrail, and pick Presidio PII 2. The category filter now lists Germany with 13 entities; they set DE_TAX_ID to MASK, DE_KFZ to BLOCK, language "de", and save 3. The same POST now returns a completion in which the provider only ever saw `Meine Steuer-ID ist ` 4. A request containing "Kennzeichen M-AB 1234" is refused with 400 naming DE_KFZ as a blocked entity ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All captured at commit 68f73490b8 against a live proxy on localhost:4000 and a live Presidio analyzer/anonymizer (current ghcr.io/data-privacy-stack images; the analyzer built with a German spaCy model, `de` in the registry languages, and the upstream-default-disabled German recognizers enabled) The analyzer serves all 13 German entities for language de, proving the enum values match upstream recognizer names exactly: ``` $ curl "http://localhost:5002/supportedentities?language=de" ["PHONE_NUMBER","DATE_TIME","ORGANIZATION","DE_TAX_NUMBER","DE_VAT_ID","DE_PLZ","LOCATION","DE_HEALTH_INSURANCE","DE_TAX_ID","MAC_ADDRESS","CRYPTO","IP_ADDRESS","AGE","NRP","EMAIL","ID","DE_SOCIAL_SECURITY","EMAIL_ADDRESS","DE_ID_CARD","DE_HANDELSREGISTER","PERSON","IBAN_CODE","DE_KFZ","DE_BSNR","DE_PASSPORT","URL","MEDICAL_LICENSE","DE_LANR","DE_FUEHRERSCHEIN"] ``` Guardrail config used on the proxy (`presidio_language: de`, MASK tax ID and postal code, BLOCK license plates): ```yaml guardrails: - guardrail_name: presidio-pii-de litellm_params: guardrail: presidio mode: pre_call default_on: true presidio_language: de pii_entities_config: DE_TAX_ID: MASK DE_PLZ: MASK DE_KFZ: BLOCK ``` German text is masked end to end through the proxy guardrail: ``` $ curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/guardrails/apply_guardrail -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"guardrail_name": "presidio-pii-de", "text": "Meine Steuer-ID ist 65929970489 und meine PLZ ist 10115."}' {"response_text": "Meine Steuer-ID ist und meine PLZ ist ."} ``` A chat completion carrying a German license plate is blocked pre-call with 400: ``` $ curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Mein Auto hat das Kennzeichen M-AB 1234, was bedeutet das?"}]}' {"error": {"message": "Blocked entity detected: DE_KFZ by Guardrail: presidio-pii-de. This entity is not allowed to be used in this request.", "type": "None", "param": "None", "code": "400"}} ``` The UI settings endpoint that feeds the dashboard entity picker now returns the Germany category (plus Korea, Canada, Sweden, Thailand, Turkey, Nigeria, Philippines, South Africa): ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/guardrails/ui/add_guardrail_settings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq '.pii_entity_categories[] | select(.category == "Germany")' {"category": "Germany", "entities": ["DE_TAX_ID", "DE_TAX_NUMBER", "DE_VAT_ID", "DE_PASSPORT", "DE_ID_CARD", "DE_FUEHRERSCHEIN", "DE_SOCIAL_SECURITY", "DE_HEALTH_INSURANCE", "DE_LANR", "DE_BSNR", "DE_KFZ", "DE_HANDELSREGISTER", "DE_PLZ"]} ``` A real paid LLM call proves the provider only ever sees the masked text. The deployment `claude-haiku-4-5` was added at runtime through the Admin UI (models stored in DB), and the model was asked to echo the input verbatim: ``` $ curl -X POST http://localhost:4001/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Du bist ein Echo-Dienst zum Testen einer Textpipeline. Gib die folgende Zeile exakt zeichengetreu zurueck, ohne jeden Zusatz oder Kommentar: Meine Steuer-ID ist 65929970489 und meine PLZ ist 10115."}]}' ``` The completion (id `chatcmpl-a492d6ad-1cd9-47a0-ab52-18b88bf8bd89`, 88 prompt / 32 completion tokens billed, captured at d79155d681 running the docker image built from this branch) came back as: ``` Meine Steuer-ID ist und meine PLZ ist . ``` The model echoed the masked tokens, so the real Steuer-ID and postal code never left the proxy UI flow verified against the docker build: http://localhost:4001/ui -> Guardrails -> Add New Guardrail -> Presidio PII -> PII Configuration. Filtering by the new Germany category lists exactly the 13 DE_* entities with per-entity MASK/BLOCK selectors (screenshots and a screen recording below) Germany category filter showing the first DE entities with per-entity actions: Remaining German entities down to DE PLZ: Screen recording of the full flow (Guardrails -> Add New Guardrail -> Presidio PII -> Germany filter): ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Detection needs the current ghcr.io/data-privacy-stack analyzer images; mcr latest is stale - Upstream ships German recognizers disabled; operators must enable them in the registry conf - DE entities need `presidio_language: de` and a German model in the analyzer NLP conf - MEDICAL_* NER entities intentionally excluded; they need a special transformers model - Docs entity table lives in the docs repo, follow-up needed there ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: vertex_ai: tool schemas with tuple-form `items` crash `_build_vertex_schema` ('list' object has no attribute 'get')
signal.text: ## Summary On the `vertex_ai/*` provider path, LiteLLM's Vertex schema builder crashes with `litellm.APIConnectionError` when a tool's JSON Schema uses **tuple-form `items`** (`"items": [{...}, {...}]` — valid JSON Schema, which OpenAI-compatible clients and several MCP servers emit). The same request works fine through other providers (e.g. OpenRouter), because the crash is in Vertex-specific schema transformation code. ## Reproduction ```bash curl https://<proxy>/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "x"}], "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": { "name": "f", "description": "f", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": { "a": {"type": "array", "items": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "string"}]} }} }}] }' ``` ## Error ``` litellm.APIConnectionError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' Traceback (most recent call last): File "litellm/main.py", line 5270, in completion File "litellm/utils.py", line 3955, in get_optional_params File "litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py", line 1152, in map_openai_params File "litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py", line 613, in _map_function File "litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py", line 603, in _build_vertex_schema File "litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py", line 810, in convert_anyof_null_to_nullable File "litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py", line 814, in convert_anyof_null_to_nullable File "litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py", line 781, in convert_anyof_null_to_nullable anyof = schema.get("anyOf", None) ^^^^^^^^^^ AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' ``` A sibling variant in `add_object_type` (same file) produces `TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not str` when it hits the same list-valued `items` node (`schema["type"] = "object"` on a list). ## Root cause `convert_anyof_null_to_nullable(schema)` and `add_object_type(schema)` in `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py` recurse into `schema.get("items")` assuming it is always a dict: ```python items: Final = schema.get("items", None) if items is not None: convert_anyof_null_to_nullable(items, depth=depth + 1) # crashes when items is a list ``` Tuple-form `items` is valid JSON Schema (2020-12 allows `items` to be an array of schemas). Both walkers should either guard with `isinstance(items, dict)` (and iterate lists) or normalize tuple-form `items` to `{"anyOf": [...]}` before processing. Still present on `main` as of 2026-08-14. ## Workaround Sanitizing the schema before LiteLLM sees it — rewriting tuple-form `"items": [...]` as `"items": {"anyOf": [...]}` — makes the same request pass (verified against a LiteLLM proxy). We're carrying that as a proxy pre-call hook until the upstream fix lands.
signal.author: JulienRineau

signal.title: [Bug]: Prisma query engine crashes immediately on first query on Windows (pip install) - LiteLLM 1.82.x / 1.83.0
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Environment OS: Windows 10/11 x64 Python: 3.12.x (pythoncore-3.12-64) LiteLLM versions affected: 1.82.0, 1.82.3, 1.83.0 LiteLLM last working version: 1.81.16 Installation method: pip (not Docker) prisma-client-py: 0.15.0 Prisma CLI: 5.17.0 Node.js: v20.19.1 (also reproduced with v24.14.1) PostgreSQL: 15.x at 127.0.0.1:5432 Virtual environment: Python venv at C:\LiteLLM\venv What happened? After upgrading from LiteLLM 1.81.x to any 1.82.x or 1.83.0 release via pip on Windows, the Prisma query engine crashes immediately on the first database query after startup. LiteLLM becomes completely unable to read from or write to the PostgreSQL database. The Prisma migrations run successfully. The query engine binary is found and its PID is logged. However the very first query LiteLLM makes after startup returns httpcore.ReadError, indicating the engine process crashes mid-response. All subsequent queries fail with httpcore.ConnectError: All connection attempts failed because the engine process is dead. Critically: The Prisma engine works perfectly fine in isolation. A standalone Python test script connecting to the same database with the same DATABASE_URL succeeds without any issues: pythonimport asyncio from prisma import Prisma async def test(): db = Prisma() await db.connect() print('SUCCESS - connected!') await db.disconnect() asyncio.run(test()) # Output: query-engine 393aa359c9ad4a4bb28630fb5613f9c281cde053 # SUCCESS - connected! This confirms the issue is in how LiteLLM 1.82.x/1.83.0 initializes or interacts with the Prisma client internally — not in Prisma, the binary, the database, or the network. Relevant log output (with --debug) query-engine 393aa359c9ad4a4bb28630fb5613f9c281cde053 LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: utils.py - Started Prisma DB health watchdog LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: utils.py - Found prisma-query-engine at PID 29404. LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: utils.py - Watching engine PID 29404 via os.kill polling. LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: proxy_server.py - litellm.proxy_server.py::add_deployment() - Error getting new models from DB - File "prisma/engine/_http.py", line 217, in request httpcore.ReadError <-- engine crashes on FIRST query LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: utils.py - LiteLLM Prisma Client Exception get_generic_data: All connection attempts failed LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: utils.py - LiteLLM Prisma Client Exception get_generic_data: All connection attempts failed LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: proxy_server.py - ProxyConfig:add_deployment - All connection attempts failed File "prisma/engine/_http.py", line 217, in request httpcore.ConnectError: All connection attempts failed <-- engine is dead, all subsequent queries fail What I expected LiteLLM should connect to PostgreSQL via Prisma and start successfully, as it did in 1.81.16. What actually happened The Prisma query engine process starts (PID is found and logged), but crashes on the very first query LiteLLM makes after startup (ReadError). All subsequent queries fail with ConnectError because the engine process is no longer running. Steps to reproduce Windows 10/11 x64, Python 3.12, pip install (not Docker) Create a fresh venv: python -m venv venv Install: pip install "litellm[proxy]==1.83.0" Install prisma separately (not pulled in automatically): pip install prisma Fetch binaries: cd venv/Lib/site-packages/litellm/proxy && prisma py fetch --force Generate client: prisma generate --schema schema.prisma Set DATABASE_URL environment variable to a valid PostgreSQL URL Run: litellm --config config.yaml --debug Observe ReadError on first query, then ConnectError on all subsequent queries Additional investigation done The following were ruled out as causes: ✅ PostgreSQL is running and accessible — standalone Prisma test script connects successfully ✅ DATABASE_URL is correctly set — confirmed via python -c "import os; print(os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL'))" ✅ Prisma binary is downloaded — prisma version shows correct binary at cache path ✅ Node.js version — reproduced with both v20.19.1 (LTS) and v24.14.1 ✅ HTTP/HTTPS proxy vars — cleared $env:HTTP_PROXY, $env:HTTPS_PROXY, set $env:NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 — no change ✅ Windows Defender — not blocking the binary (binary runs standalone) ✅ Fresh venv — reproduced on completely fresh virtual environment ✅ prisma py fetch --force — binaries downloaded successfully ✅ prisma generate --schema schema.prisma — client generated successfully ✅ Downgrading to litellm==1.81.16 — fixes the issue completely ### Steps to Reproduce 1. 2. 3. ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? _No response_ ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.53.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(proxy): use Popen.poll() instead of os.kill(pid, 0) for engine liveness on Windows
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #30847 (duplicated issue) Fixes #25260 ## Linear ticket N/A ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Type Bug Fix ## Changes On Windows, `os.kill(pid, 0)` does not check liveness; it routes all signals except `CTRL_C_EVENT`/`CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` through `TerminateProcess`, which terminates the target process outright. This meant `_poll_engine_proc` was silently killing the Prisma query-engine sidecar (`query-engine-windows.exe`) on every poll tick, within the first event-loop yield after startup. The fix dispatches to a new `_is_engine_alive_windows()` method on Windows, which uses `Popen.poll() is None` to check whether the subprocess is still running without touching it. A `process.pid == self._engine_pid` guard ensures we only trust the process object if its PID matches the one we recorded at connection time, preventing a false liveness result from a stale internal reference. The POSIX path (`os.kill(pid, 0)`) is unchanged. `_poll_engine_proc` is simplified to call `_is_engine_alive()` instead of calling `os.kill` directly, which removes the now-unnecessary `PermissionError`/`OSError` handler. Six regression tests are added to `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_prisma_self_heal.py`: living engine, dead engine, pid mismatch fallback, no-process fallback, AttributeError fallback, and a behavioral test that the loop correctly triggers reconnect when `_is_engine_alive` returns False. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix To reproduce the original crash on Windows, start the proxy with a PostgreSQL `DATABASE_URL` configured: ``` python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload 2>&1 | tee litellm.log ``` Before this fix, the proxy would crash within ~1 second of startup with the Prisma engine silently terminated. The log would show no explicit error; the engine process simply disappeared. After this fix, the proxy starts cleanly. To verify: ``` # Wait for startup (engine connects in ~3s on first run) curl -s http://localhost:4000/health | python -m json.tool ``` Expected response includes `"status": "healthy"` with a connected database. The sidecar (`query-engine-windows.exe`) remains alive for the duration of the proxy process.

signal.title: feat(azure_ai): shape FW-Kimi / Kimi for Azure Foundry + Claude Code
signal.text: ## Summary - Shape **Azure AI Foundry / Fireworks `FW-Kimi-K3`** (and related Kimi ids) like Moonshot on the `azure_ai` chat path: drop fixed sampling, sanitize `reasoning_effort` (`low`/`high`/`max`), fill `reasoning_content` on tool-call turns, and **strip `thinking_blocks`** (Foundry returns `Extra inputs are not permitted`). - Shape the Anthropic `/v1/messages` → Responses bridge used by Claude Code: flush assistant text/thinking before `function_call`, convert pre-tool assistant text into a `reasoning` item, and drop invalid sampling / `reasoning.effort` on Responses kwargs. - Add `azure_ai/FW-Kimi-K3` pricing/context entry + unit tests. Validated in a Nubank prod-shaped sandbox against Foundry with Claude Code multi-turn tool use. Related Nu deployment PR: [nubank/litellm#95](https://github.com/nubank/litellm/pull/95). Supersedes/extends the earlier closed attempt [#36773](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/36773) with the Responses-path + `thinking_blocks` fixes we needed in practice. ## Test plan - [ ] `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/azure_ai/test_azure_ai_kimi_shaping.py` - [ ] Chat: assistant history with `thinking_blocks` + `tool_calls` → outbound has `reasoning_content`, no `thinking_blocks` - [ ] Responses: Anthropic messages with thinking + tool_use → provider input has reasoning before `function_call` - [ ] End-to-end (optional): Claude Code → LiteLLM `/v1/messages` → Foundry `FW-Kimi-K3` multi-turn tools succeeds Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: docs llms.txt has dead links, including the Docusaurus template intro page
signal.text: hey! i was testing an llms.txt validator against popular docs sites and docs.litellm.ai came back with 2 dead links out of 52: ``` $ curl -so /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://docs.litellm.ai/intro 404 $ curl -so /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/archive 404 ``` the `/intro` one is worth a look beyond the 404: it's listed as "Docusaurus Setup Guide - Quickly learn to set up a Docusaurus site", which is the default Docusaurus template page leaking into the file. so whatever generates your llms.txt picked up a page that was later (rightly) deleted, and the entry stayed behind. `/release_notes/archive` looks like the same staleness, the page moved or got removed and the llms.txt kept the old route. any AI tool that reads llms.txt to answer questions about litellm hits those 404s. happy to PR a fix if you point me at where the file is maintained, i couldn't find a generator for it in the repo so i'm guessing it's hand-maintained or built out-of-band. for context, i maintain [docusaurus-plugin-copy-page-button](https://github.com/portdeveloper/docusaurus-plugin-copy-page-button) (runs on 28 docs sites; react native and pnpm are the big ones, puppeteer too) so i spend a lot of time in this corner of docs tooling. the checker i used is [llms-txt-check](https://github.com/portdeveloper/llms-txt-check) if you want to reproduce: `npx llms-txt-check https://docs.litellm.ai`. and if you want it guarding this permanently, it's one line in CI after deploy: ```yaml - run: npx llms-txt-check@0.1.1 https://docs.litellm.ai ``` it exits nonzero when any listed url stops serving. happy to PR that too, no pressure either way.

signal.title: [Bug]: responses() crashes with TypeError 'int object is not iterable' when input is numeric instead of returning 400
signal.text: ## Description `litellm.responses()` crashes with `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable` when `input` is a non-string, non-list type (e.g. integer, float, bool, None, dict). Instead of returning a clear validation error (HTTP 400), the TypeError propagates through `exception_type()` which has no `status_code`, falls through to `APIConnectionError`, and returns HTTP 500. ## Repro ```python import litellm response = litellm.responses( model="gpt-5.1", input=12345, # integer instead of string or list ) ``` ## Stack trace ```text File "litellm/responses/main.py", line 588, in _apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call for item in input TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable ``` ## Root cause In `litellm/responses/main.py`, `_apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call()` (both the async branch in `aresponses()` and the sync helper) checks only `isinstance(input, str)`: ```python if isinstance(input, str): client_input = [{"role": "user", "content": input}] else: client_input = [ item for item in input # ← crashes when input is not iterable if isinstance(item, dict) and "role" in item ] ``` When `input` is not a string, it assumes it is iterable. Non-string, non-list types (int, float, bool, None, dict) raise TypeError during `for item in input`. ## Expected behavior Invalid `input` types should raise `BadRequestError` with a descriptive message (e.g. "input must be a string or list of input items, got int") so the proxy returns HTTP 400 instead of HTTP 500. ## Suggested fix Add a type guard before iteration: ```python if isinstance(input, str): client_input = [{"role": "user", "content": input}] elif not isinstance(input, list): raise BadRequestError( message=f"'input' must be a string or list of input items, got {type(input).__name__}", model=model, llm_provider=custom_llm_provider or "unknown", ) else: client_input = [ item for item in input if isinstance(item, dict) and "role" in item ] ``` This applies at two locations in `litellm/responses/main.py`: 1. The async prompt-management branch (line ~472) 2. The sync `_apply_prompt_management_to_responses_call` helper (line ~583) ## Impact - Invalid client requests are misclassified as provider/system failures - Client receives retryable-looking 500 instead of non-retryable 400 - LiteLLM retry/cooldown machinery may treat this as a deployment failure, which can amplify impact ## Environment - LiteLLM version: v1.92.0 (observed in production; also present on current main) - Endpoint: `POST /v1/responses` / `POST /responses`

signal.title: feat(proxy): global SSE keepalive ping interval for OpenAI-shaped streaming routes
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - OpenAI-shaped streams send zero bytes until the first model token - Ingresses and load balancers kill those silent connections at their idle timeout - Keepalive pings today require per-deployment `keepalive_seconds` opt-in How it solves it: - Adds global `litellm_settings.sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds` - Used when neither the request nor the deployment sets an interval - A deployment's explicit `keepalive_seconds: 0` disable still wins - Also arms keepalive on router-less proxies ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming a long document to their self-hosted model through the company ingress gets a 504 before the first token ever arrives 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "qwen-local"`, `"stream": true`, and a ~16k-token document prompt 2. The self-hosted backend starts crunching the prompt; the first token is about 2.5 minutes away and the connection carries zero bytes in the meantime 3. At exactly 60 seconds the ingress gives up on the silent connection and returns `504 Gateway Time-out`; no SSE data ever arrives 4. Every retry dies the same way, so requests past the ingress idle timeout can never complete After: the same request emits `: ping` comments within seconds, holds the connection open through the whole prompt crunch, and completes 1. The proxy admin sets `litellm_settings.sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds: 3` and restarts the gateway 2. The developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same document prompt 3. Within ~3 seconds a `200` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream` arrives, followed by a `: ping` comment every 3 seconds 4. About 2.5 minutes in the real `data:` chunks arrive, then `data: [DONE]`; SSE-conformant clients ignore the comment lines, so nothing else about the stream changes ## Relevant issues Fixes #31865 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5300 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs ran the identical config below against real backends: gpt-5.6 (OpenAI, real API), claude-sonnet-5 (Anthropic, real API), and qwen-local, a self-hosted llama-server (Qwen2.5-0.5B Q8_0, CPU) whose ~16k-token prompt takes ~2.5 minutes of prefill before the first token. Each proxy sat behind a real nginx ingress mirror with two listeners: `proxy_read_timeout 10s` (aggressive) and `proxy_read_timeout 60s` (the nginx default). Before leg is the merge base 422d925334, after leg is this PR's head e53f044d20 ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6 litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.6 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: claude-sonnet-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: qwen-local litellm_params: model: openai/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct api_base: http://127.0.0.1:47611/v1 api_key: none timeout: 600 litellm_settings: anthropic_sse_ping_interval_seconds: 3 sse_keepalive_ping_interval_seconds: 3 general_settings: master_key: sk-qa-36154 ``` ### /v1/chat/completions, self-hosted slow backend through the 60s ingress ```bash curl -sS -N -i --max-time 300 http://127.0.0.1:<ingress-60s>/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-36154" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "qwen-local", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<74k-char document>"}], "stream": true, "max_tokens": 40}' ``` Before (422d925334): the proxy sends nothing while the backend prefills, so the ingress 504s at its read timeout with zero bytes delivered ```text [t+ 60.06s] HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out [t+ 60.06s] ping_comments=0 data_chunks=0 ``` After (e53f044d20): headers plus the first ping arrive in ~3s, 55 pings bridge the 164s prefill, and the stream completes ```text [t+ 3.16s] HTTP/1.1 200 OK [t+ 3.16s] Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8 [t+ 3.16s] : ping [t+ 6.16s] : ping [t+ 9.16s] : ping [t+ 167.28s] data: {"id":"chatcmpl-BOY3tXGcuL7uE6knLd2ItTlAj9KKL8HY","created":1786518422,"model":"qwen-local","object":"chat.completion.chunk",... [t+ 167.63s] data: [DONE] [t+ 167.64s] curl exit=0 ping_comments=55 data_chunks=20 ``` ### /v1/responses, gpt-5.6 with reasoning effort high through the 10s ingress openai SDK, real OpenAI API: `client.responses.create(model="gpt-5.6", input=<hard math prompt>, stream=True, reasoning={"effort": "high"})` Before (422d925334): the first reasoning gap exceeds the ingress timeout and the stream dies mid-flight ```text [t+ 0.64s] first event: response.created [t+ 10.99s] STREAM FAILED: RemoteProtocolError: peer closed connection without sending complete message body (incomplete chunked read) ``` After (e53f044d20): pings cover every reasoning gap and the stream runs to completion ```text [t+ 0.49s] first event: response.created [t+ 205.39s] STREAM COMPLETED: 396 events, answer tail: ...'\\]\n\nintegers \\(n\\) with \\(0\\le n\\le 20000\\) make \\(n^2+n+41\\) prime.' ``` ### /v1/messages, claude-sonnet-5 through the 10s ingress (regression check, route untouched) anthropic SDK, real Anthropic API: `client.messages.stream(model="claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens=600, ...)`. This route keeps its pre-existing Anthropic ping events and completes on both legs ```text before: [t+ 4.86s] STREAM COMPLETED: 6 text deltas after: [t+ 4.05s] STREAM COMPLETED: 6 text deltas ``` ### Known limit, identical on both legs: hosted-provider chat completions with a slow first token OpenAI holds the entire HTTP response, headers included, until the first post-reasoning token, so no gateway-level layer can emit anything before that. gpt-5.6 chat completions through the 10s ingress 504s identically before and after; proof it is provider-side, bypassing LiteLLM entirely: ```text curl -N https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (gpt-5.6, reasoning_effort=high, stream=true) [openai-direct][t+ 45.02s] curl: (28) Operation timed out after 45005 milliseconds with 0 bytes received ``` Once headers do arrive, mid-stream gaps on chat completions are covered the same way as shown for /v1/responses above ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Hosted providers hold headers until first token; that wait stays uncoverable - Deployment `keepalive_seconds`, including explicit `0`, still beats the global - `/v1/messages` untouched; Anthropic ping events already cover it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix: preserve prompt_tokens_details when raw PromptTokensDetails reaches chunk aggregator
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `prompt_tokens_details` (including `cached_tokens: 0`) was silently dropped from the final streaming usage chunk on some requests - The helper that aggregates per-chunk usage only handled `dict` and `PromptTokensDetailsWrapper`; a raw openai-SDK `PromptTokensDetails` object was silently ignored How it solves it: - Add an `elif isinstance(..., PromptTokensDetails)` branch in `_usage_chunk_calculation_helper` to wrap the base class into a `PromptTokensDetailsWrapper`, matching the existing handling for dicts and wrapper instances ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming chat completions through LiteLLM Proxy with `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` gets inconsistent usage chunks 1. They send POST https://litellm-proxy/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}` 2. The final SSE usage chunk contains `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens` but no `prompt_tokens_details` field, even though the upstream provider returned `cached_tokens: 0` 3. Their cache-aware cost calculation must fail closed because `cached_tokens` is absent After: the final SSE chunk always includes `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` when the upstream provider returns it 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-proxy/v1/chat/completions 2. The final SSE usage chunk includes `"prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}` as the upstream provider intended 3. Their cost calculation can use the field to compute effective input tokens ## Relevant issues Fixes #36882 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The added unit test `test_prompt_tokens_details_base_class_preserved_in_usage_chunk` directly reproduces the failure: it sets `usage_chunk.prompt_tokens_details` to a raw `PromptTokensDetails(cached_tokens=0)` (simulating a chunk that bypasses litellm's `Usage.__init__`), calls `_usage_chunk_calculation_helper`, and asserts the result is not `None` and `cached_tokens == 0`. Before the fix this assertion fails; after, it passes. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix: no-log should not disable spend tracking
signal.text: ## The problem `Logging.should_run_callback` already intends to keep the proxy's cost-tracking callback running on a `no-log` request. The comment says so explicitly: ```python if litellm_params.get("no-log", False) is True: # proxy cost tracking cal backs should run if not ( isinstance(callback, CustomLogger) and "_PROXY_" in callback.__class__.__name__ ): return False ``` But the cost-tracking callback's class is **`_ProxyDBLogger`** (`litellm/proxy/hooks/proxy_track_cost_callback.py`), and the test is a case-sensitive substring match: ```python >>> "_PROXY_" in "_ProxyDBLogger" False ``` `_PROXY_` (upper-case, trailing underscore) never appears in `_ProxyDBLogger`. The exemption is dead code, so `_ProxyDBLogger` is skipped along with every other callback and **`no-log` silently disables spend tracking**. Other proxy hooks (`_PROXY_MaxParallelRequestsHandler`, `_PROXY_MaxBudgetLimiter`, …) do match the pattern, which is presumably why this went unnoticed — the one callback the comment is actually about is the one that doesn't match. Present on `litellm_internal_staging`, `main`, `v1.96.0-rc.1` and as far back as `v1.88.2`. ## Why it matters `no-log` is a reasonable thing for an application to send when it already reports its own traces and doesn't want the proxy to duplicate them. Nothing signals that it also turns off billing. We hit this in production: three services set `no-log` purely to avoid duplicate Langfuse traces, and their keys reported **$0** and were absent from `/team/daily/activity` for months, while every other key reported correctly. One of them was ~$170/month. Nobody had opted out of cost tracking — the flag just did more than its name implies. For a proxy used as a metering and budget-enforcement chokepoint, a request-level flag that lets any caller zero their own spend is worth closing. Budgets are affected too: with spend never incrementing, `max_budget` on those keys can never trip. ## The fix Replace the class-name heuristic with an explicit opt-in on `CustomLogger`: ```python class CustomLogger: # Set True on callbacks that must still run for `no-log` requests -- # metering, billing and budget enforcement, as opposed to observability. runs_on_no_log: bool = False ``` `_ProxyDBLogger` sets `runs_on_no_log = True`, and `should_run_callback` honours it: ```python if not ( isinstance(callback, CustomLogger) and ( callback.runs_on_no_log # Retained for callbacks predating `runs_on_no_log`. or "_PROXY_" in callback.__class__.__name__ ) ): ``` This keeps `no-log` meaning *"do not send this request to logging integrations"*, while accounting keeps working. ## Backwards compatibility - The `"_PROXY_"` check is **kept**, so any existing callback relying on the naming convention behaves exactly as before. - `runs_on_no_log` defaults to `False`, so every existing third-party callback is unaffected. - `litellm.global_disable_no_log_param` is untouched. - The only behaviour change is the one the existing comment already asks for: the cost callback now runs on `no-log` requests. ## Tests New: `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_no_log_spend_tracking.py` - `_ProxyDBLogger` **runs** on `no-log` (the regression) - an observability-style callback is still **skipped** on `no-log` - any callback can opt in via `runs_on_no_log` (not just the proxy's) - everything runs when `no-log` is absent or `False` - legacy `_PROXY_*`-named callbacks remain exempt without setting the flag - `global_disable_no_log_param` still overrides everything ## Alternative considered Simply correcting the string match (e.g. `startswith("_Proxy")`) is a one-liner, but keeps behaviour coupled to class naming, which is what allowed the bug to hide. An explicit attribute makes the intent checkable and lets other infrastructure callbacks (metering, budget enforcement) opt in deliberately. Happy to reduce this to the one-line string fix instead if you'd prefer the smaller change.

signal.title: fix(langfuse): log `custom_tool_call` items in Responses API output
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Freeform (custom) tool calls log no output to Langfuse - Every code-mode turn looks like the model answered nothing How it solves it: - Map `custom_tool_call` output items into the Langfuse output payload ## User Flow Before: a developer proxying a coding agent that uses a freeform `exec` tool sees blank outputs in Langfuse, so a whole session reads as if the model never answered 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"tools": [{"type": "custom", "name": "exec", ...}]` 2. The response comes back with a `custom_tool_call` item carrying the JavaScript to run, and the agent runs it 3. They open that generation in Langfuse: **Output is `null`**, while input, token counts and cost are all correct 4. Every turn where the model called `exec` looks empty, so the trace can't be used to review what the agent actually did After: the same request records the tool call it actually made 1. They send the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with the same custom tool 2. The response comes back with the same `custom_tool_call` item, and the agent runs it 3. They open that generation in Langfuse: **Output shows the call** — `[{"id": "...", "name": "exec", "call_id": "call_...", "type": "custom_tool_call", "input": "console.log(6*7)\n"}]` 4. Turns that called `exec` are reviewable alongside the plain-text and `function_call` turns that already worked ## Relevant issues <!-- none found --> ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) — ran `ruff format`/`ruff check` on the touched file and the target test module locally; full suite left to CI - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real `/v1/responses` calls through a local proxy against a live `gpt-5.6-sol` deployment, exporting to a self-hosted Langfuse. No mocks. Same request both times, only the commit differs. **Before** — proxy at `423b791ee0395815050998dd73542445350ab792` (this PR's parent): ```console $ python probe.py # POST /v1/responses, tools=[{"type":"custom","name":"exec"}], tool_choice=required 200 ['custom_tool_call'] ``` Langfuse observation `dc21eba5e810824f`: ```json {"output": null, "usageDetails": {"input": 148, "output": 15, "total": 163}} ``` **After** — proxy at `77c9ed0` (this PR): ```console $ python probe.py # identical request 200 ['custom_tool_call'] ``` Langfuse observation `1727d450336f4f56`: ```json {"output": [{"id": "U12e7ZEbFvdvGAeB3Wad7...", "name": "exec", "call_id": "call_...", "type": "custom_tool_call", "input": "console.log(6*7)\n"}]} ``` Plain-text and `function_call` turns were unaffected in both runs (they already worked). Unit test, red before the one-line branch and green after, at `77c9ed0`: ```console $ pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_langfuse_otel.py -k responses_api # without the fix: 1 failed, 5 passed # with the fix: 6 passed ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only `/v1/responses` emits `custom_tool_call`; the other two endpoints are unaffected ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(transcription): stop a zero output rate from zeroing transcription cost
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 43 of 55 per-second transcription models bill $0 - A zero output rate silently suppresses the real input rate - Every deepgram, assemblyai, elevenlabs and groq entry is affected How it solves it: - Take the output branch only when that rate is billable - A zero output rate now falls through to the input rate - No pricing data edits and no existing test rewrites ## User Flow Before: a developer transcribing audio through the proxy is billed nothing, so spend tracking and budgets never see the usage 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `"model": "deepgram/nova-3"` and a 60 second audio file 2. The transcript comes back correctly, so nothing looks wrong 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request is listed at $0.00 spend 4. They call GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs and the entry reads `"spend": 0.0` 5. Their key budget never decrements, so transcription traffic is effectively free and unbounded After: the same request records real spend, so logs and budgets reflect the audio actually transcribed 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `"model": "deepgram/nova-3"` and the same 60 second file 2. The transcript comes back identically 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now lists the request at $0.0043 4. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs returns `"spend": 0.0043` for that entry 5. The key budget decrements, so transcription traffic counts against limits like every other route ## Relevant issues Fixes #19154 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? signal.title: [Bug]: Anthropic /v1/messages: role:"system" messages inside messages[] are silently dropped
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a client sends an Anthropic `/v1/messages` request whose `messages[]` array contains an entry with `role: "system"`, that entry never reaches the backend model. The top-level `system` field is delivered correctly; the in-array one is discarded with no warning and no error. **What I expected:** the in-array system content reaches the model (translated into an OpenAI system message), or failing that, an explicit error. Silent omission is the harmful case, because the request succeeds with HTTP 200 and the response looks completely normal. **Why this shape matters.** Anthropic supports mid-conversation system messages, and Claude Code uses that channel to deliver its skill listing — the catalogue of available Agent Skills that a model needs in order to decide whether to invoke one. Pointing Claude Code at a LiteLLM proxy backed by an OpenAI-compatible model therefore strips the catalogue, and the model behaves as though no skills exist. We lost a 192-cell benchmark run to this. Every cell recorded zero skill invocation, which read as a model-capability finding until we captured request payloads on both sides of the proxy and saw the message count drop from 2 to 1. Anyone benchmarking agent-skill discovery across models through this bridge will silently measure the bridge instead of the model. **Related, but not duplicates:** - #23841 (open) reports five bugs in this same area — `input_text` content blocks being dropped, plus several env-var routing failures. It does not cover `role: "system"` entries inside `messages[]`. - #17904 ("Cannot use claude-code + LiteLLM with openai models") describes symptoms that may share this root cause, but does not identify it. **Workaround** for anyone hitting this now: a small shim in front of the proxy that hoists `role: "system"` messages into the top-level `system` field before the request reaches LiteLLM. Ours is ~150 lines and restored skill invocation from 0/192 cells to the expected rates. ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix** — the model never learns which skills exist, so it never invokes one, and nothing tells me why. 1. I install an Agent Skill into my project so Claude Code can use it, then point Claude Code at my gateway with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4002` and pick an OpenAI-compatible model. 2. I ask it to do the task the skill exists for: "Write the release notes for version 0.2.0." 3. Claude Code sends `POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages`. Its request carries two messages: one with role `"system"` listing the skills available to me, and one with role `"user"` holding my request. 4. I get back HTTP 200 and a perfectly normal answer — the model writes release notes in its own default style. 5. The skill is never invoked. There is no warning, no error, and no hint in the response that anything was missing. From my seat it is indistinguishable from the model deciding the skill was not relevant. 6. I can isolate the invisible part with two requests. I send `POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages` with a codeword inside a role `"system"` message in `messages[]`, asking the model to repeat it — it replies `NONE`. I send the identical request with that codeword in the top-level `"system"` field instead — it replies `PINEAPPLE-7731`. Same gateway, same model, same question, HTTP 200 both times. **After a (hypothetical) fix** — the model receives the listing and invokes the skill. 1. Identical. 2. Identical. 3. Identical. 4. I get back HTTP 200, and the release notes follow the format the skill defines rather than the model's default style. 5. The skill is invoked, because the model actually received the listing describing it. 6. Both requests in step 6 now reply `PINEAPPLE-7731` — whether the codeword arrives inside a role `"system"` message in `messages[]` or in the top-level `"system"` field. ### Proof the bug occurs Live proxy I ran myself, real provider calls, no mocks. **Version** ``` LiteLLM: Current Version = 1.91.4 ``` **config.yaml** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: qwen3.6-35b litellm_params: model: openai/qwen3.6-35b api_base: https://freeinference.org/v1 api_key: os.environ/FREEINFERENCE_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-repro-local ``` **Env vars the proxy ran with** ``` FREEINFERENCE_API_KEY=<redacted> ``` **Started with** ```bash litellm --config config.yaml --port 4002 --host 127.0.0.1 ``` --- ### TEST A — codeword inside `messages[]` as `role: "system"` (the bug) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages \ -H "x-api-key: sk-repro-local" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "messages":[ {"role":"system","content":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731."}, {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `content`: ```json [ { "type": "text", "text": "NONE" } ] ``` The model never received the codeword. --- ### TEST B — identical codeword in the top-level `system` field (control) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages \ -H "x-api-key: sk-repro-local" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "system":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731.", "messages":[ {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `content`: ```json [ { "type": "text", "text": "PINEAPPLE-7731" } ] ``` Same gateway, same model, same question — the only difference is where the system content was placed. --- ### TEST C — `/v1/chat/completions` with the same `role: "system"` message (endpoint NOT affected) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-local" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "messages":[ {"role":"system","content":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731."}, {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `choices[0].message.content`: ``` PINEAPPLE-7731 ``` So the same message shape is honoured on `/v1/chat/completions` and dropped on `/v1/messages`. `/v1/responses` was not tested. signal.title: fix: report real token usage on guardrail-blocked /v1/responses replies
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - POST /v1/responses replies blocked by a post-call guardrail always reported `input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0, total_tokens: 0`, even though the upstream LLM call completed and consumed real tokens - POST /v1/chat/completions already reported real token counts on guardrail blocks; /v1/responses did not How it solves it: - Added `_blocked_responses_api_usage(original_response)` helper in the responses endpoint, mirroring `_blocked_response_usage` in proxy_server.py - The `ModifyResponseException` handler now calls this helper instead of constructing a hardcoded zero `ResponseAPIUsage`, so post-call blocks carry the real counts from `e.original_response` - Pre-call blocks still report zeros because no upstream call was made ## User Flow Before: a developer whose app tracks per-request token spend from response bodies gets zeros for every guardrail-blocked Responses API call 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "..."}` and the reply trips a post-call guardrail 2. They receive a 200 whose `usage` reads `"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0` 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at $0 spend despite a real upstream call After: the same blocked call reports the real token counts 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses and the reply trips the same post-call guardrail 2. They receive a 200 whose `usage` now carries the real counts, e.g. `"input_tokens": 14, "output_tokens": 20, "total_tokens": 34` 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at the correct non-zero spend ## Relevant issues Fixes #36880 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The fix is a two-line change in `litellm/proxy/response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py`. To verify, run the proxy with a post-call guardrail and send a request that trips it via POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses; the response body's `usage` object will carry the real token counts from the upstream call instead of zeros. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix

signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - SCX.ai is not a supported provider, so callers have to route through `openai/` with a custom `api_base` - SCX.ai takes `max_tokens` rather than `max_completion_tokens`, and caps `temperature` How it solves it: - Registers `scx-ai` in `litellm/llms/openai_like/providers.json` with the parameter mapping and the ceiling as a constraint, so no Python module is needed - Adds GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.8 Max to the cost map, and registers the provider in the endpoint matrix and the dashboard ## Relevant issues Docs live in the other repo, so the provider page goes up separately in [BerriAI/litellm-docs#808](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/808). That one is a prerequisite here: `documentation` and `code-quality` both run `tests/documentation_tests/test_env_keys.py`, which checks out `BerriAI/litellm-docs` and fails while `SCX_API_KEY` is read under `./litellm` but mentioned nowhere in the docs. If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All captured at `1e24f93d3` against the real SCX.ai API, with the proxy started as `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config scx_config.yaml --port 4000` on a config with both models pointed at `os.environ/SCX_API_KEY` Chat completions, with the cost header showing the new rates being applied ```bash $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS -D /tmp/h_$m.txt http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Reply with exactly: hello from SCX\"}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", content: .choices[0].message.content}" grep -i "^x-litellm-response-cost:" /tmp/h_$m.txt done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","content":"hello from SCX"} x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0002285815 {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","content":"hello from SCX"} x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0004901237 ``` Tool calling and `json_schema` structured output on both ```bash $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is the weather in Sydney? Use the tool.\"}],\"tools\":[{\"type\":\"function\",\"function\":{\"name\":\"get_weather\",\"description\":\"Get the weather for a city\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"city\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"city\"]}}}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", tool: .choices[0].message.tool_calls[0].function}" done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","tool":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Sydney\"}","name":"get_weather"}} {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","tool":{"arguments":"{\"city\": \"Sydney\"}","name":"get_weather"}} $ for m in scx-glm-5.2 scx-qwen3.8-max; do curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"City is Sydney\"}],\"response_format\":{\"type\":\"json_schema\",\"json_schema\":{\"name\":\"c\",\"schema\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"city\":{\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"city\"],\"additionalProperties\":false}}},\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c "{m:\"$m\", content: .choices[0].message.content}" done {"m":"scx-glm-5.2","content":"{\n \"city\": \"Sydney\"\n}"} {"m":"scx-qwen3.8-max","content":"{\"city\":\"Sydney\"}"} ``` Image input on Qwen3.8 Max, which is the one of the two that declares `supports_vision`, sending a 64x64 solid red PNG as a data URI ```bash $ IMG=$(base64 -i red64.png) $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"scx-qwen3.8-max\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"What colour fills this image? One word.\"},{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":{\"url\":\"data:image/png;base64,$IMG\"}}]}],\"max_tokens\":2048}" \ | jq -c '{content: .choices[0].message.content, image_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens_details.image_tokens}' {"content":"Red","image_tokens":66} ``` The Add Model form reads `/public/providers/fields`, which now returns the provider ```bash $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/public/providers/fields | jq -c '.[] | select(.litellm_provider=="scx-ai") | {provider, provider_display_name, default_model_placeholder}' {"provider":"SCX_AI","provider_display_name":"SCX.ai","default_model_placeholder":"scx-ai/GLM-5.2"} ``` With that proxy running and `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`, Models and Endpoints then Add Model lists SCX.ai in the Provider dropdown with its logo ## Type New Feature ## Changes `providers.json` carries the base URL, `SCX_API_KEY`, the `SCX_API_BASE` override, the `max_completion_tokens` to `max_tokens` mapping and a `temperature_max` of 1.99. SCX accepts `temperature` in `[0.0, 2.0)` and returns a 400 on 2.0 exactly, and the clamp is an inclusive `min()`, so 2.0 would let through a value the endpoint rejects. The slug is registered in `LlmProviders`, the OpenAI-compatible provider and endpoint lists, the api base autodetection branch, and the endpoint support matrix Two chat models go into the cost map. GLM-5.2 has a 1M context window and is text only; Qwen3.8 Max has a 1M window and takes image input. Both cap output at 131072, which is what the endpoint's own validator enforces rather than what the catalogue advertises, and both do implicit prompt caching, so each carries a cache read rate The dashboard needs both the display metadata in `provider_info_helpers.tsx` and an entry in `provider_create_fields.json`, since the Add Model form renders from the latter Tests cover registration, config values, model resolution, api base override and autodetection, the temperature clamp, the parameter mapping, router config, cost map and backup sync, the create-fields entry and the dashboard helpers I work at SCX.ai ## QA runbook Export `SCX_API_KEY`, start the proxy on the config above and run the curl commands in the proof section ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Feature]: Support Azure AI Foundry Agents v2 (Responses API with agent_reference)
signal.text: ## Feature Request ### What is your use case? We are integrating with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service. We've deployed agents using the new Foundry Agents v2 experience, which uses the Responses API with `agent_reference` (referencing agents by name and version) rather than the deprecated Assistants API (thread/run pattern with `asst_*` IDs). The current `azure_ai/agents/{agent_id}` route in LiteLLM implements the old Assistants API pattern, which: 1. Requires agent IDs beginning with `asst_` (but the new Foundry experience does not surface these IDs) 2. Uses the thread → message → run → poll flow (but the new Foundry Agents v2 uses `openai_client.responses.create()` with an `agent_reference` in `extra_body`) Microsoft has [deprecated the Assistants API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry-classic/openai/how-to/assistant) with retirement set for **August 26, 2026**. ### The new API pattern From the Azure AI Foundry getting-started code: ```python from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential project_client = AIProjectClient( endpoint="https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>", credential=DefaultAzureCredential(), ) openai_client = project_client.get_openai_client() response = openai_client.responses.create( input=[{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me what you can help with."}], extra_body={ "agent_reference": { "name": "my-agent-name", "version": "1", "type": "agent_reference", } }, ) ``` Key differences from the current `azure_ai/agents` implementation: - **Endpoint**: Project-level (`https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>`) - **API**: Responses API (`/openai/responses`), not Assistants/Threads API - **Agent identification**: By `name` + `version` via `agent_reference` in extra_body, not by `asst_*` ID - **Auth**: Azure AD (Entra ID) bearer token — same as current implementation ### Proposed model format ``` azure_ai/agents/<agent_name>:<version> ``` For example: `azure_ai/agents/my-agent-name:1` ### Reference docs - [Agent identity concepts in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity) - [Authentication and authorization in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry) - [Assistants API deprecation notice](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry-classic/openai/how-to/assistant) ### Are you a LiteLLM Enterprise customer? No

signal.title: fix(ci): unflake build_and_test pipeline
signal.text: ## Summary The `build_and_test` job on `litellm_fix_v3_stash_leak_provider-ceb3` failed on every recent workflow attempt. Investigation showed it wasn't broad flakiness — a handful of distinct issues compound under `pytest -x`, and a CI rerun bug turns every auto-retry into a guaranteed failure. ### 1. CircleCI rerun step was a guaranteed failure ```yaml --command="awk '/\.py/ {print; next} {sub(/\.[A-Z][^.]*$/, ""); gsub(/\./, "/"); print $0 ".py"}' | xargs ... pytest" ``` The awk assumed **one classname per stdin line**. CircleCI's rerun-failed mechanism pipes them **space-separated on a single line**: ``` tests.test_spend_logs tests.test_team_members ``` `gsub(/\./, "/")` ran once over the whole line and `.py` was appended only at the end, producing `tests/test_spend_logs tests/test_team_members.py`. xargs split that — neither path resolved, pytest collected `0 items`, exit non-zero. Every retry was DOA regardless of underlying tests. Fix: prepend `tr -s '[:space:]' '\n'` so each classname is processed independently. Happy-path glob output (already newline-separated) is unaffected. Applied to all 34 occurrences. ### 2. `test_chat_completion_anthropic_structured_output` (Bedrock LLM nondeterminism) Calls real `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0` and runs the response through the OpenAI client's strict pydantic parse. Sonnet occasionally emits invalid JSON (observed: `"participants": ["Kingdom of Sardinia", <UNKNOWN>]`), which raises `pydantic_core.ValidationError`. Added `temperature=0` and `@pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=3)`. ### 3. `test_check_num_callbacks_on_lowest_latency` tolerance too tight Asserted `abs(num_callbacks_diff) <= 4`; observed 10 under CI load (4 xdist workers hammering shared proxy). Switching routing strategy transiently re-registers internal callbacks; the leak signal we care about is monotonic growth, not count wobble. Bumped tolerance to 20. ## Test plan - [ ] Re-run the failed pipeline on this PR and confirm `build_and_test` passes - [ ] Confirm rerun-failed CI step actually runs the failed tests instead of collecting 0 items - [ ] Confirm `test_chat_completion_anthropic_structured_output` either parses or hits the flaky reruns transparently - [ ] Confirm `test_check_num_callbacks_on_lowest_latency` stays green across multiple runs --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01NrVzKeCKNi4pzDpe24sESW)_ <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Changes are limited to CI test execution plumbing and test assertions/markers; main risk is masking real regressions by widening tolerances and adding reruns. > > **Overview** > Fixes CircleCI test reruns across jobs by normalizing whitespace before the `awk` classname→path transform, preventing rerun-failed from generating invalid pytest targets and collecting 0 tests. > > Reduces CI flakiness in a couple of integration tests: widens callback-count delta tolerance during latency-routing switches (`tests/test_callbacks_on_proxy.py`) and makes the Bedrock Claude structured-output test more deterministic via `temperature=0` plus `pytest` reruns (`tests/test_openai_endpoints.py`). > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 3fd6791b7ac92e9e586671f262392297a104faef. signal.title: fix(exceptions): don't map upstream 400 to RateLimitError on substring match
signal.text: ## Problem OpenAI's `Unknown parameter: ''` / `Unrecognized request arguments supplied: , ` 400s, which echo the rejected field name back in the message, get misclassified as 429 `RateLimitError` whenever the field name contains `rate_limit` (or any `rate[\s_\-]*limit` substring) — e.g. `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors`. Concretely: while reproducing the v3 limiter leak (PR #27001 → PR #27913), OpenAI returned ``` { "error": { "message": "Unknown parameter: '_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors'.", "code": "400" } } ``` and LiteLLM surfaced it to the client as ``` HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests { "error": { "message": "litellm.RateLimitError: OpenAIException - Unknown parameter: '_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors'.", "type": "throttling_error", "code": "429" } } ``` That breaks two contracts: 1. **Retry semantics.** Clients see `429 throttling_error` and assume "back off and retry" — but the upstream rejected the body, retrying won't help. Loops forever on a malformed request. 2. **Debuggability.** It's the misclassification that hid the v3 leak: the 429 made it look like rate-limiting working as intended. The bug only surfaced after end-to-end provider testing. ## Root cause In `litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py`: **Cause 1 — unanchored regex:** `ExceptionCheckers.is_error_str_rate_limit` uses `re.search(r"rate[\s_\-]*limit", _error_str_lower)`. No word boundary, so it matches `rate_limit` as a substring of any identifier. Real OpenAI 400 body fields named with `rate_limit` (or LiteLLM-internal field names like `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors` leaked into the body) all trip the heuristic. **Cause 2 — heuristic runs before status code:** Inside the OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible / Mistral branch of `exception_type`, `is_error_str_rate_limit` is called unconditionally — *before* the status-code branch that handles 400 → `BadRequestError`. So an explicit upstream 400 never gets a chance to map correctly when the string matches. Anthropic's branch was already correct: it routes 400/413 to `BadRequestError` via status code, no string heuristic up front. (Companion observation in PR #16482, which tightened `\b429\b` against `429` substrings — same shape of bug, different token.) ## Fix **Anchor the regex** with a leading word boundary: `\brate[\s_\-]*limit`. Embedded identifiers like `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors` no longer match (the preceding `_` is a word char so `\b` fails). Standalone phrases all still match: `Rate limit exceeded`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `rate-limit-exceeded`, `You hit a rate limit`. **Status-code gate at the mapping site:** when `getattr(original_exception, "status_code", None) == 400`, skip the string heuristic entirely. A 400 is unambiguous per RFC 9110 — the upstream rejected the body, not the rate. Don't second-guess it. Both fixes are independent and complementary: the regex fix protects unknown-status-code paths (some upstream errors don't carry `status_code`), and the gate protects against any future heuristic that could mistake a 400 message for a 429. ## Tests `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py`: - `test_is_error_str_rate_limit_ignores_field_name_substring` — three forms of the OpenAI 400 wire message all return False. - `test_is_error_str_rate_limit_still_matches_standalone_token` — proves the tightening didn't regress legitimate detections. - `TestExceptionTypeStatusCodeGate` — end-to-end mapper tests. Build a real `openai.BadRequestError` with status 400 and the wire messages we saw, run `exception_type`, assert the result is `litellm.BadRequestError` (not `RateLimitError`). - `test_openai_429_still_maps_to_rate_limit` — confirms the genuine 429 path is untouched. ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py -q 43 passed in 0.21s ``` ## Related Companion to #27913 (which fixes the underlying v3 limiter leak that this misclassification was hiding). [Slack Thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/D0AUCPA0MLN/p1778738597799989?thread_ts=1778738597.799989&cid=D0AUCPA0MLN)

signal.title: fix(router): scan all deployments for weight/rpm/tpm in simple-shuffle
signal.text: ## Problem `simple_shuffle` only consults `healthy_deployments[0]` when deciding whether to do a weighted random pick. A config like: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini # ^ no weight/rpm/tpm declared - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini rpm: 1000 - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini rpm: 500 ``` silently falls back to **uniform random across all three** because the first entry has no `rpm`. Users perceive this as "deployment-level `rpm:` (or `tpm:` / `weight:`) is silently ignored under `simple-shuffle`" — the actual behavior is ordering-sensitive: if the first deployment happens to declare the weight field, everything works; if not, the rest are silently disregarded. This was reported as part of a broader audit of v3 rate limit semantics (sibling to #27913, #27914, #27915). It is the only one of those audit findings that's a pre-existing router bug rather than a v3-limiter or exception-mapper issue. ## Fix Extract `_pick_weight_field(healthy_deployments)` which scans **every** deployment for the precedence-ordered weight fields (`weight` > `rpm` > `tpm`) and returns the first one declared by any of them. Deployments that don't declare the chosen field continue to get weight `0` (preserves the existing semantics for in-list-but-unweighted entries). Also: defensive divide-by-zero guard when `total_weight == 0` (every deployment declared the field as 0 — pathological config). Falls through to uniform random instead of crashing. Docstring updated to be explicit that `rpm` and `tpm` here are **static relative weights**, not cap-enforced limits, and to point users at `router_settings.enable_pre_call_checks` (router-level RPM cap filter, gated on `messages is not None`) or the proxy's key-level v3 TPM/RPM limiter for actual cap enforcement under simple-shuffle. ## Scope notes This PR does **not** change the documented semantics of `rpm`/`tpm` under simple-shuffle (still relative weights). Adding actual cap enforcement to simple-shuffle would change load-balancing behavior for every user on that strategy and is out of scope here — leaving it for a follow-up. ## Tests `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_simple_shuffle.py` — 10 new unit tests: `TestPickWeightField`: - `test_returns_none_when_no_deployment_declares_anything` - `test_returns_weight_when_declared_on_first` - `test_returns_weight_when_declared_only_on_later_deployments` — **the headline regression test** - `test_precedence_weight_over_rpm_over_tpm` — covers two precedence pairs - `test_handles_missing_litellm_params` — defensive `TestSimpleShuffle` (statistical assertions over 6,000 picks): - `test_uniform_random_when_no_weights` - `test_rpm_on_later_deployment_is_respected` — end-to-end regression for silent-fallthrough - `test_zero_total_weight_falls_through_to_uniform_random` — divide-by-zero defense - `test_single_deployment_always_picked` - `test_weight_field_wins_over_rpm` — precedence under simple_shuffle (not just helper) ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_simple_shuffle.py -q 10 passed in 0.17s ``` ## Related Companion PRs from the same audit: - #27913 — fix(rate-limit): stop v3 limiter from leaking internal stash to provider body - #27914 — fix(rate-limit): resolve router model_name aliases to real provider (stacked on #27687) - #27915 — fix(exceptions): don't map upstream 400 to RateLimitError on substring match [Slack Thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/D0AUCPA0MLN/p1778738597799989?thread_ts=1778738597.799989&cid=D0AUCPA0MLN)
